times during the operative and post-operative period.
   (e)   Pathologic examination of all tissue removed from the uterus shall be
performed routinely.
   (f)   Facilities shall be maintained or proper procedures provided for the
incineration of human remains.
   (g)   Patients shall receive the following post-operative care:
      (1)   Patients whose pregnancy was terminated on an ambulatory basis
shall be observed in the abortion service for a reasonable number of hours, not
less than three, to ensure that no immediate post-operative complications are
present. Thereafter, such patients may be discharged if their course has been
uneventful.
      (2)   Patients in whom any adverse condition exists or in whom a
complication is known or suspected to have occurred during or after the
performance of the abortion shall remain in the abortion service for further
observation or be transported to the hospital.
   (h)   Written instructions shall be issued to all patients in accordance
with the rules of the physician in charge of the abortion service and shall
include the following:
      (1)   Symptoms of complications to be looked for;
      (2)   Activities to be avoided;
      (3)   The specific telephone number to be used by the patient should any
complication occur or question arise; and
      (4)   The date for a follow-up or return visit after the performance of
the abortion, which shall be scheduled within two to six weeks, as indicated by
the condition of the patient.
(Ord. 67-77. Passed 3-21-77.)
719.15   ABORTION OF VIABLE FETUS.
   No person shall perform or participate in the performance or induction of an
abortion of a viable fetus (twelve weeks or thereafter) unless such abortion is
performed by a physician in a hospital, and unless two physicians, one of whom
may be the physician performing the abortion, certify in writing that the
abortion is necessary to preserve the life or health of the mother.
(Ord. 67-77. Passed 3-21-77.)
719.155   FAILURE TO PERFORM VIABILITY TESTING.
   (a)   Except as provided in subsection (c) hereof, no physician shall
perform or induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion upon a pregnant
woman after the beginning of her twenty-second week of pregnancy unless, prior
to the performance or inducement of the abortion or the attempt to perform or
induce the abortion, the physician determines, in good faith and in the
exercise of reasonable medical judgment, that the unborn human is not viable,
and the physician makes that determination after performing a medical
examination of the pregnant woman and after performing or causing the
performing of gestational age, weight, lung maturity or other tests of the
unborn human that a reasonable physician making a determination as to whether
an unborn human is or is not viable would perform or cause to be performed.
   (b)   Except as provided in subsection (c) hereof, no physician shall
perform or induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion upon a pregnant
woman after the beginning of her twenty-second week of pregnancy without first
entering the determination described in subsection (a) hereof and the
associated findings of the medical examination and tests described in that
subsection in the medical record of the pregnant woman.
   (c)   Subsections (a) and (b) hereof do not prohibit a physician from
performing or inducing or attempting to perform or induce an abortion upon a
pregnant woman after the beginning of her twenty- second week of pregnancy
without making the determination described in subsection (a) hereof or without
making the entry described in subsection (b) hereof if a medical emergency
exists.
(ORC 2919.18; Ord. 66-97. Passed 3-18-97.)
719.16   LIABILITY INSURANCE.
   An abortion service, prior to the issuance of a license to it, shall furnish
a liability policy or copy thereof to the City, with minimum limits of one
million dollars/three million dollars ($1,000,000/$3,000,000) protecting
patients of such abortion service against any and all acts of misfeasance or
malfeasance by such abortion service or its employees.
(Ord. 67-77. Passed 3-21-77.)
719.17   LICENSURE; APPEAL.
   (a)   No person shall operate or maintain an abortion service without first
obtaining a license therefor issued by the County Board of Health acting for
the City. The Board may revoke such license if it finds, after a hearing, that
the abortion service has failed to comply with this chapter and that such
failure of compliance has materially affected or will materially affect the
health of a patient. Any denial, suspension, or revocation of a license under
this chapter may be appealed pursuant to Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
   (b)   The annual fee for the license to operate an abortion service in the
City shall be five hundred dollars ($500.00).
(Ord. 67-77. Passed 3-21-77; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
719.18   SEPARABILITY.
   Should any part of this chapter be declared unconstitutional for any reason,
the remainder of this chapter shall not be affected thereby and shall remain in
full force and effect.
(Ord. 67-77. Passed 3-21-77.)
719.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter shall be fined not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or, if an
individual, imprisoned not more than six months, or both, for each offense. A
separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on which a
violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 67-77. Passed 3-21-77.)
CHAPTER 721
Coin-Operated Machines
721.01   Definitions.
721.02   Permit required.
721.03   Effective period; prorating fees.
721.04   Periodic check.
721.05   Exceptions. (Repealed)
721.06   Transfer of permits.
721.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   License fees - see ADM.
185.04(c)
   Tampering- see GEN. OFF.
642.13
   Use of slugs - see GEN. OFF.
642.16
   Newspaper dispensing devices - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 752
721.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Amusement machine" means any device which is operated by electronic
and/or mechanical means, with or without moving parts, which satisfies all of
the following criteria:
      (1)   The device becomes operational upon deposit of a coin or insertion
of a credit card.
      (2)   The device is located in a business establishment.
      (3)   The person who owns the business establishment where the device is
located intends that the device will be used by the operator to play a game
(whether or not the game involves competition between two or more players and
whether or not a winner results in playing the game) and/or to try his skill in
the use of the device and/or to otherwise derive amusement, enjoyment or
relaxation from its operation. For purposes of this paragraph, there shall be a
rebuttable presumption that devices known as video games, pinball machines and
bowling machines satisfy this third criterion. "Amusement machine" does not
mean or include gumball machines, cigarette machines, postage stamp machines
and/or other devices which dispense personal property upon deposit of one or
more coins or currency.
   (b)   "Service dispensing machine" means any mechanical device which, upon
deposit of a coin, performs a service of any nature such as washing of
clothing, drying of clothing, cleaning, dyeing or pressing of clothing or shoe
shine service.
   (c)   "Licensing authority" means the Director of Public Safety and/or his
designated subordinates, such as the Building Commissioner and/or his clerks.
   (d)   "Coin" means and includes in addition to its usual meaning of a piece
of metal stamped by or on behalf of the Federal Government for use as money,
any token, slug, chip or other item which can be deposited into a device to
render it operational and which is purchased, leased, rented or exchanged for
on the premises of the establishment where the device is located. In such case,
the token, slug, chip or other item, as described, shall be valued at the
monetary rate of exchange for which it is purchased, leased, rented or
exchanged.
   (e)   "Credit card", as used in this section, includes, but is not limited
to, a credit card, charge card, debit card, or other card, code, device, or
other means of access to a customer's account for the purpose of obtaining
money, property, labor or services on credit, or for initiating an electronic
fund transfer at a point-of-sale terminal, an automated teller machine, or a
cash dispensing machine.
(Ord. 118-83. Passed 7-5-83; Ord. 37-05. Passed 2-6-06.)
721.02   PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (a)   The owner of any business establishment that is otherwise properly and
lawfully authorized to operate within the City, who desires to install and
maintain upon, at or near such business premises any amusement machine or
service dispensing machine, whether as a main or incidental use of the business
premises, must secure a permit before such machine is installed for operation
and use by the general public. The owner of the business establishment shall
secure the necessary application forms from the licensing authority and shall
state thereon the total number of machines to be installed, operated or
maintained in, at or near such establishment or its premises and shall be
charged with the duty of reporting any newly installed machines or any
substitutions made during the licensing period. The fee for such a permit is as
set forth in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule).
   (b)   The licensing authority shall be responsible for the preparation of
all forms and/or applications and an insignia or decal-type stamp. Upon
investigation by the licensing authority and upon sufficient evidence as
presented by the applicant on the application blank furnished by such licensing
authority, the licensing authority shall issue a general permit covering one or
more machines and shall, further, issue a sufficient number of insignias or
decal-type stamps to cover the number of mechanical devices contained in the
application blank. Such insignias or decal-type stamps shall be placed upon
such machine by the applicant, and it shall be the duty of the applicant to
insure that such insignias or decal-type stamps remain affixed thereto during
the licensing period.
   (c)   Notwithstanding subsection (a) hereof, the owner of any business
establishment shall not be required to apply for or obtain a permit with
respect to any machine for which he has applied for or obtained a permit
pursuant to some other chapter of Part Seven of these Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 118-83. Passed 7-5-83.)
721.03   EFFECTIVE PERIOD; PRORATING FEES.
   (a)   For the purposes of this chapter, all permits shall terminate on
December 31 of each calendar year and, except as provided in subsection (b)
hereof, there shall be no prorating of any fee required by
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule).
   (b)   Whenever a fee is payable for a coin-operated amusement machine permit
newly acquired during the course of a calendar year, the fee shall be prorated
as follows:
 
Date of Permit:
January through March    100% of the current annual fee
April through June       75% of the current annual fee
July through September   50%of the current annual fee
October through December 25% of the current annual fee
 
   This subsection notwithstanding the fee shall be a minimum of ten dollars
($10.00) for a partial calendar year.
(Ord. 118-83. Passed 7-5-83.)
721.04   PERIODIC CHECK.
   The licensing authority is hereby authorized to make periodic checks of all
permit premises during the business hours of such establishments for the
purpose of inspection of such machines to protect the health, safety and
welfare of the general public using such machines.
(Ord. 118-83. Passed 7-5-83.)
721.05   EXCEPTIONS. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section 721.05 was repealed by Ordinance 118-83, passed July
5, 1983.)
721.06   TRANSFER OF PERMITS.
   With respect to coin-operated amusement machines only, a permit granted for
one such machine is transferable, during the same calendar year, from one
machine to another, if the replacement machine is approximately the same size
and voltage as the original and if it is in the same location. However, to
effect a non-fee transfer, a written receipt of transfer shall be maintained at
the permit premises and shall be available for public inspection. A written
notice, on a form to be provided by the City, shall also be filed with the City
within fifteen days for each such transfer.
   The licensing authority may adjust or revise procedures and forms to
effectuate this section.
(Ord. 118-83. Passed 7-5-83.)
721.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00). Each day's violation shall constitute
a separate offense.
(Ord. 118-83. Passed 7-5-83.)
CHAPTER 723
Dance Halls, Public
723.01   Definitions.
723.02   License required for hall or academy; fee.
723.03   Posting of license.
723.04   Investigation.
723.05   Suspension of license; appeal.
723.06   Permit required for public dances. (Repealed)
723.07   Fee; effective period.
723.08   Sanitation.
723.09   Prohibitions.
723.10   Hours.
723.11   Minors.
723.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Authority of a municipality to regulate dancing academies or schools - see
Ohio R.C. 715.61
   Admissions tax - see ADM.
Ch. 181 
   License fee - see ADM.

   Smoking in public places - see GEN. OFF.
668.02
   Adult entertainment businesses - see BUS. REG.

   Amusement places with music - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 703 
723.01   DEFINITIONS.
   The terms used in this chapter shall have the meaning herein defined unless
another meaning is clearly apparent in the language or context.
   (a)   "Public dance" or "public hall" means any dance or ball to which
admission can be had by payment of a fee or by the purchase, possession or
presentation of a ticket or token obtained for money or other valuable
consideration, or in which a charge is made for caring for clothing or other
property, or any other dance to which the public generally may gain admission
with or without the payment of a fee, including restaurant dancing or any other
dance or party where dancing is held before or after a program of some other
nature and dancing to which any of the public generally may gain admission with
or without the payment of a fee.
   (b)   "Public dance hall" means any auditorium hall, academy, room, place,
restaurant or night club in which a public dance or public ball is held or any
room, place, hall or academy in which classes in dancing are held or
instruction in dancing is given for a fee.
   (c)   "Known," as used in Section
723.09, means known to the manager, owner or lessee of a public dance hall, or
to the persons conducting a public dance or to the Division of Police.
   (d)   "Private dancing" means and includes any dance given at any home or by
any permanently organized club, society or corporation, where the dancing is
restricted to members of the society, club or corporation admitted by
invitation only.
   (e)   "Home" means and includes only such buildings as are used exclusively
for private dwelling purposes.
   (f)   "Dancing" does not mean or include exhibitions or performances in
which the persons paying for admission do not participate.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
723.02   LICENSE REQUIRED FOR HALL OR ACADEMY; FEE.
   No person shall hold any public dance or give instruction in dancing for
hire in any hall or academy within the City until the hall or academy in which
the same may be held is first duly licensed for that purpose, as hereinafter
provided. The owner of any such hall or academy shall apply to the Mayor for a
license for the hall or academy, which application shall be on a form which
shall be furnished by the Mayor and, before any license is granted, the
application shall be approved by the Mayor. Upon approval of the license by the
Mayor, the applicant shall pay an annual license fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule).
   Any license issued hereunder shall expire on December 31 following the
issuance thereof. Any such license may be revoked upon order of the Mayor.
(Ord. 26-73. Passed 3-5-73.)
723.03   POSTING OF LICENSE.
   Upon approval of the application, the Mayor shall issue a license as
hereinbefore provided, and the owner, lessee, person, firm or corporation in
charge of the hall or academy shall post the license in a conspicuous place in
the hall.
(Ord. 26-73. Passed 3-5-73.)
723.04   INVESTIGATION.
   No license for a public dance hall or academy shall be issued until the
Mayor or some duly authorized City official appointed by the Mayor has
investigated the hall or academy and determined that the hall or academy
complies with and conforms to all ordinances and health and fire regulations of
the City, that the hall or academy is properly ventilated and supplied with
adequate toilet conveniences and that it is a safe, sanitary and proper place
for the purpose for which it is to be used.
(Ord. 26-73. Passed 3-5-73.)
723.05   SUSPENSION OF LICENSE; APPEAL.
   The license of any public dance hall may be suspended by the Mayor for
disorderly or immoral conduct therein or for violation of any of the provisions
set forth herein or any other ordinance, law or regulation affecting public
dance halls or public dances. The public dance hall may be entered at any time
by the Mayor, by any member of the Division of Police or by any other person
duly authorized by the Mayor for that purpose. Any police officer of the City
may cause any public dance to be discontinued and the hall to be vacated,
during the progress of a public dance, for any reason for which a license may
be forfeited or revoked and, in case any license granted under the provisions
of this chapter is forfeited or revoked, as herein provided, at least six
months shall elapse before another license or permit shall be issued for
dancing in the same hall or academy.
   Any denial, suspension, or revocation of a license under this chapter may be
appealed pursuant to Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
(Ord. 26-73. Passed 3-5-73; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
723.06   PERMIT REQUIRED FOR PUBLIC DANCES. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: Section 723.06 was repealed by Ordinance No. 119-22, passed
August 22, 2022.)
723.07   FEE; EFFECTIVE PERIOD.
   A fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) shall be paid
for each and every dance held in a public dance hall, whether public or
private, and the permit may he issued by the Mayor for a period not to exceed
thirty days.
(Ord. 26-73. Passed 3-5-73.)
723.08   SANITATION.
   All public dance halls shall be kept at all times in a clean, healthful and
sanitary condition and all stairways and other passages shall be kept clear and
well lighted. After a public dance hall license has been granted, it shall be
the duty of the Mayor to see that sufficient toilet conveniences, sanitary
drinking facilities and adequate ventilating facilities are maintained in the
dance hall. It shall be the duty of the Division of Fire to see that all fire
hazards are immediately removed from public dance halls. The Mayor may require
the owner or manager of any public dance hall to employ a matron who shall be
in attendance at all dances to supervise the conduct and deportment of patrons.
(Ord. 26-73. Passed 3-5-73.)
723.09   PROHIBITIONS.
   No person conducting a public dance or public dance hall or any agent or
employee of such person shall:
    (a)   Permit any known prostitute, male or female procurer or vagrant to be
present at any public dance of public dance hall;
   (b)   Permit on the public dance hall premises any person having in his
possession, being under the influence of, selling or offering for sale, giving
away or drinking, any intoxicating liquors or drugs;
   (c)   Permit idlers, loiterers or other hangers-on to be on or about the
dance hall premises;
   (d)   Permit smoking, except in rooms reserved for smoking or in a
restaurant or dining room when seated at a table;
   (e)   Permit gambling in any form on the premises;
   (f)   Permit men to enter the ladies' room or parlor;
    (g)   Permit persons to indulge in dancing that is vulgar, suggestive or
immoral;
    (h)   Permit moonlight dances unless there is sufficient light in the dance
hall so that patrons can be easily seen;
    (i)   Permit or employ any instructor under the age of twenty-one years to
give instructions in dancing to persons of the opposite sex;
   (j)   Discriminate between sexes by offering free admission to either sex as
inducement to stimulate attendance;
   (k)   Permit endurance dancing contests commonly known as marathon dances;
   (l)   Permit dancing in restaurants with persons seated at different tables;
    (m)   Permit any cabaret or other similar entertainment in a restaurant
wherein any entertainers shall perform their acts by mingling with the audience
or traveling about among them.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
723.10   HOURS.
   All public dances and all public dance halls shall be closed on or before
the hour of 12:00 midnight. However, upon the application of a bona fide
responsible person, club, organization, corporation or society, and after
investigation, the Mayor may grant such person, club, organization or society a
permit to continue the dance until such time as in his opinion is reasonable.
(Ord. 180-75. Passed 11-5-75.)
723.11   MINORS.
   No person under the age of eighteen years shall be admitted to or allowed to
remain in a public dance hall after 10:00 p.m. of any day, unless accompanied
by a parent or legal guardian.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
723.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)

Ch. 759 
727.01   EXTERMINANTS DEFINED.
   "Exterminants," as used in this chapter, means and includes any substance
not a fumigant, under whatever name known, for the extermination, destruction
or control of insects, vermin, germs, rodents or other pests.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.02   EXTERMINATORS; LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall engage in the business of exterminating or be employed as an
exterminant operator in the City unless licensed to do so as hereinafter set
forth.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.03   APPLICATION FOR EXTERMINATOR'S LICENSE.
   Application for an exterminator's license shall be made to the Director of
Public Safety upon blanks furnished for that purpose which shall set forth, in
addition to other information, the following:
   (a)   Name, age and address of applicant.
   (b)   Qualifications of applicant.
   (c)   If an employee, the name and address of present employer.
   (d)   If applicant is a corporation:
      (1)   Full and accurate corporate name.
      (2)   When and where incorporated.
      (3)   Name of county where certificate has been filed and date of filing.
      (4)   Principal place of business of corporation.
      (5)   Full names and addresses of officers of corporation and their
qualifications.
   (e)   If applicant is a partnership, the names and addresses of members and
partners and their qualifications.
   (f)   If applicant conducts business under a trade name, the following
additional information:
      (1)   Complete and full trade name.
      (2)   The name of the person or persons doing business under such trade
names.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.04   INVESTIGATION; ISSUANCE OF LICENSE.
   The application shall also state the applicant's experience and
qualifications in the use of exterminants, or such other information as the
Director of Public Safety may from time to time require, whereupon such
application shall be referred to the Health Officer who shall make or cause to
be made an investigation thereof and shall report his findings to the Director,
whereupon, if such investigation discloses that the applicant is possessed of
adequate and sufficient knowledge, training, experience and fitness in the use
of exterminants intended to be used for the purposes herein defined, the
Director shall direct that the application be granted and a license be issued
to such applicant according to the provisions herein set forth.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.05   FEE.
   The fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) for such
license shall he paid upon the filing of the application. The fee shall be
refunded if the application is rejected.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.06   POISONS IN EXPOSED PLACES.
   No exterminator shall place any deadly poison or fumigant on the streets,
alleys or yards of the City without first securing written permission from the
Health Officer. Such permission shall specify the exact type of poison to be
placed in such exposed positions.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.07   EXPIRATION DATE.
   All such licenses shall expire on December 31 immediately following the date
of issue, after which they may be renewed upon payment of the fee as originally
paid.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.08   REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION.
   The Director of Public Safety, upon the recommendation of the Health
Officer, may at any time suspend or revoke any license granted under the
authority of this chapter for failure to comply with the terms and provisions
of this chapter or any laws or regulations relating to the use of exterminants.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.09   HELPER.
   No person may be employed as a helper unless under the supervision of a
licensee.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.10   SUPERVISION.
   No person shall work and no employer shall engage, allow or permit such
person to work as a helper or engage in any part of the work of exterminating
except in the presence and under the constant direction and supervision of the
holder of a license under this chapter.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.11   LABELS.
   No person shall sell or give away in the City any poisonous substance as an
exterminant or insecticide unless the container bears a label legibly and
conspicuously printed with the word "Poison" and the symbol of the skull and
crossbones in red ink followed by the word "Caution", the name of the poison,
the antidote therefor and the name and address of the manufacturer or packer.
The words "poison", "caution" and "antidote" shall be in block type of a larger
size than the other wording, as follows:
   POISON
   (Skull and Crossbones)
   CAUTION
   This exterminant or insecticide contains (insert name of poison), a deadly
poison.
   ANTIDOTE - (state briefly)
   MANUFACTURED (or PACKED) BY
   NAME
   ADDRESS
   No person shall sell or give away in the City any substance as an
exterminant or insecticide which contains wholly or in part flourine, its salts
or compounds, or any other highly toxic ingredient, unless the container bears
the following label with the caution and antidote therefor conspicuously and
legibly printed, and the words "caution" and "antidote" in block type of a
larger size than the other wording, as follows:
   CAUTION
   This exterminant or insecticide contains flourine (or name other highly
toxic ingredient), which is highly toxic and must be used with care pursuant to
the following directions:
   (state directions)
   ANTIDOTE - (state briefly)
   MANUFACTURED (or PACKED) BY
   NAME
   ADDRESS
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.12   EXTERMINANTS WITH LIVING BACTERIAL ORGANISMS.
   No person shall prepare or manufacture, sell, offer for sale, give away,
deal in, supply or use, or have in his or her possession with intent to sell,
offer for sale, give away, deal in, supply or use an exterminant or insecticide
which contains living bacterial organisms or any culture or preparation
thereof.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.13   EXCEPTIONS TO CHAPTER; ECONOMIC POISONS.
   Nothing contained in this chapter shall be deemed to apply to economic
poisons used in agricultural and industrial arts or to products used for the
control of insects, animal or other pests when sold in original, unbroken
containers, properly labeled in accordance with the Federal Insecticide Act of
1910, as the same may be amended, or in accordance with State law.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.14   FUMIGANT DEFINED.
   "Fumigant", as used herein, means and includes any substance or combination
of substances which emits Or liberates a gas, fumes or vapors, which gas, fumes
or vapors when liberated or used for the extermination, destruction or control
of insects, vermin, germs, rodents or other pests, is lethal, poisonous,
noxious or dangerous to human life.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.15   PERMIT TO FUMIGATE.
   No person shall use in any building, structure or other enclosed space in
the City, a fumigant for the extermination, destruction or control of insects,
vermin, germs, rodents or other pests, without first having obtained a permit
to do so from the Health Officer as provided for herein.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.16   PERMIT TO ENGAGE IN BUSINESS.
   No person shall engage in the business of generating or releasing in any
building, structure or enclosure, or any part thereof, in the City, any
fumigant or noxious or poisonous fumes, gases or chemicals, for the purpose of
exterminating, destroying or controlling any insects, vermin, germs, rodents or
other pests, without first having obtained a permit to do so from the Health
Officer as provided for herein.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.17   DISPLAY OF PERMIT.
   Permits provided for in Sections
727.15 and
727.16 shall be displayed on the premises to be fumigated during the period of
fumigation in compliance with the regulations of the Health Officer and the
provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.18   FUMIGATORS; LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall engage in the business of fumigation or be employed as a
fumigator without first having obtained a license to do so as herein set forth.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.19   APPLICATION FOR FUMIGATOR'S LICENSE.
   Application for a license to conduct and engage in the business of fumigator
shall be made to the Director of Public Safety upon blanks furnished for that
purpose which shall set forth, in addition to other information, the following:
   (a)   Name, age and address of applicant.
    (b)   Qualifications of applicant.
    (c)   If an employee, the name and address of present employer.
    (d)   If applicant is a corporation:
      (1)   Full and accurate corporate name.
      (2)   When and where incorporated.
      (3)   Name of county where certificate has been filed and date of filing.
      (4)   Principal place of business of corporation.
      (5)   Full names and addresses of officers of corporation and their
qualifications.
   (e)   If applicant is a partnership, the names and addresses of members and
partners and their qualifications.
   (f)   If applicant conducts business under a trade name, the following
additional information:
      (1)   Complete and full trade name.
      (2)   The name of the person or persons doing business under such trade
name.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.20   INVESTIGATION.
   The application shall also state the applicant's experience and
qualifications in the use of such poisonous gases, fumes or chemicals, and such
other information as the Director of Public Safety may from time to time
require, whereupon the application shall be referred to the Health Officer who
shall make or cause to be made an investigation thereof and shall report his
findings to the Director, whereupon, if such investigation discloses that the
applicant is possessed of adequate and sufficient knowledge and experience in
the use of the particular gases, fumes or chemicals to be used for the purpose
defined herein, the Solicitor shall direct that the application be granted and
a license be issued to such applicant according to the provisions herein set
forth.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.21   DEPOSIT OF CASH OR GOVERNMENT OBLIGATIONS.
   No fumigator's license shall be issued under the provisions of this chapter
unless and until the applicant for such license deposits with the Auditor cash
or obligations of the United States of America in the aggregate amount of five
thousand dollars ($5,000), pursuant to an agreement prepared and executed to
the satisfaction of the Solicitor, for the benefit of any person or persons who
may receive injuries, acquire illness or suffer death by reason of the use of
fumigating by such licensee, his agents or employees.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.22   BOND.
   In lieu of such deposit of cash or government obligations, the applicant may
deposit with the Auditor a bond in the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000)
for the benefit of any person or persons who may receive injuries, acquire
illness or suffer death by reason of the use of fumigants by the licensee, his
agents or employees, which bond shall be approved by the Solicitor and the
Auditor. The applicant may also deposit a policy or certificate of liability
insurance, acceptable to and approved by the Solicitor and the Auditor,
insuring and indemnifying the applicant in a sum of at least five thousand
dollars ($5,000) for the injury or death of one person, and ten thousand
dollars ($10,000) for the injury or death of two or more persons in any one
accident resulting from the use of fumigants by the applicant, his agents or
employees. The policy shall further contain a clause obligating the insurance
company issuing the same to give thirty days written notice to the Solicitor
and the Auditor before cancellation of the same. In case the policy of
insurance is not replaced, the license of the licensee shall forthwith be
cancelled at the expiration of the thirty day period.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.23   FEE.
   The fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) for each
license shall be paid upon the filing of the application. The fee shall be
refunded if the application is rejected.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.24   EXPIRATION DATE.
   All such licenses shall expire on December 31 immediately after the date of
issuance, after which they may be renewed upon payment of the fee as originally
paid.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.25   REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION.
   The Director of Public Safety, upon recommendation of the Health Officer,
may at any time suspend or revoke any license granted under the authority of
this chapter for failure to comply with the terms and provisions of this
chapter or any laws or regulations relating to the use of fumigants, noxious or
poisonous gases, fumes or chemicals.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.26   COMPLIANCE WITH FUMIGATING REGULATIONS REQUIRED.
   No fumigating shall be done in any building, structure or other enclosed
space except in accordance with the regulations hereinafter set forth.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.27   NOTICE OF FUMIGATION.
   Noxious or poisonous gases, fumes or chemicals shall not be generated or
released for the purposes herein provided in any building or structure or part
thereof in the City unless notice of such intention, in writing, has first been
given to the Director of Public Safety, which notice shall be accompanied by
the written consent and approval thereof from the Health Officer.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.28   INVESTIGATION DEPOSIT.
   At the time the written notice is given to the Director of Public Safety of
intention to generate or release such gases, fumes or chemicals in any building
or structure within the City, a deposit of ten dollars ($10.00) shall be made
to the Auditor, whereupon a permit to fumigate shall be issued to such
licensee. Out of this fee shall be paid the cost of inspecting the premises
where such fumigation is to be made and of inspecting the premises during the
process of such fumigation and the releasing of such fumes at the termination
of the fumigation. Any balance left from the deposit after paying the cost of
the inspections shall be returned to the person making the deposit.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.29   WARNING SIGNS.
   Prior to releasing the generating gases, fumes or vapors, warning signs
shall be posted on all entrances or doors to the premises in which the
fumigating is to be carried on. Such warning sign shall be as follows:
   DANGER
   (Crossbones and Skull)
   Fumigated With
   (State name of chemical or gas)
   (Crossbones and Skull)
   DEADLY POISON- HIGHLY TOXIC
   ALL PERSONS ARE WARNED TO
   KEEP AWAY
      Name of Fumigator
      Address
      Operator in Charge
   Such signs shall be printed in red ink on white cardboard and the letters
shall be at least two inches in size.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.30   RIGHT TO ENTER PREMISES DURING FUMIGATION.
   No person, other than a licensed fumigator or City official in the discharge
of his duty, shall be permitted to enter into any area or chamber in which
fumigating work is in progress.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.31   REMOVAL OF FOOD.
   Unless the fumigant to be used is approved by the United States Public
Health Service as not affecting foods, all food and drink in the building or
room being fumigated shall be removed, except by special exemption of the
Health Officer or when packed in sealed containers or intended to be cooked or
boiled, or when the fumigation performed is for the purpose of destroying
vermin infesting such food.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.32   PROCEDURE BEFORE FUMIGATING.
   Before work is done, the licensee, fumigator or operator in charge shall
inspect the premises and serve notice on all occupants of each room or
apartment within the danger area, stating the danger and precautions to be
observed and designating the rooms and apartments to be vacated and the time in
which the gases, fumes or vapors are to be generated or liberated. The danger
area shall be deemed any room, apartment or other enclosure into which any of
the gases, fumes or vapors may penetrate.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.33   TEMPORARY EVICTION.
   The Health Officer is hereby authorized to order the temporary eviction of
any person or family who may in the course of any fumigation work impede the
completion of the work by refusing to leave the premises, for the time required
for the fumigating process.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.34   EXCEPTION TO NOTICE OF FUMIGATION.
   Where fumigation is done in special rooms, vaults, tanks or cars, the notice
of fumigation shall not be necessary. These special or especially constructed
vaults, rooms, tanks or cars shall be approved as to their location,
construction and gas-tightness by the Health Officer. Proper provision shall be
made for the airing of such vaults and to allow for the escape of such gases,
fumes or vapors without endangering life or health.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.35   SEALING OPENINGS.
   Before fumigating, the licensee shall seal or cause to be sealed securely
all cracks, crevices, openings and apertures in the walls, ceiling and floors
in such a manner and way as to confine the gases, fumes and vapors to the
premises intended to be fumigated.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.36   WATCHMEN.
   During the period fumigation is in process, a capable, alert watchman or
watchmen shall remain on duty at the entrance or entrances to every building or
enclosed space fumigated, except single and two- family residences when wholly
vacated, until after the fumigation is completed and until the premises are
properly ventilated and again safe for human occupancy. All guards and watchmen
shall be reliable persons acceptable as such to the Health Officer. The
licensee shall be held strictly responsible and accountable for the conduct of
his guards or watchmen. All guards or watchmen shall be given definite and
proper instructions by the licensee as to their duties and responsibilities.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.37   HOURS.
   Fumigation shall be carried on only between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 6:00
p.m., except that single dwellings, store rooms or other structures wholly
vacated by the inhabitants thereof during the entire time of fumigation may be
fumigated at times other than between such hours.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.38   RELEASE OF FUMES AND VAPORS.
   After the process of fumigation has been completed, it shall be the duty of
the operator to release the gases, fumes and vapors in a careful manner and in
such a way that they are transmitted to the outside air so as not to endanger
health or life. Such gases, fumes or vapors shall not be released except
between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., except as set forth in Section
727.37. Before permitting any person to enter any building or enclosed space
which has been exposed to gases, fumes or vapors as aforesaid, it shall be the
duty of the operator to make sure that any and all traces of the gases, fumes
and vapors have been removed therefrom.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.39   RE-ENTRY INTO PREMISES.
   No person other than a licensed fumigator or City official in the discharge
of his duty shall be permitted to enter any place where fumigation has been
carried on until all traces of gases have disappeared and the warning signs
have been removed. In no event shall any adult person be permitted to enter any
such premises until six hours after the airing thereof has been commenced; nor
shall any aged, infirm or convalescent adult, nor any child under the age of
six years, be allowed on such premises until sixteen hours after the airing
process has been commenced. No fumigants shall be dropped on the floor or left
exposed where persons or domestic animals may come in contact with them.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.40   RULES AND REGULATIONS; HEALTH OFFICER.
   The Health Officer is hereby authorized and directed to make and enforce
such rules and regulations relative to fumigation, not in conflict with the
provisions of this chapter, as he may deem necessary for the protection of life
and health.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.41   SALE OF FUMIGANTS.
   No person shall sell or give away fumigants, except to persons licensed as
fumigators under the provisions of this chapter, unless a signed statement is
obtained from the recipient of such fumigant to the effect that the same will
not be used for the purpose of fumigating in any building used for human
habitation or otherwise in violation of the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
727.42   SALE OF FERTILIZERS, EXTERMINANTS, INSECTICIDES.
   No fertilizer, exterminant or insecticide shall be sold or offered for sale
in any establishments within the City which sells or offers for sale, prepared
or unprepared food, unless such exterminant, fertilizer or insecticide is
properly packaged in a leakproof metal, glass, plastic or similar container and
plainly marked.
(Ord. 59-61. Passed 5-1-61.)
727.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
CHAPTER 731
Food Establishments
731.01   Employee affected by disease.
731.02    Annual X-ray.
731.03    Liability.
731.04    License required; fee.
731.05    Meat inspection.
731.99    Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Power to inspect food products - see Ohio R.C. 715.46
   Food service operations - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 3732
   License fee - see ADM.
185.04(c)
   Harmful objects in food or confectionery - see GEN. OFF.
636.15 
   Amusement places with music - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 703 
   Removal of food during fumigating - see BUS. REG.
727.31 
731.01   EMPLOYEE AFFECTED BY DISEASE.
   No person owning or conducting any place where food is prepared, cooked,
mixed, baked, exposed, bottled, packed, handled, stored, manufactured, offered
for sale or sold shall knowingly employ any person who is affected with any
communicable disease or with any venereal disease in a communicable form to
work in any place controlled, owner or operated by such person.
   Whenever required, any person employed in such place shall submit to a
physical examination by the Medical Examiner.
(Ord. 46-55. Passed 3-7-55.)
731.02   ANNUAL X-RAY.
   It shall be the duty of each and every owner, manager or operator of any
place where food is prepared, cooked, mixed, baked, exposed, bottled, packed,
handled, stored, manufactured, offered for sale or sold, to require an annual
chest X-ray of every person in his employ and to retain in his possession for
the inspection of any police officer or the Medical Examiner, who may require
it, the report from the chest X- ray.
(Ord. 46-55. Passed 3-7-55.)
731.03   LIABILITY.
   The manager of any establishment owned by a corporation shall be held liable
to carry out the requirements of this chapter.
(Ord. 46-55. Passed 3-7-55.)
731.04    LICENSE REQUIRED; FEE.
   No person shall operate any establishment wherein food is handled as
described in Sections
731.01 and
731.02 without first obtaining a license to do so from the City. The fee for
such license shall be as provided in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule).
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
731.05   MEAT INSPECTION.
   (a)   As used in this section, "meat or meat product" means the flesh or
viscera of cattle, calves, sheep, swine and goats, and any edible product of
same.
    (b)   No person shall dispose of, sell, offer for sale or have in his
possession for sale, whether at wholesale or retail, any meat or meat products
within the City, unless such meat or meat products have been inspected by the
Ohio State Department of Agriculture or bear the inspection mark of the Ohio
State or Federal Department of Agriculture.
731.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
CHAPTER 733
Fortunetelling and Clairvoyancy
   EDITOR'S NOTE: Chapter 733 was repealed in its entirety by Ordinance 166-25,
passed October 6, 2025.
CHAPTER 734
Mobile Food Service Operation
734.01   Definitions.
734.02   Operation in right-of-way; public property.
734.03   Mobile food service operation permit.
734.04   General regulations.
734.05   Property owner permission, time period.
734.06   Suspension or revocation of mobile food service operation permit.
734.07   Voiding of permit.
734.99   Penalty.
734.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Food" shall mean a raw, cooked, or processed edible substance, ice,
beverage or ingredient used or intended for use or for sale in whole or part
for human consumption.
   (b)   "Food service operation license" means the official document issued by
an Ohio County Board of Health or by another jurisdiction's health district
with the authority to license food service operations.
   (c)   "Mobile food service operation" means a food service operation
required to be licensed under Ohio Revised Code that is operated from a single
movable vehicle or portable structure and that routinely changes location.
   (d)   "Mobile food service operation permit" shall mean the permit issued by
the Building Department pursuant to this chapter.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.02   OPERATION IN RIGHT-OF-WAY; PUBLIC PROPERTY.
   (a)   Unless otherwise permitted in this chapter, no person shall cause a
mobile food service operator to operate on any public street or sidewalk within
the City while such public street or sidewalk is open to normal public use.
   (b)   No person shall cause a mobile food service operator to operate on any
public street or sidewalk within the City unless the mobile food service
operation has an existing agreement to participate in a permitted parade,
special event, block party, or public show.
   (c)   No person shall cause a mobile food service operator to operate on
public property, including public parks, unless the mobile food service
operation has an existing agreement to participate in a permitted parade,
special event, block party, public show, or has otherwise received written
permission from the Director of Public Safety.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.03   MOBILE FOOD SERVICE OPERATION PERMIT.
   (a)   No person shall cause a mobile food service operator to operate in the
City unless the operator has received a mobile food service operation permit
from the City.
   (b)   An application for a mobile food service permit shall be submitted to
the Building Department on an application provided by the Building
Commissioner. Applicants must also provide the following documentation upon
submittal of the permit application:
      (1)   A copy of a current mobile food service operation license, and
      (2)   Proof of general liability insurance coverage, including without
limitation, bodily injury and property damage, in coverage amounts of at least
one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence, and naming the City as an
additional insured, in a form that provides that the insurance coverage shall
not be canceled or reduced by the insurance carrier without thirty days' prior
written notice to the City.
   (c)   The fee for a mobile food service operation permit shall be as set
forth in Section
185.04 of this Code of Ordinances.
   (d)   Upon receipt of the completed application, the Building Department
shall tender it to the Fire Department, which shall inspect the mobile food
service operation to ensure it complies with fire and safety standards
promulgated by the Fire Chief, and, upon completion, issue a certification of
compliance to the Building Department.
   (e)   The Building Department, upon receipt of the certificate of compliance
from the Fire Department, and upon a determination that all of the requirements
of this
Chapter 734 have been met, shall issue the mobile food service operation permit
to the applicant, except that the Building Department is not required to issue
a mobile food service operation permit fewer than ten days after receipt of a
completed application.
   (f)   Mobile food service operation permits are effective on a calendar year
basis, and shall expire on March 1st of each year, and are not transferable.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.04   GENERAL REGULATIONS.
   (a)   No person shall operate a mobile food service anywhere in the City and
in any place in, upon, or along the streets or other public places, or engage
in any other activities within the City as described under this Chapter 734,
unless they are the holder of a mobile food service operation permit issued
pursuant to the provisions of this chapter and which is in full force and
effect.
   (b)   No person shall cause a mobile food service operator to:
      (1)   Sell food items, display food items, or conduct vending operations
to the occupants of vehicles stopped in traffic;
      (2)   Display food items or place lines or other devices for the display
of food items on any building or on any utility pole, planter, tree, trash
container, or other sidewalk fixture;
      (3)   Place any food items in or upon any street or sidewalk;
      (4)   Leave a vending device unattended at any time during hours of
operation;
      (5)   Utilize loudspeakers or other noise-making devices in order to
attract attention or in such a way to create a nuisance; or
      (6)   Conduct business without making available a container suitable for
the placement of refuse.
   (c)   All mobile food service operations must:
      (1)   Conspicuously display evidence of their mobile food service
operation permit issued pursuant to this chapter;
      (2)   Be constructed to internally store and contain all wastewater for
proper disposal, to prevent ground water contamination, and to prevent
discharge of any wastewater, grease, oil, food waste, etc., onto the ground or
into any storm water sewer within the City;
      (3)   Obey any lawful order of a police officer to relocate to avoid
congestion or obstruction during an emergency;
      (4)   Operate at all times in accordance and comply with all requirements
of applicable state and local law, including, without limitation, the City's
fire prevention code, the State of Ohio Fire Code, the Ohio Uniform Food Safety
Code, County Board of Health, and the City's traffic and zoning codes; and
      (5)   Exercise reasonable care to ensure that operations do not create a
health or safety hazard to customers, other users of the sidewalks and streets,
or persons on abutting property.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.05   PROPERTY OWNER PERMISSION, TIME PERIOD.
   (a)   All mobile food service operations must obtain written permission from
the property owner to place and operate the mobile food service on the subject
property.
   (b)   Mobile food service operations may not conduct operations at a
property for more than fourteen consecutive days. Upon the expiration of the
fourteen day period, the mobile food service shall be removed from the site and
may not return to the property for a minimum of thirty consecutive days.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.06   SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF MOBILE FOOD SERVICE OPERATION PERMIT.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner may suspend or revoke any mobile food
service operation permit or renewal thereof issued under Section
734.03 for any of the following reasons:
      (1)   Misrepresentation of a material fact by the applicant in obtaining
a mobile food service operation permit, or the renewal thereof;
      (2)   The operator fails to maintain compliance with all regulations
imposed by this chapter, the Building Department, the Department of Public
Safety, the Ohio Department of Health, County Board of Health, or any other
local, state, or federal agencies;
      (3)   Misrepresentation of a material fact to any City official regarding
the mobile food service operation including its use or condition.
   (b)   Notice of the revocation of a mobile food service operation permit
shall be given in writing, setting forth the grounds for the revocation. Such
notice shall be emailed or mailed, postage prepaid, to the licensee at his or
her last known address.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.07   VOIDING OF PERMIT.
   A mobile food service operation permit issued under the provisions of this
Code shall become null and void whenever a change occurs in the use, in whole
or in part, to the mobile food service operation without a permit first having
been obtained for such change.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)
734.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the fourth degree for a first offense, and for a second or subsequent offense,
shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the second degree.
(Ord. 2-25. Passed 4-7-25, amended 5-5-25.)

   CROSS REFERENCES

737.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter
   (a)   "Waste" means all trash, rubbish, garbage, offal and other refuse or
discarded matter required to be removed from private and public places. It
shall not include recognized by-products of any business or industry having
commercial value and regularly handled in the ordinary course of business,
unless such by-products, or the handling of them, shall become a nuisance or
menace to the public health.
   (b)   "Combustible waste" means all waste substances capable of incineration
or burning, including garbage, paper, rags, excelsior, wood, grass, leaves and
the like.
   (c)   "Noncombustible waste" means all waste substances incapable of
incineration or burning, including tin cans, tinware and other metallic
substances, bottles, glassware, earthenware, ashes and similar materials, and
also discarded articles the greater part of which is incapable of incineration
or burning, such as asphalt roofing material, electric batteries and the like.
   (d)   "Garbage" means all putrescible wastes, including vegetable and animal
offal, carcasses of dead animals and the like, but excluding recognized
industrial byproducts.
   (e)   "Ashes" means the residue of combustion of such fuels as wood, coal,
coke, charcoal and the like.
   (f)   "Commercial waste" means all wastes, combustible and noncombustible,
arising out of the operations of business and industry and all other wastes not
resulting from the ordinary operations of private residences or households.
(Ord. 31-61. Passed 3-6-61.)
   (g)   "Refuse bin" means a metal receptacle having an internal volume of one
cubic yard or greater, by actual measurement, which temporarily receives and
holds refuse for ultimate disposal, either by unloading into the body or
loading hopper of a refuse collection vehicle or by other means.
   (h)   "Internal volume" means the actual volumetric capacity of the
container. This may not necessarily correspond to the nominal size rating used
by industry.
   (i)   "Tip over" means that during the application of either test force
described in Section
737.08(a), the refuse bin begins to rotate forward about its forwardmost ground
supports.
(Ord. 37-80. Passed 4-7-80.)
737.02   PERMIT REQUIRED; INSURANCE; WINDSHIELD STICKERS.
   (a)   No person, firm or corporation shall engage in the business of
collection and disposition of waste, combustible waste, noncombustible waste,
garbage, ashes, commercial waste and all other refuse or discarded material
within the City unless a permit to do so has first been obtained by such person
from the Director of Public Service for such purposes.
   Upon payment of a fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) for each
vehicle operated in connection with such business within the City per year or
any part thereof, and the furnishing of evidence of compliance with State law
relating to workmen's compensation, and the submission of a policy or policies
of public liability and property damage insurance, to the approval of the
Solicitor, protecting the City as a named additional insured to the extent of
one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) for an individual accident, three
hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) for a collective accident and twenty-five
thousand dollars ($25,000) property damage arising out of the contractual use
of the City incinerator and/or dumping sites, the Director of Public Service
shall issue to the applicant a windshield sticker indicating the issuance of
the permit herein required.
    (b)   Each operator of a vehicle used in connection with such business
shall secure from the office of the Director of Public Safety a registration
certificate, as provided for in
Chapter 757.
    (c)   If no contractual and permitted use of the City incinerator and/or
dumping sites is made, the insurance required shall be one hundred thousand
dollars ($100,000) for an individual accident, three hundred thousand dollars
($300,000) for a collective accident and twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)
property damage, except that the City shall not be named in such policy of
insurance. However, all other provisions shall be complied with before the
permit is issued.
    (d)   The aforementioned windshield sticker shall be of such size and
composition as meets the approval of the Director of Public Service and the
Purchasing Agent and shall be inscribed "Private Waste Hauler Permit, Parma,
Ohio, NO. ______________" indicating in the blank space the number of the
permit and the year in force, and such other information as the City desires.
Such windshield sticker shall be securely placed on the inside of the
windshield of the truck to which the permit is issued in such a way as to be in
plain view.
   (e)   Nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to apply to the
hauling of waste from premises within the City by the owner or tenant of such
premises except when such owner or tenant performs such services for hire.
    (f)   This section shall be effective for collection or renewal of licenses
July 1 of each year, commencing July 1, 1961.
(Ord. 83-61. Passed 6-19-61.)
737.03   CONSTRUCTION OF VEHICLES; LEAKING LOADS.
   No person, firm or corporation shall use, suffer or permit to be used any
vehicle in transporting and conducting waste, garbage, combustible waste,
noncombustible waste, ashes or commercial waste unless such vehicle is tightly
constructed and equipped with a closely fitted cover and unless such vehicle is
tightly covered at all times except when the same is being loaded or unloaded.
No person, firm or corporation shall load or drive, or cause to be loaded or
driven, on any public way in the City any such vehicle containing any such
materials so as to suffer or permit any part of the contents of such vehicle to
fall, spill or leak therefrom.
(Ord. 33-61. Passed 3-6-61.)
737.04   OPERATION OF VEHICLES; SANITATION.
   No owner of, or person, firm or corporation in possession or control of, any
vehicle used for carrying or transporting the materials defined in Section
737.01 shall permit such vehicle to stand or be stored or kept in such manner
or for such length of time that it will constitute a nuisance. All persons,
firms or corporations in possession of or in control of such vehicles shall
cause such vehicles to be cleaned at least once a week while in use and kept
clean when not in use.
(Ord. 34-61. Passed 3-6-61.)
737.05   COLLECTION FROM NONRESIDENTIAL ESTABLISHMENTS.
   No collection of garbage and refuse shall be made at establishments of a
commercial or industrial nature which abut property used for residential
purposes, except between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. daily.
(Ord. 234-78. Passed 10-16-78.)
737.06   REFUSE BINS; CRITERIA FOR BANNING.
   (a)   Any refuse bin of metal construction produced or distributed for sale
to, or for the personal use, consumption or enjoyment of, consumers, in or
around a permanent or temporary household or residence, a school, in recreation
or otherwise, which is in commerce or being distributed in commerce on or after
the effective date of this ban and which has an actual internal volume of one
cubic yard or greater and tips over when tested under the conditions specified
in Section
737.07 using the procedures described in Section
737.08, is a banned hazardous product and its use is hereby prohibited.
    (b)   A refuse bin is considered capable of tipping over when it begins to
rotate forward about its forwardmost ground supports.
(Ord. 37-80. Passed 4-7-80.)
737.07   TESTING OF REFUSE BINS; CONDITIONS.
   (a)   The refuse bin shall be empty and have its lid or cover in a position
which would most adversely affect the stability of the bin when tested.
   (b)   The refuse bin shall be tested on a hard, flat surface. During
testing, the bin shall not be tilted from level in such a way as to increase
its stability.
    (c)   Those refuse bins equipped with casters or wheels shall have the
casters or wheels positioned in a manner which would most adversely affect the
stability of the bin and shall be chocked to prevent movement.
    (d)   The stability of the refuse bin shall be tested without dependence
upon nonpermanent attachments or restraints, such as chains or guys.
    (e)   For purposes of enforcement, bins shall be tested by authorized City
personnel in that position which most adversely affects their stability.
(Ord. 37-80. Passed 4-7-80.)
737.08   TEST PROCEDURE.
   (a)   The refuse bin shall be tested by applying forces as described in
paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) hereof, as follows:
       (1)   A horizontal force of seventy pounds (311N) shall be supplied to a
point and in a direction most likely to cause tipping.
       (2)   A vertically downward force of 191 pounds (850N) shall be applied
to a point most likely to cause tipping. (See Figure 1 below.)
    (b)   These forces shall be applied separately and the bin shall not tip
over under the application of either action referred to in paragraphs (a)(1)
and (2) hereof.
(Ord. 37-80. Passed 4-7-80.)
737.09   HOURS OF COLLECTION AND TRANSPORTATION.
   (a)   No person owning or driving a vehicle hauling solid waste shall cause
the collection, transportation or transfer of such waste other than between the
hours of 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. No collection, transportation or transfer
shall occur on Saturdays after 4:00 p.m. nor anytime on Sundays. Application
for exceptions to this provision may be made to the Director of Public Service,
on a form provided by the Director. Such exceptions shall be granted only where
the applicant is able to demonstrate circumstances of great practical
difficulty in the collection and transportation of solid waste in areas where
there is heavy daytime vehicular and pedestrian traffic and a concentration of
commercial activity.
   (b)   All vehicles hauling liquid or solid waste within any area of the City
shall obtain a permit from the Director prior to any such hauling.
   (c)   The fee for the permit provided for in subsection (b) hereof shall be
twenty dollars ($20.00) per year.
   (d)   Open-bodied trucks must use a securely fastened water-and rip-
resistant tarp while hauling waste.
(Ord. 124-91. Passed 9-3-91.)
737.10   INCLUSION OF RESIDENTIAL CONDOMINIUM PROPERTIES, COOPERATIVE APARTMENT
CORPORATIONS AND CLUSTER HOME ASSOCIATIONS IN RECYCLING AND TRASH PROGRAMS.
   (a)   The Mayor and the Director of Public Service are hereby authorized and
directed, after the start date of January 1, 1999, to include the following in
the City's recycling and trash hauling programs: residential condominiums
organized pursuant to and in compliance with Ohio R.C. Chapter 5311,
cooperative apartment corporations, and dwellings within single-family cluster
districts organized pursuant to and in compliance with
Chapter 1156 of these Codified Ordinances.
   (b)   The inclusions set forth in subsection (a) hereof are conditioned upon
an agreement being executed by and between the various residential condominium
associations, cooperative apartment corporations and/or cluster home
associations, the City and the City's recycling and trash hauler.
   (c)   As part of any agreement, the residential condominium associations,
cooperative apartment corporations and/or cluster home associations must agree
that the City and the recycling and trash hauler shall not be liable and shall
be held harmless for any street, road or other related damage which may occur
as a result of the inclusion of these properties in the aforementioned
recycling and trash pickups.
   (d)   The funds for the inclusion of residential condominiums, cooperative
apartment corporations and cluster home dwellings in recycling and trash
programs shall be paid from Fund No. 1709-Service Director, Account No. 115-
Refuse Disposal.
(Ord. 122-93. Passed 12-4-95; Ord. 148-98. Passed 9-8-98; Ord. 250-98. Passed
11-4-98.)
737.99   PENALTY.
   (a)   Whoever violates Section 737.09(a) is guilty of a misdemeanor of the
third degree for a first offense and shall be fined not more than five hundred
dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty days, or both. For a second
or subsequent offense, such person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the second
degree and shall be fined not more than seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00)
or imprisoned not more than ninety days, or both, for each offense. A separate
offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on which a violation
occurs or continues.
   (b)   Except as provided in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) hereof, whoever
violates Section
737.09(d) is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined
not more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or imprisoned not more than
thirty days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed
committed each day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.
      (1)   If a violation of Section
737.09(d) results in injury to the property of another, then the offender is
guilty of a misdemeanor of the second degree and shall be fined not more than
seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00) or imprisoned not more than ninety days,
or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.
      (2)   If a violation of Section
737.09(d) results in injury to a person, then the offender is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree and shall be fined not more than one thousand
dollars ($1,000) or imprisoned not more than six months, or both, for each
offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on
which a violation occurs or continues.
   (c)   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter for which a
penalty is not specifically designated is guilty of a misdemeanor of the third
degree and shall be fined not more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or
imprisoned not more than sixty days, or both, for each offense. A separate
offense shall be deemed committed each day or on which a violation occurs or
continues.
(Ord. 124-91. Passed 9-3-91; Ord. 191-91. Passed 9-3-91.)
