752.01   NEWSPAPER DISPENSING DEVICE DEFINED.
   As used in this chapter, "newspaper dispensing device" means a mechanical
container constructed of metal or other material of a substantially equivalent
strength and durability, not more than fifty inches in height and not more than
twenty-five inches in length and width.
(Ord. 181-97. Passed 9-15-97.)
752.02   PERMIT REQUIRED; APPLICATION; ISSUANCE; CONDITIONS.
   (a)   No person shall sell or distribute newspapers, through the use of a
newspaper dispensing device, without first obtaining a permit therefor through
the office of the Director of Public Safety or his or her designee.
    (b)   Applications may be made to, and on forms approved by, the Director
of Public Safety or his or her designee allowing newspaper dispensing devices
on public property along the streets and thoroughfares in the City. Upon a
proper application, the Director of Public Safety or his or her designee shall
grant such permit subject to the following terms and conditions:
      (1)   The permittee shall pay a rental fee as set forth in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (General Fee Schedule) per year or part
thereof, for each location where a newspaper dispensing device is installed.
      (2)   The permittee, upon the removal of a newspaper dispensing device,
shall restore the property of the City to the same condition as when the device
was initially installed, ordinary wear and tear excepted.
      (3)   The permittee shall maintain the device in good working order and
in a safe and clean condition and shall keep the immediate area surrounding
such device free from litter and debris.
      (4)   The permittee shall save and hold the City harmless from any and
all liability, for any reason whatsoever, occasioned upon the installation and
use of each newspaper dispensing device and shall furnish, at the permittee's
expense, such public liability insurance as shall protect the permittee and the
City from all claims for damage to property or bodily injury, including death,
which may arise from the operation of such device under the permit or in
connection therewith. Such policy shall name the City as an additional insured,
shall be in an amount of not less than one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000)
combined single limit for any injury to persons and/or damaged property and
shall provide that the insurance coverage shall not be canceled or reduced by
the insurance carrier without thirty days prior written notice to the City. A
certificate of insurance shall be provided to the City and maintained before
and during the installation of such devices.
      (5)   Permits shall be for a term of one year, shall not be assignable
and shall not grant any permanent right.
(Ord. 181-97. Passed 9-15-97.)
752.03   ADVERTISING AND WRITINGS ON DEVICES.
   Notwithstanding any other provision of these Codified Ordinances or action
of any board of the City, the following minimum provisions shall be contained
in any standards enacted for newspaper dispensing devices:
   (a)   The device shall be permitted to have the logo of the newspaper
contained therein on three sides, the price of the paper contained therein and
the name of the newspaper contained therein on the front.
   (b)   No other advertising or writing of any type shall be permitted
elsewhere on the device.
   (c)   A temporary insert of less than two square feet placed in a bracket on
one and only one side of the newspaper dispensing device, informing the public
of stories or news features of the publication, shall not be considered
advertising or use for publicity purposes.
(Ord. 181-97. Passed 9-15-97.)
752.04   IMPOUNDING AND DISPOSITION; SERVICE OF NOTICE; APPEALS; FEES FOR
RECOVERY OF DEVICES.
   (a)   Upon a determination by the Director of Public Safety or his or her
designee that a newspaper dispensing device has been installed, placed or
maintained in violation of any of the provisions of this chapter, the Building
Department shall issue an order to remedy the violation. The order shall be
served in person or by certified mail on the individual or other person
identified in the permit application. If no permit application for the
newspaper dispensing device has been filed within the City, the order shall be
served on the owner in person or by certified mail. The order shall state the
nature of the violation and provide that the owner has seven business days from
the date of the notice to remedy the violation or to file an appeal from the
order with the Mayor.
   If a violation is neither remedied nor appealed within the time period set
forth in the order issued, the newspaper dispensing device which has been
determined to be in violation may be impounded.
   (b)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the Director of
Public Safety or his or her designee shall take immediate steps necessary to
remove and impound any newspaper dispensing device upon the determination by
the Director of Public Safety or his or her designee that such device has been
installed, placed or maintained in a manner which presents a clear and present
danger to the public health or safety. Within two days of the date of the
impoundment, notice of the impoundment, including the reasons therefor, shall
be served in person or by certified mail to the individual or other person
identified in the permit application. If no permit application for the
newspaper dispensing device has been filed with the City, the order shall be
served on the owner in person or by certified mail. The owner of the impounded
newspaper dispensing device may file an appeal to the Mayor in the manner
prescribed in Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
   (c)   Unless the newspaper dispensing device and its contents are being held
as evidence in a criminal prosecution, the owner of an impounded newspaper
dispensing device may, at any time after impoundment, recover the newspaper
dispensing device upon payment of an impound fee of twenty- five dollars
($25.00) plus the reasonable additional costs, if any, of impounding the
newspaper dispensing device, including a storage charge of one dollar ($1.00)
per device per day for each day in excess of five working days after
notification is given to the owner that said device is in the possession of the
City. Unless the contents of the newspaper dispensing devices are being held as
evidence in a criminal prosecution, the owner of the contents of an impounded
newspaper dispensing device may recover those contents at any time after
impoundment.
(Ord. 181-97. Passed 9-15-97; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
   (d)   The remedies provided for in this section shall be in addition to the
penalty provided in Section
752.99.
752.05   ABANDONMENT.
   (a)   For the purpose of this section, either or both of the following shall
constitute abandonment:
      (1)   In the event a newspaper dispensing device remains empty for a
period of a least thirty consecutive days, said device shall be deemed
abandoned.
      (2)   The newspaper dispensing device is located on the premises of a
vacated or otherwise unoccupied building without written consent of the
property owner, said device shall be deemed abandoned.
   (b)   The Director of Public Safety or his or her designee may treat an
abandoned device in the same manner as provided in Section
752.04.
(Ord. 181-97. Passed 9-15-97; Ord. 244-03. Passed 9-15-03.)
752.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a minor
misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one hundred dollars ($100.00) for
each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or
on which a violation occurs or continues.
CHAPTER 753
Oil and Gas Wells
   EDITOR'S NOTE: This chapter, previously a codification of Ordinance 51-48,
passed July 19, 1948, and Ordinance 196-57, passed July 29, 1957, was reenacted
in its entirety by Ordinance 88-85, passed July 15, 1985.
753.01   Intent.
753.02   Permit required.
753.03   Permit applications.
753.04   Review of applications.
753.05   Approval or rejection of applications by Planning Commission.
753.06   Issuance of permits; bonds; insurance.
753.07   Effective period of permits; renewals; fee.
753.08   Permit limitations.
753.09   Duties of permit holders.
753.10   Well operations.
753.11   Prohibited locations.
753.12   Abandonment of wells; permit required.
753.13   Compliance with Planning and Zoning Code and other State and local
requirements; conflicts.
753.14   Inspections.
753.15   Nonissuance or revocation of permits; stop work orders; changed
conditions.
753.151   Appeals.
753.16   Application of chapter; liability of City and permit holders.
753.99   Penalty; equitable remedies.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   State regulations - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 1509
   License fees - see ADM.
185.04(c)
753.01   INTENT.
   It is the intent of this chapter to regulate the drilling, operation,
deepening and modification of oil and gas wells and the sites upon which such
wells are located in the City in accordance with Ohio R.C. Chapter 1509. These
regulations are necessary to protect the public health, safety and welfare as
well as adjoining properties and the environment.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.02   PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person, corporation or other entity shall commence to drill or operate a
new well for gas or oil, or deepen or modify an existing well for gas or oil,
or the site upon which such a well is located, until a permit for such activity
has been obtained as hereinafter provided from the Director of Public Safety.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.03   PERMIT APPLICATIONS.
   Any person desiring to engage in the drilling or operation of a new well for
gas or oil, or the deepening or modification of any new or existing well for
gas or oil, or the site upon which such a well is located, shall, prior to the
commencement of any operation associated with such activity, make an
application therefor to the Director of Public Safety. Applications shall be
filed by the owner of the property upon which such a well is located or by a
person who has been granted authority by the owner to file such application.
There shall be a separate application filed and permit required for each
proposed well. Such application shall consist of the following:
   (a)   A copy of an approved permit application from the Division of Oil and
Gas of the Ohio Department of Natural Resources. The application shall include
all information required therein along with evidence of compliance with all
conditions for such permit approval.
   (b)   Eight copies of a plat drawn by a registered surveyor to a scale not
smaller than 100 feet to an inch, or as required by the City Engineer, and
indicating:
      (1)   Proposed locations of the well, tanks and other large equipment,
access drives, pipelines, fences, landscaping and any culverts, ditching or
other physical changes to the existing drainage or topography of the site;
      (2)   Locations, uses and ownership of all land, buildings and
structures, parking areas, drives, public rights-of-way, property lines, zoning
and drilling unit boundaries within the drilling unit, and all utility
easements within 1,000 feet of the minimum drilling unit area required;
      (3)   The topography of the site and abutting properties;
      (4)   The designated route for City inspection and emergency access,
proposed truck routes in and out of the site via public roads and proposed
truck routes to the site for such time such trucks are within the City. The
latter route may be provided at a scale approved by the City Engineer.
      (5)   Necessary dimensions to indicate compliance with all minimum
distances required in this section;
   (c)   The name, address and telephone number of a person responsible for the
operation and maintenance of the site and available for contact for emergency
or other purposes;
   (d)   A plan showing all pipelines, connections and shut-off valves for
emergency purposes;
   (e)   A fee as set forth in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule); and
   (f)   Any other information necessary to adequately determine compliance
with this chapter or State law.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.04   REVIEW OF APPLICATIONS.
   The Director of Public Safety may refer each completed application to the
Building Commissioner who shall concurrently submit such application, for
recommendation, to the City Engineer, the Fire Chief and the Director of Public
Service for a review period of not more than ten working days. The resulting
recommendations shall be included in the Building Commissioner's report which,
along with the application, shall be submitted to the Planning Commission for
its action at the end of the review period.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.05   APPROVAL OR REJECTION OF APPLICATIONS BY PLANNING COMMISSION.
   (a)   The Planning Commission may recommend the approval of an application
for a gas or oil well permit.
    (b)   The Commission may recommend the rejection of any application for a
permit which is not in accordance with the requirements of this chapter or
where the proposed drilling, operation, deepening or modification of the well
or site will constitute a serious disadvantage to the City or its inhabitants
by reason of the character and value of the land and existing permanent
improvements within the area of or adjacent to the well and its site and the
extent to which the surrounding land and improvements are adapted for civic
purposes. When a permit is refused, the deposit of cash required to be made
with the application shall be returned to the applicant.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
753.06   ISSUANCE OF PERMITS; BONDS; INSURANCE.
   After the Planning Commission approves an application for a gas or oil well
permit, the Director of Public Safety shall issue the permit upon the
applicant's furnishing:
   (a)   A surety bond in the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000) to
guarantee compliance with all maintenance, restoration and other requirements
of State law and this chapter. This bond shall be maintained until the Director
has verified compliance with all requirements of this chapter and State law,
including, but not limited to, Section
753.09(a), (b), (c) and (d). Forfeiture of the bond may result from a violation
of any of the provisions of this chapter.
   (b)   A policy of public liability insurance having minimum limits of one
million dollars ($1,000,000) per person and two million, five hundred thousand
dollars ($2,500,000) per incident for personal injury, and two hundred thousand
dollars ($200,000) per person and five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) per
incident for property damage, insuring the City and any person suffering any
personal injury or property damage arising from the drilling, operation,
deepening or modification of the well or its site. In lieu of such policies,
the applicant may deposit certificates of insurance showing that he or she has
such policies in effect. The Mayor shall approve the adequacy and the Law
Director the form of such policies or certificates of insurance which shall be
maintained from the time drilling, operation, deepening or modification
activities are commenced until the well is plugged, storage tanks are emptied
and taken out of use and the well and site are abandoned and approved pursuant
to this chapter and State laws, rules and regulations.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.07   EFFECTIVE PERIOD OF PERMITS; RENEWALS; FEE.
   No permit shall be issued under this chapter or any amendment thereto, and
no right or privilege shall be granted hereby or hereunder, existing for longer
than a period of twenty years from the date of the issuance of the permit. The
permit shall be renewed on an annual basis, and if the permittee is not in
violation of the laws of the State or the ordinances of the City relative to
the drilling, operation, deepening and modification of oil and gas wells and
the sites upon which such wells are located, the Director of Public Safety
shall renew the permit upon payment of a fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00).
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.08   PERMIT LIMITATIONS.
   No permit shall be issued for the drilling, operation, deepening or
modification of a well for gas or oil, or the site upon which such well is
located, except upon ground owned by the applicant or held by the applicant
under an oil or gas lease or a drilling contract from the owner giving the
owner's permission to drill, operate, deepen and modify the well and the site
upon which such well is located. Nothing herein contained, nor any permit
issued hereunder, shall be deemed to grant any right or license to the
permittee to enter upon or occupy any land in any respect. When a permit has
been issued, the same shall terminate and become inoperative without any action
on the part of the City unless, within thirty days from the date of issuance,
actual drilling, operation, deepening or modification of the well or site is
commenced as allowed by the permit. After the drilling, operation, deepening or
modification of a well or site has commenced, the cessation of such activities
for thirty consecutive days shall operate to terminate and cancel the permit
and the well and site shall be condemned or abandoned in accordance with this
chapter and State law. Thereafter, no person shall drill, operate, deepen or
modify any such well or site without first obtaining another permit therefor.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.09   DUTIES OF PERMIT HOLDERS.
   The permit holder shall obey all laws of the City and the State which
concern the drilling or operation of oil and gas wells. This includes all laws
now passed or which are passed hereafter. In addition, the permit holder shall:
   (a)   Correct damage to streets, sidewalks, other public places and private
property, which damage results directly or indirectly from activities
associated with drilling, operating, deepening or modifying a well or site;
   (b)   Clear the site and adjacent property of all litter, machinery,
derricks, equipment, buildings, oil or other substances associated with the
drilling, operation, deepening or modification of the well and site, except as
needed for the proper drilling, operation, deepening or modification of the
well or site as allowed by the permit;
   (c)   Correct all disturbances to the land associated with the drilling,
operation, deepening and modification of the well and site, except as necessary
and approved for protection, such corrections to approximate the original shape
and condition of the site prior to the development of the well and site;
   (d)   Prior to the drilling of any well, construct a road providing
emergency and service access to the site. All such roads shall be constructed
of concrete or asphalt to prevent the spread of mud, dust and debris upon any
City street and adjacent property. Such road shall service all operations of
the site and shall have a width and turning radius sufficient to accommodate
the largest contemplated vehicle to service the site.
   (e)   Pay to the owners of any realty, buildings, improvements, goods or
chattels located in the area any extra cost of insurance on the property
imposed by reason of the granting of the permit and by reason of the operation
carried on thereunder; and
   (f)   During the drilling and operation of the well, maintain the site in a
neat, clean and orderly condition. Access roads shall be kept dust free. In
order to keep public roads and adjacent property safe and clean, the permit
holder shall clear public roads of accumulations resulting from the operation
as often as necessary for compliance or upon request of the City.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.10   WELL OPERATIONS.
   While operating under a permit required under this chapter, the permit
holder shall:
   (a)   Provide every drilling rig with a fire extinguisher maintained in good
condition;
   (b)   Not store oil, or erect or maintain a facility for the storage of oil,
in excess of fifty barrels for each well. Any storage shall conform to the
requirements of any present or future ordinance or statute which provides for
the storage of oil or gas.
   (c)   Do no fracturing, tool-dressing or any work or labor which causes a
noise or disturbance, except in emergencies affecting life or property, before
the hour of 6:00 a.m. or after the hour of 10:00 p.m. in any area where there
are inhabited dwellings located within 500 feet of the drilling operation,
unless the owner thereof consents thereto. Drilling operations shall also be
restricted to the hours of 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., unless the operation
requires continuous drilling.
   (d)   Deposit all water, drillings, earth and secretions removed from the
well into a concrete or steel storage tank or into a sludge pit lined with an
impervious liner. Such pit shall be fenced in for safety purposes and shall be
filled in upon cessation of its use.
   (e)   Transport and deposit all sludge, brine or other waste products to a
disposal site approved by the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.11   PROHIBITED LOCATIONS.
   A well for the drilling of oil or gas may be located within the City, except
that no well or storage tank shall be located within 500 feet of a residence,
business or public building or within 150 feet of any public right-of-way.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.12   ABANDONMENT OF WELLS; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person shall plug and/or abandon a gas or oil well unless, upon
application to the Director of Public Safety, a permit is granted to do so. The
fee for such a permit is set forth in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule). The
abandonment of the well shall be performed pursuant to the laws, rules and
regulations of any department or division of the State relevant to the plugging
and/or abandonment of gas or oil wells and pursuant to the ordinances of the
City.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.13   COMPLIANCE WITH PLANNING AND ZONING CODE AND OTHER STATE AND LOCAL
REQUIREMENTS; CONFLICTS.
   All operations associated with the drilling and production of oil and gas
wells, except as otherwise required in this chapter, shall comply with all
requirements of the Planning and Zoning Code, all other ordinances of the City,
all County and State regulations, including Ohio R.C. Chapter 1509, and the
rules and regulations of the Ohio Division of Oil and Gas. Where there is any
conflict between such requirements, the most stringent shall apply.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.14   INSPECTIONS.
   To ensure compliance with this chapter, the Director of Public Safety, the
Building Commissioner, the Fire Chief, the City Engineer and the Director of
Public Service, or their authorized representatives, may enter the property to
inspect and test the site, equipment and other operations and conditions. This
authority may be exercised at any time from the time a well is in the process
of being drilled to the time final abandonment of the well is approved.
    Prior to the issuance of the permit required in this chapter, such
officials shall establish the detailed inspection requirements and notify the
permit holder of the same.
    The route designated by the permit holder in the approved application shall
be used as access to the site for such inspections and for emergencies.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.15   NONISSUANCE OR REVOCATION OF PERMITS; STOP WORK ORDERS; CHANGED
CONDITIONS.
   Failure to comply with any of the provisions of this chapter or State law
shall be grounds to refuse issuance of a permit or to revoke a permit already
issued by the City. The Director of Public Safety, the Building Commissioner,
the Fire Chief, the City Engineer or the Director of Public Service, or their
authorized representatives, may stop any or all work at the site upon finding a
specific violation of this chapter or State law or where continuation would
constitute a direct danger to persons or property. All activities or specified
operations shall cease until such time as the cited violation is brought into
approved compliance with this chapter and State law.
   Any change to any information on the approved application shall be
immediately disclosed in writing to the Director of Public Safety, the Building
Commissioner, the Fire Chief, the City Engineer and the Director of Public
Service. Any one of such officials may temporarily suspend the permit if he or
she feels the change is a significant enough deviation to warrant Planning
Commission approval. The decision shall be made at the next regularly scheduled
Commission meeting.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.151   APPEALS.
   Any denial, suspension, or revocation of a permit under this chapter may be
appealed pursuant to Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
(Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
753.16   APPLICATION OF CHAPTER; LIABILITY OF CITY AND PERMIT HOLDERS.
   This chapter shall apply to the heirs, executors or assigns of any
individual permittee, and to the successors and assigns of any firm,
partnership, association or corporate permittee, as fully as it applies to the
original permittee.
   The provisions of this chapter requiring responsibility of or compliance by
the permit holder, including bond conditions, shall also apply to any assignee
or to any employee, contractor, subcontractor or other person performing
services in connection with the permit. The City shall not be held liable for
the permit holder's property due to failure of City streets. The City shall not
be held liable for any damage or injury directly or indirectly caused by the
transportation of any equipment, material, by-product or waste.
   Any damage suffered to property, caused by or originating from operations
connected with the well, over and above the amount collected on insurance,
shall also be paid to the owners by the permit holder. The City shall be free
and harmless from liability resulting from the issuance of such permit. If the
Fire Chief determines that fire-fighting specialists are needed to provide
adequate protection, the permit holder shall be responsible for all costs.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
753.99   PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDIES.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree and shall be fined not
more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) and imprisoned not more than six
months, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed
each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
In addition, the Law Director may seek injunctive relief against any person, in
any proper court, for any violation of or noncompliance with any of the
provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 88-85. Passed 7-15-85.)
CHAPTER 755
Peddlers; Itinerant Vendors; Temporary Stores
   EDITOR'S NOTE: This chapter, previously a codification of Ordinance 318-91,
passed January 27, 1992, Ordinance 135-92, passed June 1, 1992, Ordinance 186-
93, passed September 20, 1993, Ordinance 177-96, passed September 16, 1996, and
Ordinance 217-96, passed October 21, 1996, was repealed in its entirety by
Ordinance 125-99, passed July 6, 1999. For provisions relating to itinerant
vendors and temporary stores, see Chapter 738. For provisions relating to
peddlers and solicitors, see Chapter 757.
CHAPTER 757
Peddlers and Solicitors
757.01   Definitions.
757.02   License required.
757.03   License application, fee, revocation and suspension; appeal.
757.04   Street peddling or vending; adult attendant required; prohibition.
757.05   Permitted hours for peddling and soliciting.
757.06   Resident prohibition by notice.
757.99   Penalties.
757.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Peddler" means any person traveling either by foot, automobile, truck
or another type of conveyance from place to place, door to door or street to
street, taking or attempting to take orders for profit by the sale of goods,
wares, and merchandise or personal property of any nature whatsoever for
immediate or future delivery or for services to be furnished or performed
immediately or in the future; and
   (b)   "Solicitor" means any person who obtains or seeks to obtain funds for
any cause whatsoever by traveling door to door either by foot, automobile,
truck or any other type of conveyance upon the private residences, including
any house, apartment or other dwelling, within the City.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06.)
757.02   LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No peddler shall peddle within the City unless he or she is the holder of a
valid license issued pursuant to this chapter.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06.)
757.03   LICENSE APPLICATION, FEE, REVOCATION AND SUSPENSION; APPEAL.
   (a)   Any person wanting a license shall obtain an application for same from
the office of the Director of Public Safety, and shall submit the completed
application, along with a valid driver's license or identification card issued
by the State of Ohio or any other State for inspection and copying, and an
appropriate fee to such office, on a form supplied by the Director, which shall
contain the following information:
      (1)   Name, address, and social security number of the applicant;
      (2)   Name and address of the organization represented; and
      (3)   A description of the proposed peddling activities.
   (b)   (1)   All license applications shall be referred to the Director, or
his or her designee, who shall, within 72 hours after receipt of the completed
application, issue licenses to the peddlers, unless the Director finds that:
         A.   The applicant has provided false information in his or her
application; and/or
         B.   The applicant or peddler named on the license application has
been convicted of a felony violation or misdemeanor violation involving fraud
or moral turpitude within the past five years.
      (2)   Any license issued under this chapter shall be valid for one
calendar year, expiring on December 31.
   (c)   Each applicant shall pay a non-refundable fee of fifty dollars
($50.00) per license, which fee shall be paid at the time the application is
submitted.
   (d)   Once issued, a license may be used only in conformity with the laws of
the City and the State of Ohio; may not be assigned or transferred; must be
carried by the licensee at all times; and shall be revoked by the Director of
Public Safety for any of the following causes:
      (1)   The licensee or person preparing the application on behalf of the
licensee provided false information in the license application;
      (2)   The licensee is convicted of a felony or misdemeanor involving
fraud or moral turpitude; and/or
      (3)   The licensee has previously been convicted of any violation of
Chapter 757 of these Codified Ordinances, and is subsequently cited for a
violation of any provision of
Chapter 757.
   (e)   In the event a license application is not approved, or in the event
any license issued pursuant to the provisions of this chapter is suspended or
revoked, written notice shall be given to the applicant or licensee by personal
service or certified mail. Any denial, suspension, or revocation of a license
under this chapter may be appealed pursuant to Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06; Ord. 116-12. Passed 6-4-12; Ord. 104-22. Passed 8-
22-22; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
757.04   STREET PEDDLING OR VENDING; ADULT ATTENDANT REQUIRED; PROHIBITION.
   No person shall peddle or vend from a vehicle in public streets and public
places in the City without a license issued under this chapter. Persons in
pursuit of such peddling or vending business or activity when children under
age 18 collect, congregate, assemble or gather about such vehicle for the
purpose of making purchases therefrom or in response to such person's actions,
are hereby required to be accompanied by an adult attendant whose sole duty and
occupation shall be to protect and safeguard such children from injury or
hazards of vehicular traffic using such streets and public places. The
attendant shall maintain a constant lookout for approaching vehicles and shall
warn and guard children from injury therefrom. Ice cream trucks shall be
prohibited to peddle or vend from a vehicle in City parks and private
properties.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06.)
757.05   PERMITTED HOURS FOR PEDDLING AND SOLICITING.
   (a)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, no peddler or
solicitor, while peddling or soliciting, shall call upon, knock at the door or
ring the doorbell of any residence, house, apartment or other dwelling in the
City before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday, or before
12:00 p.m. or after 9:00 p.m. on Sunday.
   (b)   Division (a) of this section shall not apply to any visit to the
premises as a result of a specific request or appointment made by a lawful
possessor and occupant of said premises.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06.)
757.06   RESIDENT PROHIBITION BY NOTICE.
   (a)   If requested by the City, and for as long as the Northeast Ohio Public
Energy Council ("NOPEC") shall agree to do so, NOPEC shall manage for the City
a "Do Not Knock Registry" ("Registry") and is authorized to contact persons on
the Registry to distribute "Do Not Knock" stickers to them at no cost to the
City or to said persons. NOPEC shall further contact persons listed on the
Registry to update the Registry on a quarterly basis each year.
   (b)   Any person in lawful possession and occupancy of any residence, house,
apartment or other dwelling in the City may require NOPEC to place and maintain
his or her residence, house, apartment or other dwelling on the Do Not Knock
Registry by submitting a request on form(s) supplied by the Director of Public
Safety, or by submitting a request online at www.blocktheknock.com or at a
Block the Knock community event, which shall contain the following information:
      (1)   The name and signature of the person completing the form(s), unless
the submission is done electronically;
      (2)   The complete address of the residence, house, apartment or other
dwelling to be placed on the Do Not Knock Registry;
      (3)   A valid email address of the person completing the form(s);
      (4)   The date the form was completed;
      (5)   A statement that "No Solicitors or Peddlers Shall Call at this
Address" or words of similar import; and
      (6)   The exceptions, if any, which the person completing the form(s)
wishes to be made to the requirement that peddlers or solicitors not knock at
his or her residence, house, apartment or other dwelling.
   (c)   Any person in lawful possession and occupancy of any residence, house,
apartment or other dwelling in the City may require the City or NOPEC to remove
his or her residence, house, apartment or other dwelling from the Do Not Knock
Registry by submitting a Notice of Removal form supplied by the Director of
Public Safety, or by submitting a request online to www.blocktheknock.com which
shall contain the following information:
      (1)   The name and signature of the person completing the form;
      (2)   The complete address of the residence, house, apartment or other
dwelling to be removed from the registry;
      (3)   The date the form was completed; and
      (4)   A statement that the residence, house, apartment or other dwelling
be removed from the Do Not Knock Registry.
   (d)   The decision whether to place a residence, house, apartment or other
dwelling on the Do Not Knock Registry shall be solely that of the lawful
possessor and occupant thereof and no official, agent or employee of the City
of Parma shall interfere with said decision.
   (e)   A residence, house, apartment or other dwelling, after being lawfully
placed on the Do Not Knock Registry shall remain on said registry until the
earliest of any of the following:
      (1)   The City or NOPEC receives a Notice of Removal pursuant to division
(c) of this section; or
      (2)   The City or NOPEC receives formal notice that the person who
submitted the form pursuant to division (b) of this section is not or is no
longer a lawful possessor and occupant of the premises.
   (f)   A copy of the Do Not Knock Registry shall be made available for public
inspection during normal business hours at the office of the Director of Public
Safety.
   (g)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, no peddler, while
peddling, or solicitor while soliciting, shall call upon, knock at the door or
ring the doorbell of any residence, house, apartment or other dwelling in the
City which is at that time on the Do Not Knock Registry established and
maintained pursuant to this chapter or upon which there is posted at the
entrance a notice which reads "No Peddlers Allowed", "No Solicitors Allowed",
"Do Not Knock" or words of similar import, which clearly prohibit peddlers or
solicitors on the premises, unless such peddler or solicitor has previously
been invited upon the premises by the lawful possessor and occupant thereof.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06; Ord. 178-17. Passed 10-2-17.)
757.99   PENALTIES.
   (a)   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the fourth degree on the first offense and shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree for a second or subsequent violation of this
chapter or of any substantially similar chapter of these Codified Ordinances.
   (b)   A violation of Section
757.06, in addition to other penalties provided for in this chapter, is deemed
as trespass and shall be punishable as set forth in Sections
698.02 et seq. of these Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 50-06. Passed 4-24-06.)
CHAPTER 759
Pesticide Users
759.01   Definitions.
759.02   Registration required.
759.03   Notification to abutting residents.
759.04   Posting of notice at premises.
759.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Pesticides - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 921
   Depositing poison in public place - see Ohio R.C. 3719.30
   Cutting noxious weeds and grass - see GEN. OFF.
660.22 
   Exterminating and fumigating - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 727
   Trees - see S. & P. S.
Ch. 911 
759.01   DEFINITIONS.
   The definitions contained in the Ohio Pesticide Law, Ohio R.C. Chapter 921,
are hereby adopted by reference as if fully set forth herein. In addition, as
used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Pesticide" means:
      (1)   Any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing,
destroying, repelling or mitigating any pest; and
      (2)   Any substance or mixture of substances intended for use as a plant
regulator, defoliant or desiccant.
   (b)   "User of pesticides" means any person who applies pesticides or causes
pesticides to be applied to property or the atmosphere by any means where such
person is engaged in applying pesticides for hire to trees, lawns, shrubs and
plants.
(Ord. 68-87. Passed 5-18-87.)
759.02   REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   (a)   On or after July 1, 1987, no user of pesticides shall engage in the
use or application of pesticides in the City without first registering in the
office of the Director of Public Safety and obtaining a registration
certificate. The user shall furnish proof of a current Ohio Pesticide Law
License, the name, address and telephone number of the user, the generic
chemical names of pesticides to be used and any other information the Director
deems necessary.
   (b)   After receipt of the user information as required in subsection (a)
hereof, and review by the Director, the Director shall issue to the user a
registration certificate if the user fully complies with the requirements of
this chapter and the Ohio Revised Code.
(Ord. 68-87. Passed 5-18-87; Ord. 76-96. Passed 3-4-96.)
759.03   NOTIFICATION TO ABUTTING RESIDENTS.
   (a)   Residents of the City may register at any time after the passage of
this chapter (Ordinance 68-87, passed May 18, 1987), and thereafter annually,
on or before April 1, with the Director of Public Safety, to have their names
put on a list to be given to users of pesticides. Residents who desire to be
notified of the application of pesticides may include the listing of not more
than five addresses supplied by the registrant and contiguous to the
registrant's property.
    (b)   All users shall acquire such list from the Director on a monthly
basis and shall give notice of an application of pesticides to each registered
resident requesting the same prior to such application. Notice shall consist of
an oral or written prenotification to any resident registered to receive notice
with regard to a specific address. If prenotification fails, the user shall
place a notice on the door of the home to be notified that such application has
taken place.
(Ord. 68-87. Passed 5-18-87.)
759.04   POSTING OF NOTICE AT PREMISES.
   (a)   Pursuant to Ohio R.C. 731.231, there is hereby adopted by the City,
for the purpose of prescribing regulations governing applications of lawn
pesticides to residential, commercial and public lawns in the City, that
certain rule known as The Requirements for Notice for Lawn Pesticide
Applicators, Rule 901:5-11-9 of the Ohio Department of Agriculture, promulgated
pursuant to Ohio R.C. 921.16 on May 25, 1989, and effective June 5, 1989, and
the same is hereby adopted as though fully rewritten herein, save and except
such portions as may be hereinafter deleted, modified or amended.
    (b)   Whenever in Rule 901:5-11-9 the phrase "any municipal corporation or
subdivided area of a township" appears, the phrase "City of Parma" is hereby
substituted therefor.
    (c)   A complete copy of such Rule shall be on file in the offices of the
Clerk of Council and the Director of Public Safety for inspection by the
public. A complete copy shall also be on file in the County Law Library. The
Clerk of Council shall also have copies available for sale to the public, at
cost.
(Ord. 31-90. Passed 2-20-90.)
759.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined not
more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or imprisoned not more than
thirty days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed
committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or
continues.
(Ord. 68-87. Passed 5-18-87.)
CHAPTER 763
Public Picnics
763.01   Definitions.
763.02   Owners and operators; license required.
763.03   Application; information required.
763.04   Toilets required.
763.05   Sanitary regulations; refuse containers.
763.06   Inspection regulations.
763.07   License fee; expiration.
763.08   License revocation; disorderly conduct.
763.09   Sponsors; permit required.
763.10   Appeals.
763.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Admissions tax - see ADM.
Ch. 181 
   License fees - see ADM.
185.04(c)
   Disorderly conduct - see GEN. OFF.
648.04
763.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Public picnic or recreation place" means any place where any person
or persons (other than the owners of such place) or the general public is
allowed or permitted to enter, frequent, come into or use, either free and
without charge or for hire or upon payment of some fee or charge or thing
therefor, for the purpose of rest, relaxation, recreation, amusement, eating,
lunching, picnicking, social intercourse or diversion.
   (b)   "Public picnic" means any gathering or assembly of persons at any
public picnic or recreation place to which admission can be had by payment of a
fee or by the purchase, possession or presentation of a ticket or token or in
which a charge is made for caring for clothing or other property or any other
gathering or assembly of persons at a public picnic or recreation place to
which the general public may gain admission with or without the payment of a
fee.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.02   OWNERS AND OPERATORS; LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall establish, maintain or operate any public picnic or
recreation place without being licensed to do so as hereinafter provided.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.03   APPLICATION; INFORMATION REQUIRED.
   Application for the license shall be made in writing to the Director of
Public Safety.
   The application shall set forth the name of the applicant and, if a
corporation, the name and residence of the principal officers. It shall state
the location for which the license is desired and shall contain a correct
description of the land and premises together with the correct boundaries of
same and, if the land and premises contain more than one acre of ground, there
shall be an accurate map thereof attached to the petition and identified with
the name of the applicant. There shall be indicated on the application a
description of all buildings and structures on the premises with a statement of
the number and kind of rooms in the buildings and the purpose for which such
buildings and structures are designed to be used in connection with the
license.
   The application shall state the number of water closets or toilets on the
premises and their location with respect to the premises.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.04   TOILETS REQUIRED.
   No license shall be issued unless there are erected and in suitable working
order two separate and distinct water closets or toilets on the premises
constructed and installed in accordance with State law and/or the ordinances
and regulations of the City, as required.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.05   SANITARY REGULATIONS; REFUSE CONTAINERS.
   Any and all picnic or recreation places and buildings and structures and
toilets thereon and things appurtenant thereto shall be maintained in good
repair, thoroughly clean and free from any accumulation of filth, garbage,
rubbish and other waste. Receptacles sufficient to contain all of the garbage,
rubbish and other waste accumulated therein shall be provided as required by
ordinance or regulations of the City.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.06   INSPECTION REGULATIONS.
   Any police officer, the Director of Public Safety or the Chief of Fire shall
at all times have the right to enter, inspect and examine the picnic or
recreation place and for such purpose to remain there for any length of time as
the officer deems necessary.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.07   LICENSE FEE; EXPIRATION.
   A fee for a license for a picnic or recreation place as provided in this
chapter shall be as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) which shall
be paid to the City at the time of issuing the license. Each license granted
hereunder shall expire on May 15 of each year.
(Ord. 51-52. Passed 4-21-52; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
763.08   LICENSE REVOCATION; DISORDERLY CONDUCT.
   The license may be revoked or forfeited by the Director of Public Safety for
disorderly or immoral conduct on the premises or for violation of any of the
provisions of this chapter, of State law or of any ordinance of the City,
perpetrated or committed on the premises or by the licensee under this chapter.
If any license is so revoked or forfeited, then at least six months shall
elapse before another license shall be issued to the licensee.
(Ord. 67-25. Passed 5-18-25.)
763.09   SPONSORS; PERMIT REQUIRED.
    No person shall hold, conduct or sponsor a public picnic without first
obtaining a permit therefor. Applications for such permits shall be made to the
Director of Public Safety. The Director shall issue such permits upon being
satisfied that the proposed public picnic will in no way be detrimental to the
public health, safety and welfare and upon payment to him by the applicant of a
fee as set forth in Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee
Schedule).
763.10   APPEALS.
   Any denial, suspension, or revocation of a license or permit under this
chapter may be appealed pursuant to Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
(Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
763.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
CHAPTER 767
Public Outdoor Shows
767.01   Definition.
767.02   License required.
767.03   Performance standards.
767.04   Duration of license.
767.05   Exception.
767.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Unlawful congregation on sidewalks, public grounds - see GEN. OFF.
648.04(a)(4)
   Disturbing lawful assemblage - see GEN. OFF.
648.06 
   Motion picture machines - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 751 
   Public picnics - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 763
   Fire prevention - see Part Thirteen - Fire Prevention Code
767.01   DEFINITION.
   The term “public outdoor show”, as used in this chapter, means any outdoor
circus, menagerie, wild west show, dog or pony show, or other show or
exhibition, given, conducted, produced, presented or offered for gain or
profit.
(Ord. 119-70. Passed 5-18-70; Ord. 345-08. Passed 1-5-09.)
767.02   LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person, either as owner, lessee, manager, officer or agent, or in any
other capacity, shall give, conduct, produce, present or offer for gain or
profit any public outdoor show, without first securing from the Director of
Public Safety a license for that purpose and paying therefor a license fee as
set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule).
(Ord. 119-70. Passed 5-18-70.)
767.03   PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.
   Each outdoor public show shall comply with the following performance
standards as a condition precedent to obtaining the license provided for in
Section
767.02:
   (a)   All public outdoor show operations shall be conducted upon a lot
situated entirely within a use district classified as an Industrial "A"
District or Industrial "B" District by these Codified Ordinances. However, if
such lot is adjacent to a residence district, no operations of such public
outdoor show shall be conducted within 100 feet of such residence district;
   (b)   All public outdoor show operations shall be conducted entirely upon a
lot not occupied by a "main building" as defined in Section
1121.19 of these Codified Ordinances;
   (c)   A game played for money or anything of value is prohibited as a part
of the operation of such public outdoor show;
    (d)   Every person, whether the owner, lessee, manager, officer, agent or
employee of the public outdoor show, or who is connected therewith in any other
capacity, shall be of good reputation and high moral character;
   (e)   An applicant for the license provided for in Section
767.02 shall post a cash bond as surety for the compliance of such public
outdoor show, or any person connected therewith, with the provisions of this
chapter. If such provisions are complied with, such bond shall be returned to
the applicant not later than five days after the cessation of the operations of
the public outdoor show. However, upon the violation of any provision of this
chapter, the Director of Public Safety shall order such bond to be forfeited
and credited to the General Fund of the City.
(Ord. 119-70. Passed 5-18-70.)
767.04   DURATION OF LICENSE.
   Each license issued under the provisions of this chapter shall authorize the
applicant to operate a public outdoor show at the place thereon described for
seven days, commencing on the day after the date of its issuance and no longer,
subject to revocation or cancellation for noncompliance with any of the
provisions of this chapter, these Codified Ordinances or the laws of the State.
No more than one license shall be issued to any one public outdoor show or
applicant in any year.
(Ord. 119-70. Passed 5-18-70.)
767.05   EXCEPTION.
   Nothing contained in this chapter shall be deemed to regulate a public
outdoor show operated by a charitable organization upon a lot owned by a
charitable organization.
(Ord. 119-70. Passed 5-18-70.)
767.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day a violation continues shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 119-70. Passed 5-18-70.)
CHAPTER 771
Sale of Goods Manufactured by Blind Persons
771.01   Declaration of concern.
771.02   Definitions.
771.03   Labelling.
771.04   Permits.
771.05   Fraudulent misrepresentation.
771.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Right-of-way of blind person - see TRAF.
371.02 
   Dogs with blind, deaf or mobility impaired persons - see GEN. OFF.
618.30
   Assaulting assistance dogs - see GEN. OFF.
642.31
771.01   DECLARATION OF CONCERN.
   Any misrepresentation that goods offered for sale are the products of blind
workers is hereby declared to be a special matter of public concern.
(Ord. 222-60. Passed 12-5-60.)
771.02   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Blind" means a person having a central visual acuity not to exceed
20/200 in the better eye, with correcting lenses, or visual acuity greater than
20/200, but with a limitation in the field of vision such that the widest
diameter of the visual field subtends an angle no greater than twenty degrees,
or a person with a progressive eye disease whose visual acuity or field
limitation may be expected to become further impaired to the point of the
standards set forth above. In all cases, diagnosis of blindness or progressive
eye disease must be made by a qualified physician skilled in diseases of the
eye.
    (b)   "Goods or articles made by blind workers" means goods or articles in
the manufacture of which not less than seventy-five percent of the total hours
of direct labor is performed by blind workers.
   (c)   "Manufacturing" means the preparation, processing and packaging of
goods or articles.
   (d)   "Direct labor" means all work required for the manufacture of goods or
articles, but not including administration, sales, supervision, inspection and
shipment or delivery.
(Ord. 222-60. Passed 12-5-60.)
771.03   LABELLING.
   In manufacturing goods or articles where blind workers are employed, the
product may only be labelled "made by blind workers" if seventy-five percent of
the direct labor is performed by blind workers.
(Ord. 222-60. Passed 12-5-60.)
771.04   PERMITS.
    (a)   (1)   No person, firm or corporation or its distributor may
manufacture, sell, market or otherwise dispose of any goods or articles to the
public which, by way of any imprint, stamp, label, firm name or other printed
matter, indicate that such goods or articles were made by blind workers or
which by word of mouth or otherwise have been represented to be made by blind
workers, without first obtaining a permit in writing from the Director of
Public Safety upon a form prescribed by the Director.
      (2)   None of the provisions of this section are meant to apply to any
person, firm or corporation marketing goods or articles made by blind workers
on the premises of an established retail grocery or department or variety store
permanently located within the City.
   (b)   Issuance of permits provided for in subsection (a) hereof shall be
upon application submitted to the Director of Public Safety accompanied by an
affidavit (as outlined in subsection (c) hereof) and such fees as the Director
may establish, but not to exceed five dollars ($5.00) for each person, firm or
corporation plus no more than one dollar ($1.00) for each agent or
representative listed pursuant to subsection (c)(3).
   (c)   Every person, firm or corporation or its City distributor wishing to
secure a permit shall submit the affidavit of such person, or, if a firm or
corporation, the affidavit of its president, setting forth the following:
       (1)   Name, local address and phone number of the applicant.
      (2)   Name, local address and phone number of its president or local
representative.
      (3)   Method of selling to be employed, that is, telephone, house-to-
house solicitation, etc. The names of individual agents or representatives
including solicitors of all types, whether telephone or house-to-house, and
delivery men which such applicant believes will represent him.
      (4)   Whether products to be sold are products manufactured by blind
persons.
      (5)   Assertion that such products meet all the standards set forth
herein.
   No person shall knowingly submit an application or affidavit that is false
in any of its particulars.
   (d)   The Director shall, upon receipt of the application and affidavit,
issue the permits provided for in subsection (a) hereof when he is satisfied
that the goods or articles to be manufactured, sold or marketed will meet the
standards set forth herein. It shall be the responsibility of the applicant to
properly complete the individual permit forms secured from the Director to
reflect the required information for individual agents or representatives and
further to keep the Director informed at all times of the current holder, if
any, of such permit.
   (e)   The Director shall issue the regulations which may be necessary for
the implementation of the various provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 222-60. Passed 12-5-60.)
771.05   FRAUDULENT MISREPRESENTATION.
   (a)   No goods or articles which are intended by label, symbol, trade name,
name of the manufacturer or seller or other printed matter, word of mouth or
otherwise to indicate that they were made by a blind worker shall be displayed
or offered by any person, firm or corporation for sale in this City unless at
least the above specified percentages of the total hours of direct labor of
producing such goods or articles purported to be made by the blind worker have
been performed by the blind worker.
   (b)   Any person, firm or corporation licensed under this chapter is hereby
authorized to imprint, stamp, label or use a symbol upon such goods or articles
of merchandise or affix thereto labels, stamps or symbols containing the words
"made by a blind workman" or "made by blind workers" or "blind made", provided
that not less than the above specified percentages of the total hours of direct
labor of production have been performed by a blind workman or workmen, to which
label shall be added the name and location of the individual or organization
manufacturing such goods or articles.
   (c)   No person, partnership, firm, corporation, institution or association
may use or employ such imprint, stamp, symbol, label or firm name or by word of
mouth or through another, whether or not such imprint, symbol, stamp or label
is used, to indicate or tend to indicate or represent that the articles were
manufactured by a blind worker or by blind workers when in fact such articles
were not so made, manufactured or fabricated.
(Ord. 222-60. Passed 12-5-60.)
771.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than three hundred dollars ($300.00) or imprisoned not more than ninety
days, or both. In addition, the offender's permit shall be automatically
revoked.
(Ord. 222-60. Passed 12-5-60.)
CHAPTER 773
Sale of Irradiated Foods
773.01   Definitions.
773.02   Sale of irradiated food prohibited; exception.
773.03   Applicability.
773.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Implied warranty of merchantability - see Ohio R.C. 1302.27
   Pure Food and Drug Law - see Ohio R.C. 3715.01 et seq.
   Placing harmful substance or objects in food or confection - see GEN. OFF.
636.15 
   Food establishments - see BUS. REG.
Ch. 731 
   Drive-in restaurants - see P. & Z. 1163.16, 1167.09, 1169.10
773.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Food" means fruits, vegetables, meats, poultry, eggs, dairy products
and other natural and processed products offered for sale for human or animal
consumption.
   (b)   "Irradiated food" means any food treated with ionizing radiation from
radioactive sources, x-rays or electron beams and includes any food which
contains an ingredient that has been irradiated, provided, however, that if the
irradiated ingredients of any food consist solely of spices which have been so
treated, such food shall not be deemed an irradiated food on account of such
irradiated spices.
(Ord. 12-90. Passed 3-19-90.)
773.02   SALE OF IRRADIATED FOOD PROHIBITED; EXCEPTION.
   It shall be unlawful for any merchant, broker or processor to knowingly
sell, offer for sale or expose for sale an irradiated food except as otherwise
provided in this chapter, whether or not such food is deemed to be adulterated
under the provisions of these Codified Ordinances. It shall not be unlawful
under this chapter for any merchant, broker or processor to knowingly sell,
offer for sale or expose for sale an irradiated food to a hospital, medical
clinic, physician or physician's office for use as part of a medical regimen in
the care or treatment of persons with an immune system deficiency or other
disease, provided the irradiated food is packaged with or accompanied by a
warning label that it is intended for medical use only by such persons upon a
physician's advice, nor shall it be unlawful for such persons to knowingly
sell, refer for sale or expose for sale an irradiated food if both of the
following requirements are met, on or before May 1, 1990:
   (a)   The premises on which any such irradiated food is sold, offered for
sale, or exposed for sale, are prominently posted with a sign at or near each
public entrance to such premises, on which sign is printed a message stating
that irradiated food is offered for sale or exposed for sale on such premises;
and
   (b)   Every irradiated food offered or exposed for sale within such premises
is either individually labelled as being an irradiated food, or is so offered
or exposed for sale only in the immediate vicinity of a conspicuous label which
relates to that food and which indicates that it is an irradiated food.
(Ord. 12-90. Passed 3-19-90.)
773.03   APPLICABILITY.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to irradiated foods purchased
prior to the effective date of this chapter.
(Ord. 12-90. Passed 3-19-90.)
773.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the third degree for a first offense and shall be fined not more
than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty days, or
both.
   For a second or subsequent offense, such person is guilty of a misdemeanor
of the second degree and shall be fined not more than seven hundred fifty
dollars ($750.00) or imprisoned not more than ninety days, or both.
(Ord. 12-90. Passed 3-19-90.)
CHAPTER 774
Sale of Pseudoephedrine
774.01   Definitions.
774.02   Restrictions on the sale of pseudoephedrine products.
774.03   Restrictions on public access to pseudoephedrine products.
774.04   Reporting theft of pseudoephedrine products.
774.05   Separate violation for each incident.
774.06   Strict liability offenses.
774.07   Enforcement liability.
774.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Pseudoephedrine sales, State law provisions - see Ohio R.C. 2929.25 -
2929.28; GEN. OFF.
620.15
774.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Count" means the number of pills, tablets, capsules or individual
units of a substance contained within an individual package.
   (b)   "Counter" means any obstructive, physical barrier that separates
pseudoephedrine products from access by a customer or the general public, and
which makes such products available to a customer or the general public only
through or by the act of an employee of the seller.
   (c)   "Customer" means any person who purchases or acquires products from
any retail store or establishment.
   (d)   "Pseudoephedrine" means any drug product, substance or compound,
whether legal or illegal, that contains ephedrine, ephedrine hydrochloride,
pseudoephedrine hydrochloride, pseudoephedrine sulfate, pseudoephedrine, or
phenylpropanolamine, or any of their salts, isomers, or salts of isomers, alone
or in a mixture.
   (e)   "Package" means any bottle, box, blister pack or other container in
which products containing pseudoephedrine are sold.
   (f)   "Retail store or establishment" means any single geographic location
of any business, company, corporation, person, employee or associate that sells
products, including ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, or phenylpropanolamine, to any
customer. It does not include any wholesaler engaged in a wholesale
transaction.
   (g)   "Wholesaler" means one whose business is the selling of goods in gross
to retail stores for purposes of resale.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.02   RESTRICTIONS ON THE SALE OF PSEUDOEPHEDRINE PRODUCTS.
   (a)   No person shall, during a single transaction, sell to a customer more
than three packages of products containing pseudoephedrine.
   (b)   No person shall, during a single transaction, sell to a customer
products containing pseudoephedrine where the total count exceeds 100.
   (c)   No person shall sell product containing pseudoephedrine to a person
under 18 years of age.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.03   RESTRICTIONS ON PUBLIC ACCESS TO PSEUDOEPHEDRINE PRODUCTS.
   All packages of any products whose sole active ingredient is pseudoephedrine
may not be offered for retail sale by self service, but only from behind a
counter or other barrier so that such products are not directly accessible by
the public but only by a retail store employee or agent.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.04   REPORTING THEFT OF PSEUDOEPHEDRINE.
   (a)   Any person who sells pseudoephedrine products and discovers a theft,
disappearance or other loss of a pseudoephedrine product shall report the
theft, disappearance or loss in writing to the Parma Police Department within
three calendar days of such a discovery.
   (b)   Any person who sells pseudoephedrine products shall report to the
Parma Police Department any difference between the quantity of pseudoephedrine
products shipped and the quantity of pseudoephedrine products received within
three calendar days of such a discovery.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.05   SEPARATE VIOLATION FOR EACH INCIDENT.
   Each incident in violation of this
Chapter 774 shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.06   STRICT LIABILITY OFFENSES.
   Violations of any provision of this chapter shall be treated as a strict
liability offense regardless of intent.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.07   ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITY.
   A complaint for a violation of this chapter shall be referred, for
investigation, to the Director of Public Safety or his designee. The Director
of Public Safety shall be authorized to administer and enforce the provisions
of this chapter.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)
774.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the fourth degree for a first offense and, for a second or
subsequent offense within one year of the first offense, is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree.
(Ord. 196-05. Passed 7-18-05.)

CHAPTER 777
Body Art
777.01   Definitions.
777.02   Application of chapter.
777.03   License required; fees.
777.04   Safety and sanitation standards.
777.05   Record keeping. (Repealed)
777.06   Disposal of contaminated items. (Repealed)
777.07   Inspections.
777.08   Tattooing diseased, intoxicated, or drugged persons; minors.
(Repealed)
777.09   Denial, suspension or revocation of licenses.
777.10   Conflicts of laws.
777.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Hazardous and solid waste - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 3734
   Endangering children - see GEN. OFF.
630.01
   Spreading contagion - see GEN. OFF.
660.02
777.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Body art" means the practice of physical body adornment, including
tattooing, permanent cosmetics and/or body piercing. This definition does not
include practices that are considered medical procedures by the state medical
board, performed with medical devices, that include but are not limited to
biopsy or dermal punches and scalpels.
   (b)   "Body art establishment" means any place where tattooing and/or body
piercing is performed.
   (c)   "Body artist" means an individual, including an owner, who performs
the tattooing or body piercing in the establishment.
   (d)   "Body piercing" means the piercing of any part of the body by someone,
other than a physician licensed under R.C. Chapter 4731, who utilizes a needle
or other industry specific instrument for the purpose of inserting an object
into the body for non-medical purposes. Body piercing also includes surface
anchors and surface piercing. This definition does not include practices that
are considered medical procedures by the state medical board, performed with
medical devices that include, but are not limited to, biopsy or dermal punches
and scalpels.
   (e)   "Certificate of Inspection" means written approval from the Building
Commissioner or his or her authorized representative that states that the
tattooing establishment has been inspected and meets all of the terms of this
chapter.
   (f)   "Owner'' means any individual, firm, company, corporation or
association who or which owns, controls, or operates an establishment where
tattooing and/or body piercing is performed.
   (g)   "Patron" means a person requesting and receiving body art services or
body piercing services, also known as a customer.
   (h)   "Tattoo", " tattooed" or "tattooing" means any permanent or semi-
permanent design upon or under the skin made by puncturing the skin and
inserting indelible colors or pigments, resulting in an alteration of the
appearance of the skin.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
777.02   APPLICATION OF CHAPTER.
   The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all body art establishments,
body artists, and owners who or which are operating on the effective date of
this chapter or at any time thereafter. The provisions of this chapter shall
not apply to a physician licensed to practice medicine in the State of Ohio who
is tattooing or body piercing for a medical purpose.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
777.03   LICENSE REQUIRED; FEES.
   (a)   No person shall operate a body art establishment without first
obtaining a license to engage in such business in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter and any applicable state statutes and codes.
   (b)   An application for a license to operate a body art establishment shall
be made annually to the Safety Director on forms prescribed and provided by the
City. The applicant shall submit all information the Safety Director determines
is necessary to process the application. Every application shall be accompanied
by a fee in the amount of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00). Licenses are
nontransferable. Any change of ownership or occupancy shall require a new
license with payment of all required fees. All licenses will expire on December
31 of each calendar year, and the fee for licensing shall not be prorated.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
777.04   SAFETY AND SANITATION STANDARDS.
   The safety and sanitation standards applicable to body art establishments,
owners and body artists under R.C. Chapter 3730, including, but not limited to,
requirements for the disposal of waste items, age prohibitions, record keeping,
and training of body artists, together with the rules adopted by the Ohio Board
of Health under O.A.C. Chapter 3701-9, are hereby adopted and incorporated
fully as if said statutes and codes were written herein in their entirety. The
provisions of R.C. Chapter 3730 and O.A.C. Chapter 3701-9 shall operate as the
minimum requirements for all body art establishment operating in the City of
Parma.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
777.05   RECORD KEEPING. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: Section 777.05 was repealed by Ordinance 40-24, passed
October 7, 2024.)
777.06   DISPOSAL OF CONTAMINATED ITEMS. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: Section 777.06 was repealed by Ordinance 40-24, passed
October 7, 2024.)
777.07   INSPECTIONS.
   (a)   An applicant for a license to operate a body art establishment shall
first obtain a certificate of inspection from the Safety Director indicating
that the establishment has been inspected and is in compliance with the
provisions of this chapter and all applicable state laws.
   (b)   The Safety Director or his or her designee shall have authority to
conduct annual and other periodic inspections as may be necessary of any body
art establishment for the purpose of determining whether or not the
establishment, owners thereof, and body artists working therein are in
compliance with all applicable provisions contained in this chapter and any
other applicable City and/or state laws.
   No person shall willfully prevent or restrain the Safety Director or his or
her designee from entering any body art establishment for the purpose of
inspecting said premises and all relevant business records, after proper
identification is presented to the owner of the establishment or any body
artist working therein.
   (c)   The certificate of inspection shall be posted within the body art
establishment to serve as public notice that the establishment has been
inspected and is in compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
777.08   TATTOOING DISEASED, INTOXICATED, OR DRUGGED PERSONS; MINORS.
(REPEALED)
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: Section 777.08 was repealed by Ordinance 40-24, passed
October 7, 2024.)
777.09   DENIAL, SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF LICENSES.
   The Safety Director may deny, suspend or revoke the license of a body art
establishment for noncompliance with or violation of any provision of this
chapter. Any denial, suspension or revocation of a license under this chapter
may be appealed pursuant to Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
777.10   CONFLICTS OF LAWS.
   In the event of any conflict between any provisions of this chapter or the
Ohio Revised Code, including any rules and regulations adopted pursuant to this
chapter and/or the Ohio Revised Code, and any other City ordinance, including
any rules and regulations adopted pursuant to such ordinances, that provision
or ordinance which establishes the higher or stricter standard for the
promotion or protection of the health or safety of the people shall govern.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98.)
777.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the first degree and shall be fined not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000)
or imprisoned not more than six months, or both. A separate offense shall be
deemed committed each day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.
(Ord. 11-98. Passed 2-17-98; Ord. 40-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
CHAPTER 779
Taxicabs

779.02   Public vehicle license required; exemptions.

   CROSS REFERENCES

   Taxicab stands - see Ohio R.C. 715.25(A)
   Authority to fix rates - see Ohio R.C. 715.25(C)
