779.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Taxicab" means every public vehicle for the transportation for hire
of passengers for which public patronage is solicited in whole or in part upon
the streets or in public or quasi-public places.
   (b)   "Taximeter" means any mechanical device by which the charge for hire
of a taxicab is mechanically calculated and is plainly indicated by means of
figures upon such device.
   (c)   "Automobile for hire" means every public vehicle which does not seek
its business on the public streets and is driven by and is in charge of the
owner or his agent.
   (d)   "Owner" or "applicant" means any person, firm or corporation who owns
or controls or directs the operations of any public vehicle or derives any
revenue or benefits from the operation of any public vehicle, which public
vehicle operates on or over the streets of the City, whether as owner,
licensee, bailee or otherwise, except a driver, as hereinafter defined.
   (e)   "Driver" means every person actually in charge of the operation of a
public vehicle as a chauffeur thereof, whether such person is an owner, agent,
servant or employee of the owner.
   (f)   "Taxicab stand" means those portions of the street set aside and
designated by the Director of Public Safety for the parking of taxicabs waiting
for and seeking employment.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
   (g)   "Public vehicle" means any taxicab or automobile for hire.
779.02   PUBLIC VEHICLE LICENSE REQUIRED; EXEMPTIONS.
   (a)   No person shall operate a public vehicle into, from or within the City
without first having obtained a license to do so from the Director of Public
Safety.
   (b)   Transportation Network Companies, Transportation Network Company
Drivers, and Transportation Network Company Services, as these terms are
defined in Ohio R.C. 3942.01, are exempt from the provisions of this Chapter.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47; Ord. 43-16. Passed 3-21-16.)
779.03   CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO ISSUANCE OF PUBLIC VEHICLE LICENSE.
   No license for the operation of public vehicles shall be issued unless and
until Council, by resolution, declares that public convenience and necessity
require the issuance of such license. The resolution shall specify the number
of public vehicles in respect to which such license may be issued. Upon the
passage of the resolution, approved by the Mayor, the Director of Public Safety
shall be authorized to issue the license.
   Before the adoption of the resolution, Council shall provide for a public
hearing or hearings, notice of the date of which shall be given to all existing
licensees, as may be necessary to determine whether public convenience and
necessity require the issuance of such license and the number of public
vehicles in respect to which the license should be issued. In determining
whether public convenience and necessity require the issuance of any such
license, Council shall take into consideration:
   (a)   The number of public vehicles then licensed.
   (b)   Whether the requirements of public convenience and necessity can be
met and complied with only by the issuance of such license or of any additional
license.
   (c)   The resulting effect upon the business of existing licensees and upon
the existing agencies of mass transportation.
   (d)   The effect on traffic congestion and safety of the public using the
streets.
   (e)   The effect upon working conditions and wages or other compensation
paid to drivers of public vehicles of existing licensees.
   (f)   The financial responsibility of the applicant.
   (g)   Any other factors which Council may deem relevant.
   In the event Council determines that public convenience and necessity
require the issuance of any additional license, holders of existing licenses
shall be given the opportunity to furnish any additional service in respect to
which the claim is asserted that the licensing of additional public vehicles is
required, and Council shall not authorize the issuance of any additional
license unless existing licensees shall, within a time stipulated in the
resolution, fail to provide the required additional service. 
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.04   APPLICATION FOR PUBLIC VEHICLE LICENSE.
   Every applicant for a license to operate a public vehicle shall file a
written application with the Director of Public Safety containing the following
information:
   (a)   The full name, age and residence of the applicant, and, if the
applicant is a partnership, the full name, age and residence of each of the
partners, and, if a corporation, the full name of the corporation, together
with full names of its principal officers.
   (b)   The name under which the applicant will do business.
   (c)   The type of vehicle which is proposed to be used in the service, with
information as to the age, carrying capacity and motor power of same; the color
scheme, local symbols to be used, together with all other lettering or marks
proposed to be used by the applicant on the vehicles.
   (d)   The number of vehicles proposed to be used and the rate of fare to be
charged and the method of charging the same.
   (e)   The applicant is capable of and will carry liability insurance or bond
or agreement, as hereinafter provided for.
   (f)   The application shall be accompanied with a fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) to cover the
amount of expense that Council deems the City will incur in investigating the
application and serving notice of the required public hearing.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.05   INSPECTION.
   (a)   No vehicle covered by this chapter shall be licensed until it has been
thoroughly inspected by the Director of Public Safety or by some person
designated by him and found to be in a thoroughly safe condition for the
transportation of passengers, or until the taximeter attached to the taxicab
has been in the same manner inspected and found to be accurate within five
percent. However, in the case of vehicles already licensed by the City of
Cleveland, it shall not be necessary to make the inspections herein set forth.
   (b)   The Director is hereby authorized and empowered to establish
reasonable rules and regulations for the inspection of taxicabs and automobiles
for hire, and their appurtenances, construction and condition of fitness as he
deems best for the safety and adequate transportation of passengers and the
public in general.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.06   INSURANCE REQUIRED.
   No person shall operate a public vehicle, nor shall any license be issued
hereunder, until the applicant for such license deposits with the Director of
Public Safety a policy or certificate of liability insurance for each public
vehicle for which a license is sought, acceptable to and approved by the
Director and Solicitor, indemnifying the applicant in the sum of at least one
hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) for injury to one person, three hundred
thousand dollars ($300,000) for injury to more than one person and ten thousand
dollars ($10,000) property damage in any one accident, through the operation of
the public vehicle by the applicant. The policy shall further contain a clause
obligating the insurance company to give ten days' written notice to the
Director before cancellation of the policy. Upon the lapse or termination of
the policy of insurance, the licensee's license shall automatically expire.
779.07   CONTINUING LIABILITY; NEW POLICIES.
   The policy of insurance shall contain a provision for continuing liability
thereunder to the full amount thereof, notwithstanding any recovery thereon. If
at any time, in the judgment of the Director of Public Safety, the policy is
not sufficient for any cause, the Director may order the owner of the public
vehicle to replace the policy with another approved by the Director and the
Solicitor. Failure to furnish the replacement policy within the time specified
in the order shall operate as a revocation of the license to operate the
particular vehicle or vehicles covered by the policy ordered to be replaced.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.08   CLEVELAND TAXICAB LICENSE.
   In the case of public vehicles already licensed by the City of Cleveland and
for which license an insurance policy or certificate or other evidence of
financial responsibility of the kind and character above described has been
filed with the City of Cleveland, it shall be sufficient if the licensee files
a copy thereof with the Director of Public Safety, provided that the policy or
certificate or other evidence of financial responsibility provides protection
in limitation at least equal to that herein described and in the opinion of the
Solicitor protects person or property injured or damaged by the operation of
vehicles while traveling to, within or from the City.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.09   PUBLIC VEHICLE LICENSEES' REPORTS.
   It shall be the duty of every licensee to furnish to the Director of Public
Safety semiannually or annually, as the Director may direct, a complete
statement of claims filed and unsatisfied judgments rendered against the
licensee arising out of the operation of public vehicles, which statement shall
be in such form as the Director may prescribe.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.10   ISSUANCE OF PUBLIC VEHICLE LICENSE.
   If the Director of Public Safety has been directed to issue a license, and
if he finds that the public vehicle or vehicles in respect to which the license
is authorized are fit and safe for the transportation of passengers, then, upon
the deposit with the Director of the insurance policy or certificate, or a copy
thereof in the case of public vehicles already licensed by the City of
Cleveland, and upon the payment of the license fee, the Director shall issue a
license.
   Thereupon, the Director shall deliver to the licensees license cards which
shall contain the official license number, name and address of the licensee and
other information as the Director prescribes for a public vehicle to be so
licensed, which license card shall be affixed to the interior of the public
vehicle as to be visible to passengers. However, it shall not be necessary to
issue license cards to vehicles already licensed by the City of Cleveland,
which City issues cards carrying similar information. 
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.101   COMPLAINT PROCEDURE.
   The Office of the Director of Public Safety, in the handling of complaints,
shall adhere to and be responsible for the following procedure:
   (a)   Receipts of complaints, written or verbal, concerning taxi-cab
companies and taxi-cab drivers.
   (b)   Acknowledgment to the complainant of the receipt therefor, if received
by mail.
   (c)   Investigation and report shall show the name and address of the
complainant, the date and nature of the complaint, as well as a statement of
what has been done to take care of the complaint.
   (d)   Retention by the Office of the Director of Public Safety of one copy
in a file known as the open file.
   (e)   If the subject of the complaint represents a danger of bodily harm to
the public, investigation by the Office of the Director of Public Safety shall
commence within twenty-four hours. The subject of other complaints shall be
addressed in a timely manner based upon priority.
(Ord. 114-01. Passed 5-21-01.)
779.11   SUPERVISORY POWERS OF SAFETY DIRECTOR.
   The Director of Public Safety shall have the following powers with respect
to every license to operate:
   (a)   The Director may at any time revoke or suspend any license to operate
if he finds:
      (1)   That the owner's past record is unsatisfactory.
      (2)   That the owner/driver fails to take the most direct route in
driving passengers to their destination.
      (3)   That the owner fails to operate his licensed public vehicle or
vehicles in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, other ordinances of
the City and the laws of the State.
      (4)   That the owner has failed to keep on deposit with the City the
bond, policy or certificate of insurance or security agreement required by this
chapter.
   (b)   In the event that any vehicle licensed hereunder shall become
unsuitable for operation, a written statement to such effect may be filed with
the Director, who shall thereupon transfer the license to any other vehicle
belonging to the owner, provided the vehicle conforms with all the provisions
of these Codified Ordinances.
   (c)   The Director shall not suspend or revoke any license without giving to
the owner thereof due and reasonable notice and granting to the owner a fair
hearing. Any owner whose license has been suspended or revoked by the Director
may appeal from the decision of the Director thereon to the Mayor as
hereinafter provided.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47; Ord. 114-01. Passed 5-21-01; Ord. 121-24. Passed
10-7- 24.)
779.12   DRIVER'S LICENSE REQUIRED; APPLICATION.
   No person shall drive a public vehicle unless he is licensed to do so. An
applicant for a driver's license shall:
   (a)   Be at least twenty-one years of age or over and be an American citizen
or have declared his intention to become a citizen.
   (b)   Be of sound physique, with good eyesight and not subject to vertigo,
heart trouble or any other infirmity of body or mind which might render him
unfit for the safe operation of a public vehicle. Each applicant shall supply
an affidavit to the Director of Public Safety as part of his application for a
license to the effect that he is free from any and all of the infirmities
mentioned in this section.
   (c)   Be able to read, write and speak the English language.
   (d)   Be clean in dress and person, of good moral character and not addicted
to the use of intoxicating liquors and/or drugs.
   (e)   Produce, on forms to be provided by the Director, affidavits of his
good character from two reputable citizens of the City or the County who have
known him personally, and a further testimonial on a form provided for that
purpose, from his last employer, unless, in the estimation of the Director,
sufficient reason is given for its omission.
   (f)   Fill out, upon a form to be provided by the Director, a statement
giving his full name, residence, experience in driving motor vehicles, places
of residence for five years previous to moving to his present address, age,
color, height, color of eyes and hair, place of birth, length of time he has
resided in the County, whether a citizen of the United States, place of
previous employment, whether single or married, whether he has ever been
arrested or convicted of a felony or misdemeanor, whether he has been summoned
to court, whether he has previously been licensed as a driver or chauffeur, and
if so, whether his license has ever been revoked, and for what cause. Such
statement shall be signed and sworn to by the applicant and filed with the
Director as a permanent record. The Director is hereby authorized to establish
additional rules and regulations covering the issuance of drivers' licenses,
not inconsistent herewith, as may be necessary and reasonable.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.13   PHOTOGRAPH OF DRIVER.
   Each applicant for a driver's license must file with his application three
unretouched photographs of himself, in such position as the Director may
direct, taken within the thirty days preceding the filing of his application.
Such photographs shall be of a size which may be easily attached to his
license. One of such photographs shall be attached to the license when issued
and the others shall be filed with the application in the office of the
Director. The photograph shall be so attached to the license that it cannot be
removed and another photograph substituted without detection. Each licensed
driver shall, upon demand of a policeman or a passenger, exhibit his license
and photograph for inspection. Where the application for a license is denied,
two copies of the photograph shall be returned to the applicant by the
Director.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.14   PHYSICAL EXAMINATION.
   The Director of Public Safety shall make investigation or examination of
every applicant for a driver's license as he deems necessary, and he may, in
his discretion, appoint deputies to serve without compensation in assisting him
in investigating and examining applicants for drivers' licenses. The Director
may, if he deems it necessary, require any applicant for a driver's license to
submit the certificate of a reputable physician showing that he has examined
the applicant within sixty days prior thereto and that he has found him to be
of sound physique, with good eyesight and not subject to vertigo, heart trouble
or any other infirmity of body or mind which might render him unfit for the
safe operation of a public vehicle.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.15   ISSUANCE OF DRIVER'S LICENSE.
   If, upon satisfactory fulfillment of the foregoing requirements and if the
Director of Public Safety finds the applicant to be a fit and proper person to
operate a public vehicle, then upon the payment of the license fee there shall
be issued to the applicant a license which shall be in such form as to contain
the photograph and signature of the licensee and blank spaces upon which a
record may be made of any arrest or of any serious complaint against him. Any
licensee who defaces, removes or obliterates any official entry made upon his
license shall be punished by the revocation of his license. Drivers' licenses
shall be issued as of January 1 of each year, and shall be valid to and
including December 31 next succeeding unless previously revoked.
   The provisions of Sections
779.12 through
779.15 shall not apply to drivers already examined and licensed by the City of
Cleveland, in which case it shall be sufficient that there be filed with the
Director an affidavit to that effect containing the name and address of the
driver together with his Cleveland license number.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.16   DRIVER'S BADGE. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section 779.16 was repealed by Ordinance 265-88, passed
October 3, 1988.)
779.17   RENEWAL OF DRIVERS' LICENSES.
   The Director of Public Safety may renew a driver's license from year to year
by appropriate endorsement thereon. A driver, in applying for a renewal of his
license, shall make application not less than thirty days next preceding its
expiration upon a form to be furnished by the Director entitled "Application
for Renewal of License", which form shall be filled out with the full address
and name of the applicant together with a statement of the date upon which the
original license was granted, and the number thereof.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.18   FEE FOR DRIVER'S LICENSE.
   Before the issuance of a driver's license, a fee as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) shall be paid
to the Director of Public Safety.
    In case of fleet owners already licensed in the City of Cleveland, the
provisions of this section shall not be applicable, provided, however, that
such driver's license has not been suspended or revoked by the City of
Cleveland.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.19   SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF DRIVER'S LICENSE.
   Drivers' licenses may be suspended or revoked at any time by the Director of
Public Safety for violations of the terms of this chapter. Any suspension shall
be noted on the license, together with a statement of the reasons therefor, and
the driver shall be deprived of his badge by the Director and the same shall
not be returned to the driver until the expiration of the period of suspension.
Upon a second suspension, within the same licensing year, the Director shall
revoke the license of such driver. No driver whose license has been revoked
shall again be licensed as a driver under this chapter unless upon presentation
of reason satisfactory to the Director.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.191   SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF PUBLIC VEHICLE LICENSE.
   Public Vehicle Licenses may be suspended or revoked at any time by the
Director of Public Safety for violations of the terms of this chapter. Any
suspension shall be noted on the license, together with a statement of the
reasons therefor. Upon a second suspension, within the same licensing year, the
Director shall revoke the Public Vehicle License of the taxi-cab company. No
taxi-cab company whose license has been revoked shall again be licensed as a
public vehicle under this chapter unless upon presentation of reason
satisfactory to the Director.
(Ord. 114-01. Passed 5-21-01.)
779.20   RECORD OF DRIVERS' LICENSES.
   There shall be kept in the office of the Director of Public Safety a
complete record of each license issued to a driver, and of all renewals,
suspensions and revocations thereof, which record shall be kept with the
original application of the driver for a license.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.21   METHOD OF CHARGING FARES; RATE SCHEDULE.
   (a)   A person licensed to operate a taxicab or fleet of taxicabs within the
City shall immediately file with the Director of Public Safety a schedule of
fares to be charged and the manner of computing the same. The license issued
shall not become effective until the schedule of fares to be charged is so
filed with the Director and the method of computing the same has been approved
by Council.
   (b)   The maximum rates of fare, computed by meter, for gasoline-fueled or
propane-fueled taxicabs shall be as follows:
      (1)   For the first one-sixth of a mile or fraction thereof, one dollar
and eighty cents ($1.80);
      (2)   For each succeeding one quarter mile or fraction thereof, thirty-
five cents ($.35); and
      (3)   For each such taxicab employed upon an hourly rate, twelve dollars
($12.00) per hour.
   (c)   The maximum rate of fare for coaches, for each coach employed upon an
hourly rate, shall be four dollars ($4.00) per hour.
   (d)   The rate for waiting or traffic delay shall be fifteen dollars
($15.00) per hour, except for coaches hired at the hourly rate.
   (e)   The rate for each trunk carried outside shall be twenty cents ($.20).
For ordinary handbags or suitcases, there shall be no charge.
   (f)   Irrespective of the foregoing, licensees who are already licensed by
any municipality in the County may charge a rate equal to, but not in excess
of, those prevailing in the City.
(Ord. 249-97. Passed 8-18-97.)
779.22   DISPLAY OF RATE SCHEDULE.
   The operator of a taxicab or fleet of taxicabs licensed to operate in the
City shall display in a conspicuous place in each cab so operated the schedule
or rate of fares charged and the method of computing the same.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.23   PREPAYMENT OF FARE; PASSENGERS' PREROGATIVES.
   Every driver of a taxicab or automobile for hire shall have the right to
demand payment of the legal fare in advance and may refuse employment unless so
prepaid, but no driver of a public vehicle shall, otherwise, refuse or neglect
to convey any orderly person or persons upon request anywhere in the City,
unless previously engaged. No driver of a licensed taxicab or automobile for
hire shall carry any other person than the passenger first employing a taxicab
or automobile for hire without the express consent of such passenger.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.24   DISPUTED FARES.
   All disputes as to the lawful rate of fares shall be determined by the
police officer in charge of the station or the police officer nearest to where
the dispute is had. No person shall fail to comply with such determination.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.25   LOITERING NEAR TAXICABS.
   No person shall loiter within a distance nearer than twenty-five feet of any
public vehicle occupying space upon a taxicab stand.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.26   FICTITIOUS INFORMATION.
   No person shall give any fictitious information or practice any fraud,
misrepresentation or subterfuge in order to secure each or any license provided
for in this chapter.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.27   EMPLOYMENT OF NONLICENSED DRIVER.
   No person operating public vehicles into, from or within the City shall
employ as a driver on such public vehicle any other than a driver duly licensed
or registered under the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.28   FRONT SEAT REGULATION.
   No owner or driver shall permit anyone to ride in the front seat of a
taxicab, while the same is engaged for hire, unless there is insufficient room
in the rear portion of the taxicab to seat the passenger or passengers
comfortably.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47.)
779.29   PICKUP AND DELIVERY OF PASSENGERS; FOREIGN TAXICABS.
   Taxicabs licensed by other municipalities may deliver passengers from
outside the City of Parma to any point inside the City of Parma. However, such
taxicabs shall not pick up passengers in the City of Parma or beyond without
full compliance with all the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 150-57. Passed 6-17-57.)
779.30   APPEALS.
   Appeals from the decisions made under the provisions of this chapter may be
made as prescribed under Section
700.04 of the Business Regulation Code.
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47; Ord. 121-24. Passed 10-7-24.)
779.99   PENALTY.
   (a)   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter for which no
penalty is otherwise provided shall be fined not more than five hundred dollars
($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six months, or both. Each day's continued
violation shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
   (b)   Whoever violates Section
779.24 shall be fined not more than one hundred dollars ($100.00).
(Ord. 417-47. Passed 3-17-47; Ord. 114-01. Passed 5-21-01.)

Registration of Snow Plow Operators
780.01   Registration procedure.
780.02   Display of tags.
780.03   Miscellaneous.
780.99   Penalty.
780.01   REGISTRATION PROCEDURE.
   The Building Commissioner shall register and issue sticker registration tags
to all applicants who:
   (a)   Complete an applicable form prescribed by the Building Commissioner
for the registration of private snow removal companies and/or persons providing
snow removal services in the City;
   (b)   Pay an annual registration fee as set forth in
Chapter 185 for each vehicle for which sticker registration tags are to be
issued;
   (c)   Demonstrate proof of liability insurance.
(Ord. 242-05. Passed 1-17-06.)

   All private snow removal companies, persons, firms or individuals shall
prominently display, on each vehicle used in snow removal or plowing, a current
registration tag issued by the Building Commissioner at all times while such
vehicle is engaged in removal, pushing or plowing of snow on private property
within the City.
(Ord. 242-05. Passed 1-17-06.)
780.03   MISCELLANEOUS.
   Each vehicle shall be equipped with a yellow flashing light which shall be
turned on and active at all times during snow removal operation.
(Ord. 242-05. Passed 1-17-06.)
780.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be sentenced in accordance
with Section
698.02.
(Ord. 242-05. Passed 1-17-06.)
CHAPTER 783
Trailer Rentals
783.01   Definitions.
783.02   License required.
783.03   License application.
783.04   License for separate locations; trade name.
783.05   Insurance required.
783.06   Expiration of license.
783.07   Transfer of license.
783.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Licensing house trailers - see Ohio R.C. 4503.06
   License fee - see ADM.
185.04(c)
   Trailer parking - see TRAF.
351.14 
   Trailer homes - see GEN. OFF.
Ch. 670 
783.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Trailer" means and includes all trailers except tractor trailers and
truck trailers.
   (b)   "Trailer renter" means any person in the business of renting trailers,
which is to say any person who receives compensation or reward for supplying,
furnishing, leasing or renting a trailer to another in any manner, except by
sale; or who offers, furnishes, leases, rents or supplies a trailer or trailers
to others in return for articles purchased or services rendered; or who,
directly or indirectly, receives any remuneration, reward or return for
furnishing a trailer to another other than by a bona fide sale.
(Ord. 48-50. Passed 7-3-50.)
783.02   LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall hold himself out as a renter of trailers or conduct, operate
or carry on the business of renting trailers without first having obtained a
license as a trailer renter.
(Ord. 48-50. Passed 7-3-50.)
783.03   LICENSE APPLICATION.
   Every person desiring to engage in the business of renting trailers shall
make written application to the Director of Public Safety for a license to do
so. The application shall state the name, address and telephone number of the
applicant and the length of time the applicant has been located at the address
set forth in his application. The application shall be in affidavit form and
sworn to by the applicant. No license shall be issued to any person who is not
himself the owner of all of the trailers and equipment for which licenses are
applied, who does not have a trailer license issued to him by the State, in his
own name, and who does not maintain a bona fide place of business under his own
name in the City.
(Ord. 75-53. Passed 6-1-53.)
783.04   LICENSE FOR SEPARATE LOCATIONS; TRADE NAME.
   No licensee shall operate any business under more than one trade name. A
separate operating license must be issued for each separate place of business.
(Ord. 75-53. Passed 6-1-53.)
783.05   INSURANCE REQUIRED.
   Every applicant must furnish proof satisfactory to the Director of Public
Safety that every statement set forth in the affidavit is true and that, in
addition, the applicant carries adequate public liability and property damage
insurance in such amount as the Director deems proper, but in no event to be
less than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) for each person and one hundred
thousand dollars ($100,000) for more than one person in the same accident,
public liability insurance, and ten thousand dollars ($10,000) property damage
insurance, for each trailer. Each applicant shall furnish with his application
an endorsement of an insurance company authorized to do business and in good
standing in the State, in such form as the Director deems proper, showing the
issuance of the insurance herein required, which endorsement shall be kept on
file in the office of the Director. No license shall be valid until such
insurance is provided for and furnished.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
783.06   EXPIRATION OF LICENSE.
   All licenses issued under the provisions of this chapter shall expire on
December 31 following the date of the issuance of same. The license fee shall
be payable in advance before the issuance of such license, or any renewals
thereof, and shall be as provided in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule).
(Ord. 70-52. Passed 6-2-52.)
783.07   TRANSFER OF LICENSE.
   Any duly authorized trailer renter holding a valid license issued in
accordance with all of the provisions of this chapter shall have the right to
sell, assign, transfer and deliver the same to any other person desiring to
engage in the business of a trailer renter, provided the assignee conforms to
all of the provisions of this chapter and is himself entitled, by virtue of
compliance, to a license in his own name. No license shall be assigned,
transferred or delivered that has been revoked, that has expired, where the
holder thereof is in violation of any of the provisions of this chapter or
where the Director is not satisfied that the assignee is entitled to a license
in his own name or that he is in compliance with all of the requirements of
this chapter. No license issued hereunder shall be assigned, transferred or
delivered from the location for which it is issued to another location.
(Ord. 75-53. Passed 6-1-53.)
783.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)

CHAPTER 789
Self-Storage Facilities
   
789.01   Definitions.
   
789.02   Siting, design and use regulations.
789.01   DEFINITIONS.
   "Self-storage facility" means any real property that is designed and used
for the purpose of renting or leasing individual storage spaces in the
facility, whether as rooms, lockers, containers, or other indoor and/or outdoor
space, to individuals, businesses, or other entities for the purpose of storing
possessions. The term "self-storage facility" shall include mini-storage
facilities.
(Ord. 186-2020. Passed 1-19-21.)
789.02   SITING, DESIGN AND USE REGULATIONS.
   (a)   The ground building coverage shall not exceed fifty percent of the
gross land area of the parcel proposed for development, and in no event shall
the site plan reflect a second story or higher level that is larger than the
ground floor footprint.
   (b)   No outdoor washing of any kind shall be permitted, with the exception
of washing the parking lot, the structure and the windows on the structure, and
landscaping.
   (c)   The storage of any toxic, explosive, corrosive, flammable or hazardous
materials or keeping of animals is prohibited. Fuel tanks on any motor vehicle,
boat, lawn mower or similar property will be drained or removed prior to
storage.
   (d)   Exterior walls of the ends of all storage units shall be of masonry or
face-brick construction as approved by the Planning Commission and landscaping
pertaining to screening and buffering shall comply with
Chapter 1199 of the Parma Municipal Code.
   (e)   All storage units must be accessible by paved circular drives clearly
marked to distinguish traffic flow. A minimum twenty-four-foot drives shall be
provided between buildings. Site circulation shall be designed to accommodate
fire trucks, as well as trucks that will customarily access the site.
   (f)   All self-storage facilities must have security installed. Examples
include but are not limited to property fencing, lighting, motion sensors, key
pads and access control hardware, security cameras, video monitors, gate and
digital gate operator, unit alarms and electronic doors.
   (g)   Self-storage facilities shall not be permitted on corner lots.
   (h)   The only activities permitted in individual storage units shall be the
rental of the unit and the pickup and deposit of goods and/or property in dead
storage. Storage units shall not be used for activities such as: Residences,
offices, workshops, studios, hobby, rehearsal areas, garage or estate sales or
auctions.
   (i)   No manufacturing, fabrication, or processing of goods, service, or
repair of any type of vehicles, boats or boat trailers, engines, appliances or
other electrical equipment, or any other industrial activity shall be
permitted.
   (j)   Accessory uses. Accessory uses such as the rental of trucks, trailers
or moving equipment (hand carts, jacks and lifts, etc.), the installation of
trailer hitches, or the sale of boxes or packing materials are permitted only
if they are otherwise permitted in the district in which the facility is
located, and shall meet all use and development standards of the district.
   (k)   Self-storage facilities shall not operate or allow tenant access
between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.
   (l)   Outdoor storage prohibited. All goods and property stored in a self-
storage facility shall be stored in an enclosed building. No outdoor storage of
boats, RVs, vehicles, etc., or storage in outdoor storage pods or shipping
containers is permitted.
   (m)   If the facility abuts residentially zoned property, the facility
loading bays, docks or doors shall not be visible from the residential
property.
   (n)   Electrical service to storage units shall be for lighting and climate
control only. No electrical outlets are permitted inside individual storage
units. Lighting fixtures and switches shall be of a secure design that will not
allow tapping the fixtures for other purposes.
   (o)   Fences and walls including entry gates shall be constructed of high-
quality materials and shall be compatible with the design and materials of the
building(s) and site, as approved by the Planning Commission. Decorative metal
or wrought iron fences are preferred. Chain-link (or similar) fences, barbed or
razor wire fences, and walls made of precast concrete blocks are prohibited.
(Ord. 186-2020. Passed 1-19-21.)

901.01   CHANGES BY PETITION.
   In order to change the name or number of any existing street or other public
way by petition, a petition containing the signatures of seventy-five percent
of the residents residing upon such street or other public way shall first be
presented to Council.
   All expenses incident to such change shall be chargeable to the petitioners
who executed the petition requesting the change.
(Ord. 172-61. Passed 10-2-61.)
901.02   SOIL ACCUMULATIONS.
   No person shall cause or permit soil or debris to accumulate in any public
street or appurtenant catch basin. When soil or debris is accumulated in any
public street or appurtenant catch basin, the Service Director or his or her
duly authorized agent shall notify the person causing or permitting such
unlawful accumulation that it must be removed within twenty-four hours after
the time of such notice. Upon failure of such person to remove the soil or
debris to the satisfaction of the Service Director, the Service Director shall
cause the accumulation to be removed through the use of appropriate equipment
and manpower, including outside contractors, as he or she deems necessary.
   The full cost of any such removal, including direct overhead and
administrative costs, shall be charged to the person responsible for creating
or permitting such accumulation.
(Ord. 129-89. Passed 4-3-89.)

902.01   DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter, "street", "boulevard", "avenue" and "alley" mean
that land lying between private lot lines and dedicated for public use.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
902.02   PERMIT; FEE; BOND REQUIRED TO COVER BACKFILLING, ETC.
   Before any person other than a duly authorized City officer or employee
makes any opening or tunneling in any street, alley or other public grounds in
the City or removes the surface of any sidewalk or any part thereof, such
person shall file with the Director of Public Service a written or printed
application therefor, setting forth and accurately indicating therein the
location, kind and extent of the proposed opening or removal of sidewalk and
the number, purpose and size of the openings or excavations which are desired
or necessary. If any openings or excavations are for a purpose other than
pursuant to a contract with the City, the applicant shall pay a fee as set out
in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) and shall
deposit with the City a bond sufficient to cover the cost and supervision of
backfilling, repairing, restoring and relaying the pavement or hard surface of
the sidewalk as the case may be, together with the cost of any new material, as
the same shall be estimated by the Director of Public Service, but in no event
less than one thousand dollars ($1,000).
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
902.03   INSURANCE REQUIRED.
   In addition to the bond required by Section
902.02, every applicant shall, as a condition of any permit being issued
pursuant to this chapter, maintain contractor's comprehensive general and
automobile liability insurance, or its equivalent, extended (or by means of a
separate policy) to include liability for damage caused by explosion, collapse,
underground work, independent contractors, products and completed operations,
together with owner's protective liability, with not less than the following
policy limits:
   (a)   The policy or policies of insurance required by this section shall
have a policy limit for bodily injury and property damage of not less than one
million dollars ($1,000,000) for each occurrence.
   (b)   Such policy or policies of insurance shall name the City as an
additional insured for all work performed within the City limits.
   (c)   Such policy or policies of insurance shall contain the following
special provision: The company agrees that ten days prior to cancellation,
material alteration or reduction of the insurance afforded by this policy with
respect to the permit involved, written notice shall be sent by certified mail
to the City of Parma.
   All insurance herein specified shall be with a company authorized to do
business in the State and acceptable to the Director of Public Service.
(Ord. 325-88. Passed 11-9-88.)
902.04   SUPERVISION BY DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC SERVICE; BACKFILL SPECIFICATIONS.
   (a)   All openings made within the street lines or sidewalk removed shall be
subject to the direction and made under the supervision of the Director of
Public Service. All paving, material, flagging, curbing and ballasting shall be
carefully removed and preserved. After the work is done, as contemplated by the
application for the permit heretofore referred to, the trench or opening shall
be refilled in accordance with the directions of the Director and the flagging,
concrete, paving or other paving material shall be properly replaced under the
supervision of the Director but at the applicant's expense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
   (b)   Upon final inspection of the utility work performed, the street
opening backfill shall be made with clean granular material as approved by the
Director. This material shall have a minimum compaction of ninety-five percent
density. If required by the Director, a laboratory report showing the gradation
of the material used shall be submitted for approval. Such backfilling shall
take place immediately after inspection of the utility. Repaving of the area
shall be commenced within forty-eight hours after satisfactory completion of
the backfill and shall proceed without delay so as to finish the work as soon
as possible.
   The permit holder for such street openings shall be held liable for the
maintenance of such openings for a period of one year and shall cause repairs
to such openings as may be necessary.
(Ord. 183-60. Passed 10-3-60.)
   (c)   All public utility work performed within the street right-of-way shall
be subject to the direction and made under the supervision of the Director of
Public Service. Any inspection of the work by the Director or his authorized
agent shall be paid for by the applicant at the prevailing hourly rate for
inspection.
(Ord. 144-71. Passed 7-6-71.)
902.05   BARRICADES AND WARNING LIGHTS.
   All openings, obstructions or places where the sidewalk is removed shall be
carefully guarded, protected or barricaded at all times. During the night
season such sites shall be defined by red or amber colored lights or other
lights approved by the Director of Public Service and such other precautions
shall be taken as are necessary to guard against accidents. In this respect,
the Director may issue any additional orders as he may deem proper. Such orders
shall be complied with implicitly and promptly. At all times the work shall be
done so as to cause the least inconvenience to property owners and the general
public.
902.06   NEWLY LAID PAVEMENT; REOPENINGS.
   No person shall be permitted to break into or open any newly laid pavement
in the City for a period of five years after such pavement has been laid down,
and no permit may be issued for any such opening, except upon proper authority
granted by resolution of Council.
   Nothing contained in this section shall be construed as a prohibition
against an emergency opening of the pavement for the purpose of repairing or
cleaning underground improvements upon the order of the Director of Public
Service.
(Ord. 175-55. Passed 7-18-55.)
902.07   BOND REQUIRED TO COVER SETTLING AND DEFECTS.
   (a)   In the case of any opening or tunneling in any street, alley or other
public ground in the City, and in addition to the bond required under Section
902.02, any firm, partnership, corporation, individual or other person who has
installed, constructed or repaired any pavement and/or opened the streets for
repair is hereby required to post with the City a bond to the satisfaction of
the Director of Public Service, guaranteeing against defects in workmanship or
materials and/or settling. Such bond shall be in a minimum amount equal to or
greater than twenty-five percent of the cost of constructing the pavement
involved, but in no event less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), and shall
run for a period of three years after completion of such installation,
construction, repair and/or street opening.
   (b)   In the case of newly laid pavement, including an original installation
in new subdivisions, any firm, partnership, corporation, individual or other
person who has installed or constructed any pavement is hereby required to post
with the City a bond to the satisfaction of the City Engineer, guaranteeing
against defects in workmanship or materials and/or settling. Such bond shall be
in a minimum amount equal to or greater than twenty-five percent of the cost of
constructing the pavement involved, but in no event less than one thousand
dollars ($1,000), and shall run for a period of three years after acceptance of
the work by the City. In the case of pavement in a new subdivision, such bond
shall be conditioned upon acceptance of the respective plat and streets and the
issuance of building permits therefor by the City.
   (c)   Any bond required under this section shall be issued by a company
authorized to write insurance in this State. Such bond shall warrant that the
principal shall maintain and keep in repair the paving improvement and shall
designate the City as the insured therein, by the terms of which the City is
saved harmless from any and all claims due to settling and/or defects in
workmanship or materials. The monetary values and lengths of time of such bond,
as set forth above, shall be deemed the minimum acceptable requirements and
may, for just cause, be increased or the time extended at the discretion of the
Director of Public Service or the City Engineer, respectively.
(Ord. 209-78. Passed 9-18-78.)
902.08   APPLICATION OF CHAPTER.
   Nothing contained in this chapter shall be deemed applicable to any contract
with the City with respect to street openings.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
902.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)

903.01   SIDEWALKS GENERALLY; WIDTH OF SIDEWALKS.
   (a)   All sidewalks shall be under the direction of the Director of Public
Service. Except as provided in subsection (b) hereof, the space between the
property line and the curb line on each side of the paved roadway or curbed
streets shall constitute the sidewalk. Upon unpaved streets, the sidewalk shall
be the portion adjoining the property line on each side and shall have a width
equal to one-fifth of the distance between property lines, but in no case shall
the sidewalks be less than five feet in width and one foot away from the right-
of-way line, except in streets or alleys of sixteen feet or less in width, in
which case the sidewalk shall be two and one-half feet in width.
   (b)   It is hereby established that the sidewalks on West Ridgewood Drive,
from State Road westerly to Ridge Road, shall be four feet wide. The treelawns
on West Ridgewood Drive, from State Road westerly to Ridge Road, shall be three
feet wide, measured from curbing to sidewalk.
(Ord. 77-59. Passed 4-20-59.)
903.02   CONSTRUCTION, REPAIR, ETC.; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No sidewalk shall be improved or constructed as herein provided, nor shall
any sidewalk be repaired or relaid, unless a permit for so doing has been
obtained from the Director of Public Service. The application for the permit
shall specify the owner of the property in front of which the sidewalk is to be
laid, the sublot and the house numbers, or, where no such numbers have been
established, adequate measurements identifying the location.
   A sidewalk permit must be obtained for each continuous strip of new sidewalk
constructed. This means any continuous strip of any number of lots to be
graded, formed and poured in one continuous operation requiring two inspection
trips as set out in Section
903.03. The purpose of this permit is to control uniform quality of sidewalk
construction in accordance with the City sidewalk standards and specifications.
Services rendered by the City for this permit shall be the keeping of
established street profile plats, sidewalk standards and specifications
available to the owner, contractor or his engineer or surveyor to stake out and
build sidewalks to the established line and grade.
(Ord. 118-57. Passed 6-3-57.)
903.03   INSPECTIONS.
   Before pouring concrete, the owner or contractor shall call the City
Engineer and request his inspection of forms and the approval of the same by
him.
   A final inspection by the City Engineer or the Department of Public Service,
when the work is completed and the premises cleaned, is also required. The fee
for such inspection shall be as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule). In the event
that the City Engineer or the Department of Public Service finds that the work
is not in conformity with City standards and specifications and the street
profile, then the owner or contractor shall be required to replace such
sidewalk as provided in Section
903.08(c).
(Ord. 118-57. Passed 6-3-57.)
903.04   SIDEWALK LINE AND GRADE.
   The owner or contractor shall have an engineer or surveyor stake out all new
sidewalks for line and grade according to the City sidewalk standards and
established street profile, with a layout card, furnished by the City Engineer
or the Department of Public Service, filled in and returned to the City
Engineer before inspection of forms. The owner or contractor may request the
City Engineer to perform this service if they have no engineer or surveyor
retained. Application for this service can be made at the Department of Public
Service. The fee for this service shall be as set out in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule) and shall be
payable in advance upon application for engineering services of sidewalk lines
and grade stakes.
(Ord. 118-57. Passed 6-3-57.)
903.05   SIDEWALK WIDTH, ROUGHING, GRADING.
   (a)   All sidewalks hereafter improved by placing walks with a permanent
surfacing on any public highway or street within the City shall be so improved
by constructing the walks with stone flagging or concrete in accordance with
the specifications prescribed by the Director of Public Service and shall be of
the width prescribed in Section
903.01. The sidewalk shall be so laid that the top surface shall be properly
roughened so that the same shall be prevented from becoming slippery when
covered with moisture and the roughened finish shall be of such character as in
the judgment of the Director will effectually prevent at any time the slippery
condition of such walks.
   (b)   Any grading necessary between the walks, as laid, and the curb line,
or between the walks and the edge of the sidewalk space, as herein established,
shall be done at the time of laying such walks so as to leave the sidewalk
space at the grade hereinafter described.
   (c)   The sidewalks as improved shall coincide with the line described as
follows: beginning at the curb line with the established curb grade as
determined by the Director; thence extending to the street line at right angles
to the curb line, with a rise of three-eighths of an inch to the foot. However,
at street intersections where the grade of the intersecting street prevents
compliance with the above provisions, the walk shall be laid under the
direction and to the acceptance of the Director.
(Ord. 71-52. Passed 6-2-52.)
   (d)   All sidewalks in commercial and retail rights-of-way which are under
going new construction or exterior alterations shall hereafter be improved so
as to conform to the specifications set forth in Exhibit A following the text
of this chapter. The material specifications shall conform to all requirements
of the Building Code and as determined by the Building Commissioner.
(Ord. 263-94. Passed 2-20-96; Ord. 401-96. Passed 1-21-97.)
903.06   CONSTRUCTION OR REPAIRS DIRECTED BY COUNCIL; NOTICE.
   Council may, by resolution, declare that certain specified sidewalks,
curbings or gutters shall be constructed or repaired. Upon the passage of such
resolution the Clerk of Council shall cause written notice of the passage
thereof to be served upon the owner or his agent, if a resident of the City,
for each parcel of land abutting upon such sidewalks, curbings or gutters, in
the manner provided by law for the service of summons in civil actions. A copy
of the notice, with the time and manner of service endorsed thereon, signed by
the person serving it, shall be returned to the office of the Clerk of Council
and there filed and preserved. For the purpose of such service, if the owner of
any such property is not a resident of the City, any person charged with the
collection of rent or the payment of taxes upon such property or having control
thereof in any way, shall be regarded as the agent of the owner, and service
upon such person shall have like force and effect as though personal service
was made on the owner thereof. If it appears in any such return that the owner
is a nonresident and that neither such owner or agent could be found, once
publication of a copy of the resolution in a newspaper of general circulation
in the City shall be deemed sufficient notice to such owner.
(Ord. 71-52. Passed 6-2-52; Ord. 87-59. Passed 5-11-59.)
903.07   CITY'S REMEDY IN EVENT OF NONCOMPLIANCE.
   If sidewalks, curbings or gutters are not constructed or repaired within
thirty days from the service of the notice provided for in Section
903.06, or the completion of the publication thereof, the City may proceed
through the appropriate department or office, either by direct employment of
labor or by contract, to carry out the construction or repair at the expense of
the owner. As in the case of other improvements, all such expenses shall be
reported by the Auditor to Council. Council shall thereupon, by ordinance,
assess the cost and expense thereof upon the owner or owners of all property
bounding or abutting upon such sidewalks, curbings or gutters and such
assessment shall be collected in the same manner as are other assessments, with
a penalty of five percent and interest for failure to pay at the time fixed by
the assessment ordinance.
(Ord. 71-52. Passed 6-2-52.)
903.08   SUPERVISION BY DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC SERVICE; CITY'S REMEDY FOR
IMPROPERLY LAID SIDEWALKS.
   (a)   Any sidewalk heretofore laid shall not be raised or lowered without
the approval of the Director of Public Service and all sidewalks hereinafter
laid shall be in accordance with the provisions of this chapter and under the
supervision of the Director.
   (b)   No curb line or curb grade shall be changed, except by the direction
and with the written consent of the Director.
   (c)   Any sidewalk laid on any public street or highway within the City in a
manner inconsistent with the provisions of this chapter shall, upon the order
of the Director, be relaid to the proper grade, and, upon failure of the
property owner to make the change or relay such sidewalk as so ordered within
the time specified in the notice, the City may relay the sidewalk, and the cost
thereof, together with interest and a penalty of five percent, will be taxed or
assessed against the property in the manner provided by law.
(Ord. 71-52. Passed 6-2-52.)
903.09   SIDEWALK CONTRACTORS; PERFORMANCE BOND AND INSURANCE REQUIRED.
   Each person engaged in the business of laying or repairing sidewalks in the
City shall furnish to the Director of Public Service a faithful performance
bond in the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000). In addition to the bond
required by this section, every applicant shall, as a condition of any permit
being issued pursuant to Section 903.02, maintain contractor's comprehensive
general and automobile liability insurance, or its equivalent, extended (or by
means of a separate policy) to include liability for damage caused by
explosion, collapse, underground work, independent contractors, products and
completed operations, together with owner's protective liability, with not less
than the following policy limits:
   (a)   The policy or policies of insurance required by this section shall
have a policy limit for bodily injury and property damage of not less than
three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) for each occurrence.
   (b)   Such policy or policies of insurance shall name the City as an
additional insured for all work performed within the City limits.
   (c)   Such policy or policies of insurance shall contain the following
special provision: The company agrees that ten days prior to cancellation,
material alteration or reduction of the insurance afforded by this policy with
respect to the permit involved, written notice shall be sent by certified mail
to the City of Parma.
   All insurance herein specified shall be with a company authorized to do
business in the State and acceptable to the Director of Public Service.
(Ord. 328-88. Passed 11-9-88.)
903.10   SIDEWALKS REQUIRED IN CONSTRUCTION OF BUILDINGS; CITY'S REMEDY FOR
NONCOMPLIANCE.
   (a)   Any person signing the application for a permit to build a building or
structure of any nature on any lot or land in the City is hereby required to
place sidewalks on such lot or land as directed by the proper authority of the
City, and the Building Commissioner is hereby directed to refuse final approval
of any building or structure until such sidewalks have been installed to the
satisfaction of the Building Commissioner.
   (b)   Upon failure to install sidewalks after thirty days notice has been
given, the Director of Public Service shall cause the sidewalks to be installed
and the cost thereof assessed against such property by Council certifying the
same to the County Auditor for placement for collection on the regular tax
duplicate.
(Ord. 83-56. Passed 5-7-56.)
   (c)   (1)   Notwithstanding subsections (a) and (b) hereof, any applicant
may request in writing that the Director of Public Service waive the
requirements of this section in whole or in part. Upon receipt of such an
application, copies shall be forwarded to the City Engineer and the pertinent
Ward Councilman for their comments. Following his investigation, the Director
shall approve the request, in whole or in part, if he finds that doing so will
not be materially detrimental to the public welfare and that one or more of the
following conditions exist:
         A.   The building site is located on a street that has no sidewalks
and for which construction of sidewalks is not anticipated in the reasonably
foreseeable future.
         B.   The building site is located on a side of the street that has no
sidewalks within 500 feet of the site and for which construction of sidewalks
is not anticipated in the reasonably foreseeable future.
         C.   The building site is located on a street where there are
sidewalks, but the building site is the last lot on the street and is otherwise
so situated within the neighborhood that the general public would not
reasonably be expected to pass the building site on the way to some nearby
location, provided, however, that in such case sidewalks shall still be
required of a length reasonably necessary to service occupants of the building,
         D.   The building site is located on a street where there are
sidewalks, but exceptional circumstances of terrain, geology or location of the
site would render installation of such sidewalks unnecessary to the general
public and would cause undue hardship to the applicant.
   In approving the request, the Director shall state, in writing, the
conditions justifying the waiver and, if the waiver is only a partial waiver,
shall clearly identify the area where sidewalks will still be required.
      (2)   Whenever a request is denied or modified by the Director, the
applicant may, within ten days of receipt of the Director's decision, file a
written appeal with the Clerk of Council. Council shall act within thirty days
to approve, reverse or modify the action of the Director.
      (3)   A full waiver granted under this subsection (c) shall include the
right to waive or rescind any permit fee or bond which would otherwise be
required but is no longer necessary.
      (4)   Any waiver granted under this subsection (c) shall, under no
circumstances, constitute a waiver, abrogation or estoppel of the City's right
to require sidewalk installation at come future date under changed
circumstances.
      (5)   This subsection (c) shall be deemed operative and applicable to
construction or building applications pending on the effective date of this
subsection (c).
(Ord. 46-83. Passed 4-4-83.)
903.11   INSPECTIONS AND SURVEYS; SIDEWALK/ZONING INSPECTOR.
   (a)   The Director of Public Safety is hereby authorized and directed to
conduct a systematic inspection and survey of all existing sidewalks in the
City and of all developed property in the City where sidewalks are not
currently in place. The purpose of such survey is to compile a current listing
of the location and length of all places in the City where existing sidewalks
need repair and where, in already developed neighborhoods, sidewalks are not in
place.
   (b)   In order to assist him or her in conducting such inspection and
survey, the Director is hereby authorized and directed to employ, as a full-
time employee, a Sidewalk/Zoning Inspector. The salary for the Sidewalk/Zoning
Inspector shall be the prevailing inspector rate and shall be paid from the
City Income Tax Capital Improvement Account Fund No. 4705. The Sidewalk/Zoning
Inspector shall notify the Clerk of Council monthly of the violations he or she
has discovered, and the Clerk shall proceed according to law to remedy such
violations.
(Ord. 11-88. Passed 2-16-88.)
903.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter shall be fined not
more than five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than six
months, or both. Each day's continued violation shall constitute a separate
offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)

905.01   OPENINGS, CUTTINGS; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   Only registered contractors with the City shall make openings in or cut or
remove any curb or curbing in any street, boulevard, avenue or public
thoroughfare in the City. A permit therefor shall be obtained from the Director
of Public Service. The fee and deposit for such permit are listed in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule). The deposit
shall be refunded by the Director if the work is completed to his or her
satisfaction and without damage to the pavement, remaining curb or treelawn.
(Ord. 99-90. Passed 4-16-90; Ord. 357-95. Passed 9-15-97.)
905.02   APPLICATION; INFORMATION REQUIRED.
   Any person desiring a cut or opening in the curb of any street, boulevard,
avenue or public thoroughfare in the City shall file with the Director of
Public Service a written or printed application setting forth and indicating
therein the location, kind and extent of the curb desired to be opened or cut
and the purpose and size of the opening or cut which is desired or deemed
necessary.
(Ord. 47-50. Passed 6-19-50.)
905.03   COSTS FOR CURB CUTTING BY CITY. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section 905.03 was repealed by Ordinance 357-95, passed
September 15, 1997.)
905.04   DRIVEWAY REGULATIONS FOR GAS STATIONS AND BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS.
   Driveways for gasoline stations or other business establishments shall be
limited to thirty-five feet in width at the throat and no cuts, openings or
lowerings shall be permitted in any corner where the radius of the corner would
be affected.
(Ord. 14-62. Passed 2-5-62.)
905.05   CONTRACT POWERS.
   The Director of Public Service is hereby authorized to enter into any
contract which he may deem necessary for the opening, cutting or lowering of
any curb, with any firm, person or corporation lawfully entitled to enter into
a legal contract with the City, provided the total amount to be expended by
virtue of such contract is not in excess of five hundred dollars ($500.00) and
provided further that the contract shall not provide for a higher wage than the
prevailing wage for similar services in this community.
(Ord. 47-50. Passed 6-19-50.)
905.06   PAINTING STREET ADDRESSES.
   (a)   No person shall engage in the enterprise of painting street addresses
on City street curbs for pay or profit, or with the intention of soliciting
voluntary contributions therefor, unless he or she has first obtained a permit
to do so from the Director of Public Service.
    (b)   An individual desiring a permit for curb painting shall submit an
application therefor to the Director, on a form prescribed by the Director, at
least three business days prior to the date he or she intends to commence
painting. Such form shall include the following information:
      (1)   The name of the applicant;
      (2)   The permanent residence of the applicant;
      (3)   The current residence if different from the permanent address of
the applicant;
       (4)   The name and address of any current employer of the applicant; and
      (5)   A listing of the specific streets where the individual intends to
paint curbs.
   A permit fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) shall be paid upon issuance of
the permit.
   (c)   An applicant under this section shall, at the time of filing, also
post with the Director a cash bond in the amount of five hundred dollars
($500.00) as a guarantee that the applicant will:
       (1)   Paint street addresses with accuracy;
       (2)   Paint street addresses without damaging public or private
property;
       (3)   Paint only street addresses along City curbs; and
      (4)   Refrain from painting a street address at any location where asked
to do so by the resident before the painting has been done. Upon failure to
comply with any of these requirements, the Director may correct the failure and
charge the City's costs of doing so against the cash bond. The charging of
costs against the bond shall not prevent the City from exercising any other
legal recourse to recover costs which exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00).
    (d)   The Director shall issue the permit within three business days of the
filing of the application and cash bond. Such permit shall remain in effect for
the balance of the current calendar year but may be revoked by the Director for
a violation of any of the criteria listed in subsection (c) hereof.
   (e)   On December 31 of each year or at the request of the applicant,
whichever is earlier, a permit granted hereunder shall be terminated. Thirty
days after the date of termination, an applicant may apply to the City for
release of his or her cash bond.
   (f)   The application of house numbers on curbs is strictly voluntary by the
painter. A homeowner is not required to pay for this numbering but may make a
voluntary contribution if he or she so desires.
   (g)   The applicant shall provide all residents to be serviced by the
painting of street addresses with the following information: permit number and
applicant's name, address, phone number, and e-mail address (if available).
(Ord. 199-86. Passed 10-20-86; Ord. 92-93. Passed 5-10-93; Ord. 275-98. Passed
12-21-98; Ord. 213-04. Passed 8-16-04.)
905.99   PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the third degree and shall be fined not more than five hundred
dollars ($500.00) or imprisoned not more than sixty days, or both. Each day's
continued violation shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57; Ord. 275-98. Passed 12-21-98.)

CHAPTER 911
Trees
