1501.01   DIVISION OF BUILDINGS; ESTABLISHMENT.
   There is hereby created and established as part of the Department of Public
Safety the Division of Buildings.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.011   STANDARDS.
   (a)   Ohio Building Code. The Ohio Building Code, for which the designation
"OBC" may be substituted, set forth in Chapters 4101:1-1 to 4101:1-35 of the
Ohio Administrative Code, together with all amendments thereto promulgated by
the Ohio Board of Building Standards, is hereby adopted and incorporated fully
as if the OBC were written herein in its entirety. The provisions of the OBC
shall operate as the minimum requirements for every building and structure, and
any appurtenance connected or attached thereto which is governed under the OBC
and is proposed for use in the City of Parma.
   (b)   Residential Code of Ohio. The Residential Code of Ohio, for which the
designation "RCO" may be substituted, set forth in Chapters 4101:8-01 to 4101:
8-25, 4101:8-29, 4101:8-34, and 4101:8-44 of the Ohio Administrative Code,
together with all amendments thereto promulgated by the Ohio Board of Building
Standards, is hereby adopted and incorporated fully as if the RCO were written
herein in its entirety. The provisions of the RCO shall apply to every one-,
two-, and three-family dwelling, any appurtenance connected or attached to such
building or structure, and any accessory structure which is governed under the
RCO and is proposed for use in the City of Parma.
   (c)   Ohio Mechanical Code. The Ohio Mechanical Code, for which the
designation "OMC" may be substituted, set forth in Chapters 4101:2-1 to 4101:2-
15 of the Ohio Administrative Code, together with all amendments thereto
promulgated by the Ohio Board of Building Standards, is hereby adopted and
incorporated fully as if the OMC were written herein in its entirety. The
provisions of the OMC shall apply to the design, installation, maintenance,
alteration, repair, relocation, replacement, addition to, use and inspection of
mechanical systems within buildings that are proposed for use in the City of
Parma. The OMC shall also apply to such other systems, system components,
equipment and appliances as specifically addressed in the OMC.
   (d)   In addition to the requirements and standards of the OBC, the RCO, and
the OMC, the construction, alteration, removal, demolition, equipment, use and
occupancy, location, and maintenance of buildings and structures in the City of
Parma shall conform to the provisions of this Building Code. In the event the
provisions of this Building Code are in conflict with the provisions of the
OBC, the RCO, or the OMC, the provisions of the OBC, RCO, and OMC shall apply.
   (e)   A complete copy of the OBC, the RCO, the OMC, and this Building Code
are on file with the Clerk of the Parma City Council for public inspection and
distribution at cost. Copies of said codes are also on file in the Cuyahoga
County Law Library located in the Cuyahoga County Court House, City of
Cleveland, Ohio.
(Ord. 113-17. Passed 7-10-17.)
1501.02   COMPOSITION.
   The Division of Buildings shall be composed as provided in Section
147.01.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.03   COMPENSATION.
   The salaries to be paid to the Building Commissioner and the various
officers and employees in the Division of Buildings shall be as provided by
Council.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.04   BONDS.
   The Building Commissioner shall notify the City Purchasing Agent of any
change or addition to his personnel, and before such person shall enter into
his duties, the Commissioner shall determine that the new employee is covered
by the general blanket bond of the City for its employees.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
1501.05   DUTIES OF BUILDING COMMISSIONER.
   The Building Commissioner shall be the head of the Division of Buildings and
shall:
   (a)   Have the management and control of everything pertaining thereto;
   (b)   Be charged with the inspection of buildings and with the enforcement
of this Building Code and all other laws and ordinances, now or hereafter
passed, relating to the erection, construction, alteration, additions to,
repairs of, inspection, razing, moving and safety of buildings, structures,
heating and ventilating apparatus, gas fitting, house drainage and plumbing,
electric wiring and fire protection deuces;
   (c)   Pass upon all questions relating to the strength and durability of
buildings, structures and building materials;
   (d)   Examine and approve all drawings and specifications for building
construction, before a permit is issued, or cause the same to be done;
   (e)   Sign and issue all permits, notices or other papers required to be
issued, or cause the same to be done, and promptly acknowledge the receipt of
all official communications, notices and reports;
   (f)   Give such of his time to the performance of the duties of his office
as may be required and during his term of office he shall not be employed or
engaged, directly or indirectly, in any building business or enter any contract
for building for others or for furnishing materials, plans or specifications
for others;
   (g)   Examine or cause to be examined all buildings in the course of
erection, alteration, repair, razing or removal, within the City, as often as
is required to insure sufficient supervision, and shall make written reports of
all violations of any law or ordinance which he is required to enforce,
together with the street and number where such violations are found, the name
of the person responsible therefor and all other necessary information relating
thereto;
   (h)   Have a daily report of all the work of the Division of Buildings,
which report shall be entered in books or on cards and filed in the office of
the Division of Buildings;
   (i)   Have charge of and be responsible for the property and records of the
Division of Buildings;
   (j)   Interpret and apply this Building Code to the various building
conditions arising in the City;
   (k)   Prepare or assist in preparing all revisions of this Building Code.
   (l)   The Building Commissioner may cause the prosecution of any person
violating any of the building regulations of the City. Violation of any of the
provisions of this code, unless otherwise noted, shall be a strict liability
offense.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30; Ord. 185-10. Passed 7-26-10.)
1501.06   RIGHT OF ENTRY.
   The Building Commissioner and the officers and employees of the Division of
Buildings shall, at any reasonable hour, so far as may be necessary for the
performance of their duties and upon showing their badge of office, have the
right to enter in or upon any building site or premises, any new or unoccupied
building, any building under construction, repair, alteration or removal or any
building alleged to be unsafe or a menace to life and limb or damaged or
menaced by fire. No person shall interfere with such personnel when engaged in
the performance of such duties.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.07   INSPECTION OF EXISTING BUILDINGS.
   The Building Commissioner shall have authority to inspect or cause to be
inspected any building or structure in the City for the purpose of determining
the safety thereof and the sufficiency of the means of egress therefrom in the
event of fire, panic or other accidents.
   In the event of refusal of entrance, then, upon reasonable grounds, a search
warrant may be obtained from a court of competent jurisdiction to make such
inspection.
1501.08   FLUSHING OF SEWERS BEFORE FINAL INSPECTION.
   Before final inspection is made, the builder shall, in the presence of a
building inspector, auger and flush all sewers, storm and sanitary.
(Ord. 32-57. Passed 2-18-57.)
1501.09   FINAL INSPECTION OF NEW BUIlDINGS BEFORE OCCUPANCY. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section 1510.09 was repaled by Ordinance 278-99, passed
November 3, 1999.)
1501.10   OCCUPANCY PERMITS FOR ONE, TWO AND THREE-FAMILY DWELLINGS.
   (a)   No builder, owner or other person having control of property under
construction for new dwelling units shall allow such property to be occupied
until the same has been finally inspected and approved by the Building
Commissioner, and until any necessary occupancy permits have been obtained.
   (b)   This section shall also apply to the reconstruction of a one, two or
three-family dwelling which has been rendered uninhabitable as determined by
the Building Commissioner. No person having control of such property shall
allow such property to be occupied until the same has been repaired, finally
inspected and approved by the Building Commissioner, and until any necessary
occupancy permits have been obtained.
   (c)   This section shall also apply to additions to a one, two or three-
family dwelling. No person having control of such property shall allow the
addition to be occupied until the same has been finally inspected and approved
by the Building Commissioner, and until any necessary occupancy permits have
been obtained.
   (d)   Alterations to an occupied dwelling are permitted, but the Building
Commissioner shall determine whether or not the alterations are so extensive as
to be subject to issuance of a new occupancy permit upon completion of the
alterations.
   (e)   Attached to an occupancy permit shall be the City's approved grading
plan for the lot in question, together with a statement of the City Engineer
that such lot has been graded in accordance with such approved grading plan
and, further, that such grading plan for such lot shall be maintained by the
occupant of such property under the penalty provided in Section
1501.99.
   (f)   An occupancy permit is not required for a detached garage or other
building accessory to a one, two or three-family dwelling.
(Ord. 278-99. Passed 11-3-99.)
1501.105   TEMPORARY OCCUPANCY PERMITS FOR ONE, TWO AND THREE-FAMILY DWELLINGS;
GRADING; BONDS.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner may issue a partial occupancy permit in
order to allow the occupancy of a portion of the structure prior to the
completion of work in the remainder of the structure or due to uncertain
weather factors during certain times of the year which prevent proper grading
of lots and other exterior work from being completed.
   (b)   When, because of uncertain weather factors during certain times of the
year, property grading of lots and other exterior work cannot be completed, a
cash bond shall, in lieu of the required grading and other completion, be
deposited with the Building Commissioner by the contractor, builder or
developer so requesting an occupancy permit. Such bond shall be in the amount
of five hundred dollars ($500.00) or ten dollars ($10.00) for each front foot,
whichever is greater, for a single or two-family dwelling, and in the amount of
one thousand dollars ($1,000) or twenty dollars ($20.00) for each front foot,
whichever is greater, for any other building, and shall be posted prior to
occupancy.
   (c)   A temporary occupancy permit for a one, two and three-family dwelling
may be issued upon payment of the fee prescribed in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code to permit occupancy of such dwelling or
unit until all required work is completed for an occupancy permit.
   (d)   In addition to the cash bond for grading or partial occupancy, an
affidavit of the contractor, owner or tenant to guarantee proper completion,
including compliance with the approved grading and/or building plans, shall be
deposited with the Building Commissioner.
   (e)   Whenever a cash bond and affidavit are deposited with the City in lieu
of grade completion prior to occupancy, such grading shall be completed in
accordance with the approved grading plan no later than fifteen calendar days
from the date of the written notice from the Commissioner directing the
completion of the grading in accordance with the grading plan. Upon failure to
comply with the notice from the Commissioner, the City shall complete the work
and cause the lot to be graded and shall pay, from the cash bond posted, all
costs incurred. Any balance remaining from the bond posted shall be returned to
the person who posted the bond. Any costs exceeding the amount of the bond
shall be chargeable to the person who posted the bond.
   (f)   It is further required that the owner of any dwelling or building
designed for occupancy shall, upon having such dwelling or building enclosed,
post conspicuously at the entranceway or within the nearest window, a sign of
notification that an occupancy permit must first be obtained from the
Commissioner prior to occupying the dwelling or building.
(Ord. 278-99. Passed 11-3-99.)
1501.106   OCCUPANCY PERMITS FOR COMMERCIAL AND OTHER STRUCTURES.
   (a)   This section shall apply to all buildings other than one, two or
three-family dwellings and their accessory structures.
   (b)   No builder, owner or other person having control of property under
construction or a proposed change in use group shall allow such property to be
occupied until the same has been inspected and approved according to the
requirements of the Ohio Basic Building Code, and a certificate of use and
occupancy has been obtained. This is in addition to any certificate of
compliance required by the Zoning Code.
   (c)   The Building Commissioner may issue a stop work order or stop use
order for any work not in accordance with this Building Code. This Building
Code includes the Ohio Basic Building Code, by reference, and also includes
administrative requirements for contractor registration, permits and, by
reference, zoning compliance requirements.
(Ord. 278-99. Passed 11-3-99.)
1501.107   TEMPORARY OCCUPANCY PERMITS FOR COMMERCIAL AND OTHER STRUCTURES.
   (a)   A temporary occupancy permit for any building or tenant space
requiring an occupancy permit may be issued upon payment of the fee prescribed
in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code to permit occupancy of such building or
tenant space until all required work is completed for an occupancy permit.
   (b)   A partial occupancy permit for any other building or tenant space may
be issued upon payment of the fee prescribed in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code to permit the partial occupancy of such
building or tenant space during construction in the remainder of the building
or tenant space.
   (c)   The Building Commissioner may require a floor plan showing the limits
of the area of such partial occupancy and may require barricades, temporary
walls or other protection between the partial occupancy space and the
construction area.
   (d)   A partial occupancy permit does not include permission for
merchandise, occupant employees, customers or residents in any construction
area beyond the limits designated by the Building Commissioner for partial
occupancy, and the limitations of the partial occupancy permit shall remain in
effect until final inspection and approval by the Building Commissioner of the
alterations or construction.
(Ord. 278-99. Passed 11-3-99.)
1501.11   REPORT OF VIOLATIONS.
   When any person represents to the Building Commissioner that a condition or
thing exists which is in violation of the laws or ordinances, with the
enforcement of which he is charged, it shall be his duty to examine forthwith
such condition or thing or cause it to be examined, and if such violation is
found to exist, the Commissioner shall immediately order the owner, lessee,
tenant or other person in charge thereof or responsible therefor to comply with
the laws and ordinances of the City which regulate the same. It shall be deemed
sufficient notice if sent by mail to the last known address or to the address
given in the application for a building permit or in the notice of complaint.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.12   BOARD OF EXAMINERS FOR TESTING MATERIALS.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner shall have the power to appoint a Board of
Examiners consisting of three members, each of whom shall have at least ten
years' experience as an engineer or architect, for the purpose of examining any
new material or construction which is proposed for use in the construction of
buildings. The test of such material shall be as provided in this Building
Code, or as ordered by the Commissioner.
   (b)   The Board of Examiners shall be employed, and all such tests shall be
made, at the expense of the person asking the acceptance of the material or
construction, and a detailed statement, in writing, of the methods and results
of the tests shall be submitted to the Commissioner to aid him in forming an
opinion as to the fitness of the material or construction for the proposed use.
   (c)   Such reports shall become the property of the Division of Buildings.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.13   RECORDS OF THE DIVISION OF BUILDINGS.
   The Building Commissioner shall keep or cause to be kept a book or card
filing system, in which shall be recorded the location and character of every
building, structure or other work for which a permit is issued, and a copy of
every report of inspection of the building, structure or work, so arranged that
the full history of the various inspections of each building, structure or
other work appears therein in consecutive order, with the names of the
inspectors making the inspection and the date thereof. Originals of all notes
and reports made by the inspectors in the pursuance of their duty shall be
signed and filed in the Division of Buildings for permanent record.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.14   MONTHLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner shall make a monthly report to the Mayor on
or before the fifteenth day of each month, covering the building operations of
the City and the work of the Division of Buildings during the preceding month.
   (b)   The Commissioner shall make an annual report to the Mayor which shall
contain complete statistics of the building operations during the fiscal year,
the work and cost of the Division of Buildings and such recommendations as his
experience indicates should be made.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.15   PERMITS REQUIRED; SURCHARGES.
   (a)   Before the erection, construction, installation, enlargement,
alteration, repair or removal of any wall or of any building, structure,
heating and ventilating apparatus, gas fitting, electrical work, house
drainage, plumbing or any part thereof, in the City, a permit therefor shall
first be obtained by the owner or his or her agent or the architect from the
Building Commissioner. No person shall commence or continue any such work
unless a permit has first been obtained. Notwithstanding Section
1501.99, if any of the aforementioned construction shall be commenced without
the taking out of all the necessary permits, a penalty in the amount of one
hundred dollars ($100.00) for the first offense, three hundred dollars
($300.00) for the second offense, and five hundred dollars ($500.00) for the
third offense shall be paid and should be assessed as part of the permit fee,
and all work shall be stopped until such time as such fee or fees have been
paid and permits secured, all to the satisfaction of the Commissioner. Owner
occupied one- family structures are eligible for a one-time (first offense)
waiver of the one hundred dollar ($100.00) late fee for a homeowner permit.
   (b)   Prior to the commencement of work, the permit must be posted on the
front of the structure or an adequately observable location from the street and
shall continue to be posted throughout the duration of the construction and for
five days after final inspection.
(Ord. 242-95. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 224-06. Passed 8-7-06.)
1501.16   SEPARATE PERMITS REQUIRED.
   (a)   Separate permits shall be required for the installation of tanks for
the storage of oil or any other flammable liquids or materials or explosives.
   (b)   Separate permits shall be required for the installation of all
plumbing and electrical facilities and fixtures.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.165   PERMITS: INSTALLATION OF SWIMMING POOLS.
   (a)   No person or contractor shall install a swimming pool under overhead
electrical wires.
   (b)   Every pool installer or person who has been contacted to or has
undertaken to install a swimming pool shall notify in writing a prospective
pool purchaser of any dangers related to electrical wires located above the
proposed location for the swimming pool and of the prohibition against
installing a swimming pool under overhead electrical wires.
   (c)   After written notice has been given to a prospective pool purchaser,
every pool installer or person who has been contacted to contract or undertake
to install a swimming pool shall obtain a permit from the Building Department
for the installation of the swimming pool, verifying that the swimming pool
shall not be installed in violation of this provision and that written notice
required in subsection (b) of this section has been provided.
   (d)   Notwithstanding Section
1501.99, if pool installation shall be commenced without the taking out of the
necessary permit, pursuant to Section
185.04, a penalty in the amount of five hundred dollars ($500.00) shall be
paid, and all work stopped until such time as such fee or fees have been paid
and permits secured, to the satisfaction of the Commissioner.
(Ord. 128-01. Passed 10-1-01.)
1501.17   PERMIT TO MOVE, RAISE OR ENLARGE A BUILDING.
   (a)   When application is made for a permit to move, raise, enlarge or build
upon any building or structure, the Building Commissioner shall examine the
building or structure, or cause the same to be examined, and make a record of
its condition.
   (b)   No permit to increase the height of any building shall be issued
unless the owner of the building furnishes to the Commissioner satisfactory
proof of the adequate thickness of the walls or strength of the skeleton frame
and of the adequate strength of the foundation thereof.
   (c)   No permit for raising or moving any building more than one story high,
nor for moving any building through any street, shall be issued to anyone not a
licensed house mover.
   (d)   No building being moved shall block or occupy public property for a
period longer than three days.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.18   WORK FOR WHICH PERMITS ARE NOT REQUIRED.
   (a)   Permits shall not be required for minor interior or exterior repairs
where there is no interference with the construction of the building.
   (b)   Permits are not required for repairs or partitioning off in buildings
which do not involve any change in the supporting walls, members, structural
parts, stairways, elevators, escalators, electrical work, plumbing work,
heating or air conditioning equipment, ventilation or occupancy of the
building.
(Ord. 259-94. Passed 11-9-94.)
1501.19   TIME LIMITATIONS ON PERMITS.
   (a)   If, after a permit is issued for work pursuant to Section
1501.15, the work is not completed within one year after the date of issuance
of the permit, or if the work is discontinued for any reason for a period of
three months, the permit shall become void and, before such operation can begin
again or work be resumed, the owner or his or her agent or architect must apply
to renew the permit. The permit shall only be extended for an additional six
months from the date of its reissuance.
   (b)   Fees for the renewal of such permits shall be assessed as original
permits pursuant to Section
185.04 of these Codified Ordinances. Notwithstanding Section
1501.99, if any of the aforementioned work is commenced without the renewal of
the necessary permit or permits, a penalty in the amount of five hundred
dollars ($500.00) shall be paid, and all work shall be stopped until such time
as such fee has been paid and a permit or permits secured, all to the
satisfaction of the Building Commissioner.
(Ord. 16-54. Passed 2-2-54; Ord. 266-96. Passed 10-7-96.)
1501.20   APPLICATION FOR PERMITS.
   (a)   Application for all permits shall be made in writing to the Building
Commissioner upon blank forms furnished by the Division of Buildings. The
applications shall be accompanied by the drawings and specifications required
by this Building Code.
   (b)   The application shall include the estimated cost of such building or
structure, the location and proposed use thereof, a description of the land,
giving the allotment, the number of the sublot, the name of the street or
streets on which it abuts and the name of the owner of the building, structure
or premises, together with such other information as the Commissioner may
require.
   (c)   The application shall be kept permanently on file in the office of the
Division of Buildings and the drawings and specifications shall be retained
until the completion of the work, when they may be returned.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
   (d)   The applications, drawings and specifications shall be dated upon
receipt in the office of the Division of Buildings and passed on in the order
in which they are received, and no applications, drawings or specifications
shall be passed on out of order, unless the buildings or structures are of so
complex a character that they require prolonged examination and investigation.
The applications, drawings and specifications shall not be passed upon, and no
permit for the construction of a building or for the remodeling of a building
so as to change its use or occupancy or for the removal of a building to land
situated in the City, shall be issued until ten days have elapsed after:
       (1)   The filing of the applications, drawings and specifications, which
shall be open for public inspections during business hours during the ten-day
period;
      (2)   There has been posted conspicuously, in the form and manner
directed by the Commissioner, by the applicant on the premises where the work
is to be done or to which the building is to be moved, a notice of the filing
of the applications, drawings and specifications, and
      (3)   In cases where a plumbing permit will be required, until an
application for the plumbing permit is properly filed.
(Ord. 344-46. Passed 4-1-46.)
   (e)   In case the applicant for a permit fails to give a correct statement
of the cost of the work for which a permit is requested, the Commissioner shall
change the estimate to that of the true cost, in accordance with his best
knowledge and belief.
   (f)   When an application is filed for the erection of a new building and
such erection involves the demolition of an existing building or part thereof,
the fact of such demolition shall be stated in the application.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
   (g)   When an application is filed for the razing of a structure within the
City, the Building Department shall forward a copy of the application to the
respective Councilperson of the Ward in which the structure is located.
(Ord. 334-02. Passed 9-3-02.)
1501.21   SITUATION PLAT; CONTENTS.
   Applicants for a building permit shall also file with the Building
Commissioner, for permanent record, a plat of the lot or site upon which it is
proposed to erect the building or structure. The plat shall show the location
and dimensions of the lot, the subdivision and lot number thereof, the width of
the streets, alleys or courtways upon which the lot or site abuts, the
sidewalks and curb lines thereof, the location of any building or structure
thereon or proposed buildings to be erected, and the correct location of all
buildings and their extreme projection on the adjoining lot or lots within
sixteen feet of the lot lines. The plat shall show the plan of the first story
in heavy lines and shall show all projections in their extremes in broken
lines. The plat shall give the figured dimensions of the body of the building,
its extreme projections and the distance thereof from or to the adjoining
street or lot lines and the nearest building or structure. The plat shall also
show the proposed yard elevations at the sidewalk line, front building line and
rear lot line and shall indicate the proposed height above or below the
established sidewalk grade. All such plats shall be enclosed in a single heavy
line, leaving a one-inch border or margin on all sides, oriented and lettered
with the north point of the compass at the top of the sheet. They shall be
drawn to such scale as the Commissioner shall direct.
(Ord. 43-49. Passed 7-18-49.)
1501.22   SITUATION PLAT; WHEN REQUIRED.
   When application is made for a permit for the erection of any building,
structure, addition or alteration, the cost of which does not exceed one
thousand dollars ($1,000), if the application is accompanied by a proper
specification and quarter scale floor plans and cross-sections showing the
general construction of the building structure, then the situation plat is the
only inked or indelibly rendered drawing that shall be required.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.23   SURVEY PLAT.
   Each application for a building permit for buildings to be erected along
street lines and within less than eighteen inches of the same shall be
accompanied by a plat of the survey of the lot showing the figured length of
all lot lines. This plat shall be checked and certified as correct by the City
Engineer, who, when he deems it necessary, shall establish the street lines
upon the ground.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.24   DRAWING REQUIREMENTS.
   All drawings required by this Building Code to be filed with the Building
Commissioner shall be drawn on paper or cloth, in ink or reproduced by some
process that will not fade or obliterate, to a scale of not less than one-
eighth inch to the foot. All distances, heights, dimensions, material and
thickness of walls, sizes and material of all supporting members and structural
parts and sizes of all openings shall be given and accurately figured and the
drawings made accurate and complete. The entire sewerage, drain, soil and waste
pipes, location of all plumbing fixtures, furnaces, boilers and other heating
apparatus, hot air and steam or hot water heating pipes, electric wiring and
gas and electric lighting outlets in the building shall be shown on the
drawings. The location of the building and the names and addresses of the owner
and the architect, author or maker of the drawings shall be indelibly inscribed
thereon.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.25   DRAWINGS REQUIRED.
   The drawings required to be submitted shall be duplicate sets of the general
architect's drawings, consisting of a foundation and footing plan, basement or
cellar plan, the plans of the upper floors and roof, a transverse and a
longitudinal section, at least two elevations and the necessary framing plans
to show the complete framing of the building or structure. The dimensions of
all structural members shall be given on the $rawings.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.26   DETAIL DRAWINGS.
   Should the Building Commissioner find that the drawings required under
Section
1501.25 do not definitely or clearly show the framing of the structural parts
of the building or structure, he may require that a three-quarter inch scale
detail be submitted for such parts or any complex structural part or joint. All
three-quarter inch scale details as prescribed in this section shall be
accurately and fully figured.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.27   OTHER DATA REQUIRED.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner shall, when he deems it necessary, require
that other data, calculations or strain sheets be submitted for any part of the
work. He may require such other drawings, specifications, samples of materials,
information or tests that he deems necessary to show clearly what is proposed
to be done.
   (b)   The Building Commissioner shall require the applicant for a building
permit to produce a numbered receipt from the Water Department of the City of
Cleveland attesting that a water meter permit has been obtained for the
structure for which the building permit is being requested.
(Ord. 38-73. Passed 3-19-73.)
   (c)   The Building Commissioner shall require the applicant for any building
permit, at a location not served by permanent sanitary facilities, to produce a
numbered receipt from the Cuyahoga County Board of Health attesting that a
nonsewered toilet permit has been obtained for the structure for which the
building permit is being requested.
(Ord. 180-90. Passed 6-18-90.)
1501.28   SPECIFICATIONS.
   (a)   Each set of drawings submitted for a permit shall be accompanied by a
set of specifications describing all materials and workmanship, in clear and
specific language.
   (b)   Specifications shall be written in ink, typewritten or printed.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.29   ALTERATION OR ERASURE OF DRAWINGS OR SPECIFICATIONS; DEVIATIONS FROM
PLANS.
   No person shall erase, alter or modify any line, figure, letter, word or
coloring contained upon any drawing or specifications filed with and stamped by
the Building Commissioner and for which a permit has been obtained. If, during
the progress of work, it is desired to deviate in any manner from the terms of
the application, drawings or specifications, notice of such intention to alter
or deviate shall be given in writing to the Building Commissioner and his
written assent shall be obtained before the alteration or deviation may be
made. If the change or deviation affects the carrying or structural parts of
the building or its grade, occupancy or means of egress, revised drawings shall
be submitted to the Commissioner for approval.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.30   EXAMINATION OF PLUMBING PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
   Before issuing a permit for the erection, alteration, enlargement, raising
or moving of any building or structure, where plumbing and drainage work is to
be installed or changed therein, the Building Commissioner shall examine or
cause to be examined the drawings and specifications thereof and he shall not
issue a permit therefor until the proposed plumbing and drainage is found to be
in compliance with Title Seven of this Building Code.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.31   EXAMINATION OF PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR ELECTRICAL WORK.
   Before issuing a permit for the erection, alteration, enlargement, raising
or moving of any building or structure where electrical construction is to be
installed or changed therein, the Building Commissioner shall examine or cause
to be examined the plans and specifications thereof and he shall not issue a
permit therefor until the proposed electrical work is found to be in compliance
with Title Three of this Building Code.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.32   IMPERFECT PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
   If the matter mentioned in any application for a permit or in the drawings
and specifications accompanying and illustrating the same indicate to the
Building Commissioner that the work to be done is not clearly or specifically
defined or is imperfect or is not in all respects in accordance with the
provisions of this Building Code, he shall refuse to issue a permit until the
application, drawings and specifications have been made to conform in every
respect with the requirements thereof. All unfigured plans shall be deemed
incomplete.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.33   STAMPED DRAWINGS.
      (a)   When a permit is issued, one set of drawings and specifications
shall be stamped by the Building Commissioner and shall then be filed in the
Division of Buildings, and one set so stamped shall be returned to the
applicant, which latter set of drawings shall be kept at the building or work
until such building or work is completed.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.34   TAMPERING WITH DRAWINGS AND SPECIFICATIONS; RETENTION PERIOD.
   Drawings and specifications, while in the custody of the Division of
Buildings, shall not be removed from their files except for the purpose of
official inspection and reference, and whoever removes the same from the
Division of Buildings except for the purpose aforesaid shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor and be liable to the penalties provided in this Building Code. It
shall not be obligatory upon the Building Commissioner to retain the drawings
in his custody for more than three months after the completion or occupation of
any building.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1501.35   REVOCATION OF PERMITS.
   (a)   When, in the judgment of the Building Commissioner, the work for which
any building permit was issued is not being performed in conformity with the
application, drawings or specifications upon which the permit was issued, or if
the stamped drawings are not kept at the building or work, it shall be the duty
of the Commissioner to notify the owner or his agent in writing that the work
is being constructed in violation of this Building Code and that the work must
be suspended until a permit for the deviation from the application, drawings or
specifications is obtained or that such work shall be made to conform to the
application, drawings and specifications upon which a permit therefor was
issued. If the owner or his agent fails to comply with the notice on the
service thereof, it shall be the further duty of the Commissioner to revoke the
permit. Written notice of the revocation signed by the Commissioner shall be
immediately mailed to the owner or his agent at the address given in the
application for the permit and a copy of the revocation shall be posted on the
premises. No person shall perform any work in or about the structure or
building or use, let, rent or occupy the structure or building after the
revocation of the permit and the posting of the notice thereof, except to
perform such work as may be required for the correction of existing violations.
   (b)   In cases which, in the judgment of the Commissioner, require immediate
action, the permit may be revoked without serving of the notice referred to
above.
   (c)   When a permit has been revoked on account of poor material or bad
workmanship in masonry construction, the Commissioner may require the owner to
employ a superintendent, acceptable to the Commissioner, who shall be kept on
the work until the masonry work has been finished and who shall be paid by the
owner.
   (d)   When a permit has been revoked, it shall not be reinstated until all
existing violations have been corrected and a superintendent provided, if
required. Written notice of the reinstatement of a permit shall be given to the
owner before the work may proceed.
   (e)   No person shall remove, deface or conceal the notice of revocation,
after the same has been posted, except at the order of the Commissioner.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
   (f)   The remedies provided in this section shall be in addition to the
penalties provided in Section
1501.99.
1501.36   REGISTRATION AND INSPECTION REQUIREMENTS INCLUDING DISCLOSURE OF ALL
CONTRACTORS.
   (a)   (1)   No person, firm or corporation shall engage in the business or
act in the capacity of a contractor as herein defined except pursuant to a
certificate of registration issued in conformity with the provisions of this
chapter by the Building Commissioner, unless such person, firm or corporation
is particularly exempted by the provisions of this chapter. Notwithstanding
Section
1501.99, if construction is commenced without the person, firm or corporation
acting in the capacity of a contractor having first obtained the necessary
certificate or certificates of registration, a penalty equal to, and in
addition to the original registration fee or fees, shall be paid, and all work
shall be stopped until such time as such fee or fees have been paid, and the
certificate of registration issued.
(Ord. 181-90. Passed 6-18-90.)
      (2)   As used in this chapter, “contractor” means any individual, firm,
copartnership, corporation, association or other organization, or any
combination of any thereof, who or which by himself or itself, or by or through
others, constructs, alters, repairs, adds to, subtracts from, reconstructs or
remodels any building or structure or any appurtenance thereto, or who or which
undertakes or offers to undertake, or purports to have the capacity to
undertake, or submits a bid to do so. The term “contractor” includes a
subcontractor and also a specialty contractor whose operations as such are the
performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal
contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.
The term “contractor” includes a supplier of mixed concrete to a building site,
window installers and glass block companies. The term “contractor” shall also
include homeowners, lessees, mortgage field services companies and property
management companies. A mortgage field services company and property management
company provides services to a person (as defined in Section
1703.22 of the Parma Codified Ordinances) who owns real property. Such services
include but are not limited to maintaining, repairing, improving and cleaning
the interior and/or exterior of the person’s real estate and/or dwelling
including landscaping and lawn services as defined in Section
1507.17(a) of the Parma Codified Ordinances. A mortgage field services company
and property management company shall further be subject tot he regulations set
forth in Section
1507.17(c)(2) and (3) requiring a fifty dollar ($50.00) annual license fee and
three thousand dollar ($3,000.00) surety bond, respectively.
(Ord. 169-94. Passed 7-18-94; Ord. 15-19. Passed 2-19-19; Ord. 232-19. Passed
11-18-19.)
   (b)   (1)   In order to register with the City, the contractor must present
a document from the City Tax Department stating “there are no tax arrearages
currently on record with the Tax Department. There may be tax delinquencies,
but at this point in time, none are documented.” The Tax Department shall not
issue this document to the contractor until all documented delinquencies are
paid in full. The Tax Department shall only issue this document to the
contractor and/or the contractor's designee. The Tax Department will not issue
this document directly to the Building Department.
      (2)   The Building Department shall not be required to perform a final
inspection on any project until the contractor completes a form which requests
the names of all subcontractors involved in the project and all amounts paid to
the subcontractors. This form shall be provided to the contractor at the time
he or she receives a building permit. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a mortgage
field services company and property management company shall submit the name(s)
of all subcontractors at the time it registers and, if necessary, updates the
subcontractors list quarterly.
(Ord. 171-07. Passed 8-6-07; Ord. 15-19. Passed 2-19-19; Ord. 232-19. Passed
11-18-19.)
1501.365    SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF REGISTRATION.
   The Building Commissioner may suspend or revoke any certificate of
registration or renewal thereof issued under Section
1501.36 or any other provision of this Building Code for any of the following
reasons:
   (a)   Misrepresentation of a material fact by the applicant in obtaining the
certificate of registration or the renewal thereof;
   (b)   Use of the certificate of registration in obtaining permits for
another;
   (c)   Faulty or defective workmanship;
   (d)   Departure from or disregard of plans and specifications filed with the
application for a permit;
   (e)   Noncompliance with or violation of any of the provisions of this
Building Code; or
   (f)   Misrepresentation of a material fact in a residential concrete drive
plant and contractor's report.
(Ord. 95-86. Passed 2-17-87.)
1501.37   PERMITS TO BE ISSUED ONLY TO REGISTERED CONTRACTORS.
   No permit required by the provisions of this Building Code shall be issued
for work to be undertaken by contract except to a registered contractor.
(Ord. 5-59. Passed 1-19-59.)
1501.38   SURETY BOND.
   (a)   Every applicant for registration shall, as a condition of
registration, furnish and file with the Building Commissioner a surety bond in
the following amounts:
      Suppliers of mixed concrete, as defined in Section 1501.36(b)   $200,000
      All other contractors or subcontractors, as defined in Section 1501.36
(b)   $ 25,000
   The surety bond shall be upon an official form prescribed by the Building
Commissioner. Failure to maintain the surety bond provided for in this section
may result in the suspension or revocation of any certificate of registration
or renewal thereof to do business as a contractor in the City. Continuation
certificates will not be accepted.
   (b)   The bond required by this section shall be to guarantee full and
faithful compliance by the registered contractor with all pertinent provisions
of this Building Code and with pertinent rules and regulations promulgated
under authority of this Building Code and to bind the surety thereon to correct
or abate any violation of the Building Code and all pertinent rules and
regulations promulgated under the authority of the Building Code whenever the
applicant for registration named as the principal on such bond refuses,
neglects or fails to correct or abate such violation within a reasonable time
limit set by the Building Commissioner.
(Ord. 169-94. Passed 7-18-94; Ord. 154-22. Passed 10-17-22.)
1501.39   INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS.
   (a)   No person, firm or corporation shall be permitted to commence
operation of any nature whatsoever as contained in this Building Code, and no
permit shall be issued to such person, firm or corporation, unless, during the
performance of the work authorized by such permit, the public is protected by
an approved policy of insurance commonly termed a commercial general liability
policy with limits as follows:
      (1)   At least three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) per occurrence
limit and three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) general aggregate limit.
      (2)   The City of Parma must be named as an additional insured.
   (b)   Such policy of insurance shall be in a form directed or approved by
the Law Director and shall, in addition to the public protection hereinbefore
specified, protect the City in the amounts specified from all claims for
personal injury, including death, and from all claims of property damage
resulting from the doing of the work for which the permit was issued.
   (c)   Contractor applicant shall not be allowed to cancel the policy without
giving the City advanced notice of such and receiving the City's written
consent. The contractor applicant shall have a continual duty to notify the
City of any changes that affect the contents of this section. Failure to do any
of the above shall be grounds for the City to revoke any and all permits on
this project and allow the City to consider contractor applicant's registration
as void. The City retains any and all rights to any other civil remedies and/or
criminal actions regarding contractor applicant's failure to comply with the
above duties and requirements.
   The surety company shall be obligated to send notice to the City immediately
upon cancellation and/or changes to the policy.
(Ord. 169-94. Passed 7-18-94; Ord. 82-11. Passed 3-21-11.)
   (d)   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Subsection (d) hereof was repealed by Ordinance 336-
96, passed October 21, 1996.)
1501.40   APPLICATION OF OHIO BASIC BUILDING CODE AND STATE LAW; CONFLICT OF
LAWS; ENERGY CONSERVATION. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR’S NOTE: Section 1501.40 was repealed by Ordinance No. 113-17, passed
July 10, 2017.)
1501.41   FEES.
   All building fees shall be as provided in
Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the General Fee Schedule). Copies of
Chapter 185 are available at the Building Commissioner's office.
(Ord. 196-57. Passed 7-29-57.)
1501.42   APPLICATION FOR OCCUPANCY PERMIT.
   In the case of a single-family residence which has been constructed for
sale, where an occupancy permit is required pursuant to Section
1501.10, the buyer of such residence must personally sign the application for
the occupancy permit. In such case, no occupancy permit shall issue except upon
the application of such buyer.
(Ord. 226-72. Passed 11-20-72.)
1501.43   BUILDING CONTRACTS.
   (a)   Any person, firm or corporation licensed to do business in accordance
with Section
1501.36, who or which contracts to perform work which, in whole or in part, is
governed by this Building Code, shall:
      (1)   Disclose in writing and in advance to the contractee, by general
description, those sections of this Building Code applicable to the
contemplated work;
      (2)   Include within the agreed contract price for completion of the work
all costs reasonably anticipated as being necessary to satisfy all applicable
sections of this Building Code, except where the contractee has expressly and
in writing agreed otherwise; and
      (3)   Include within such contract, in a clear and conspicuous manner,
the following disclosure, which shall appear on a page of the contract that is
signed by the contractee:
   "NOTICE
   PURSUANT TO SECTION 1501.43 OF THE CODIFIED ORDINANCES OF THE CITY OF PARMA,
A CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO INFORM YOU OF THE SECTIONS OF THE PARMA BUILDING
CODE WHICH APPLY TO THIS CONTRACT AND IS REQUIRED TO INCLUDE THE COST OF
SATISFYING THOSE REQUIREMENTS IN THE AGREED CONTRACT PRICE UNLESS YOU EXPRESSLY
WAIVE THAT RIGHT."
   (b)   From and after January 1, 1988, each contractor's bond filed as
required by Section
1501.38 of these Codified Ordinances shall, in addition to the requirements set
forth therein, be conditioned on compliance with this section, and shall
provide that in the event a contractor fails to comply with Section
1501.43(a)(2), the contractee may make a claim against the bond for all actual
expenses incurred beyond the agreed contract price to bring the work into
compliance with the City Building Code. The contractee's right to file a claim
against the bond shall survive notwithstanding the issuance of any inspection,
approval or occupancy permit by the Building Commissioner.
   (c)   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this section is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree and shall be fined not more than one thousand
dollars ($1,000) or imprisoned not more than six months, or both.
   (d)   Whenever it comes to the attention of the Building Commissioner that
work is underway in violation of any of the provisions of this section, the
Building Commissioner may, after providing the contractor with notice and
reasonable opportunity to respond, suspend any permit related to such work
until the contractor has complied with this section.
(Ord. 150-87. Passed 9-18-88.)
1501.44   ASBESTOS ABATEMENT.
   At least ten days prior to any asbestos abatement project of any school
district, governmental building or other public or private building or
residence, the contractor must submit to the Building Commissioner the name of
an unaffiliated/independent asbestos hazard evaluation specialist. The
specialist is subject to the approval of the Building Commissioner, and no work
may begin until such approval is given. An asbestos hazard evaluation
specialist shall be as defined in Ohio R.C. 3710.01(F) and must possess a
certificate as defined in Ohio R.C. 3710.01(J)(1). The specialist must present
a bond in favor of the City in an amount equal to the cost of the project and
must be insured pursuant to the provisions of Section
1501.39. The specialist will be paid for by the contractor and must directly
supervise all asbestos removal. This specialist also will assure the City, in
writing, of the contractor's adherence to all State and Federal Environmental
Protection Agency regulations, including, but not limited to, admissible air
quality preservation and proper disposal of all asbestos. The letter of
adherence shall be filed by the specialist with the City within ten days after
completion of the work.
(Ord. 201-91. Passed 9-3-91.)
1501.99   GENERAL CODE PENALTY.
   (a)   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree. A separate offense shall be deemed committed
each day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.
   (b)   In addition to the penalty provided in subsection (a) hereof, any
contractor who violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
Building Code may have his certificate of registration revoked for a period not
exceeding one year.
(Ord. 282-94. Passed 11-21-94; Ord. 238-08. Passed 10-6-08.)

1503.01   MEMBERSHIP; TERM; COMPENSATION; MEETINGS.
   The Board of Building Appeals shall consist of five resident members of the
City appointed by the Mayor with the approval of Council. Members shall be
appointed to a five-year term, except when appointed to fill an unexpired term.
A member may be removed for cause by the Mayor with the approval of Council.
Members shall receive compensation at the rate of thirty dollars ($30.00) each
per meeting. Meetings of the Board shall be held at the City Hall upon the call
of the Mayor or the Chairperson of the Board. 
(Ord. 10-89. Passed 2-6-89; Ord. 390-96. Passed 2-3-97.)
1503.02   APPEALS TO THE BOARD GENERALLY.
   (a)   A determination of the Building Commissioner made in the enforcement
of this Building Code or other related ordinances, including, without
limitation,
Chapter 1713 of the Parma Codified Ordinances, may be appealed to the Board of
Building Appeals by a person deeming himself adversely affected by such
decision. A notice of appeal must be in writing and must be filed with the
Board within thirty days of the personal delivery or mailing, whichever is
applicable, of the order or notice being appealed. Failure to file a written
appeal with the Board within the time prescribed shall constitute a waiver of
the right of appeal. Filing of a notice of appeal does not operate to suspend
the order or notice being appealed and shall not prevent the Building
Commissioner from acting in accordance with his decision.
(Ord. 74-79. Passed 5-7-79; Ord. 188-22. Passed 1-17-23.)
   (b)   The applicant shall pay a fee to the Building Commissioner as
designated in Section
185.04(e) of the Administrative Code. The Board shall not proceed with a
hearing until the fee is paid.
(Ord. 283-88. Passed 10-3-88.)
1503.03   HEARINGS BEFORE THE BOARD.
   The Board of Building Appeals shall give reasonable notice to the parties to
the appeal and the property owners or their agents that are abutting or within
a 200-foot radius of the boundaries of the property subject to appeal. The
Board shall hold a hearing on the matter as soon as reasonably possible
following filing of the notice of appeal. The presence of three members of the
Board shall constitute a quorum and the concurring vote of three members of the
Board shall be necessary to reverse or modify any order, requirement, decision
or determination of the Building Commissioner or to decide in favor of the
appellant any matter upon which the Board is required to pass.
(Ord. 74-79. Passed 5-7-79; Ord. 147-17. Passed 9-18-17.)
1503.035   VARIANCE APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS.
   (a)   Applications for variance shall contain at least the following
information:
      (1)   The name, address, telephone number, and email address of the
applicant and/or agent;
      (2)   A statement of the reason(s) for requesting a variance;
      (3)   Any other information the Building Commissioner may require.
   (b)   The applicant shall pay a fee to the Director of Public Safety as set
forth in Chapter 185 of the Administrative Code (the general fee schedule).
   (c)   The applicant shall pay postage for the required notifications.
   (d)   The Building Commissioner shall then certify for hearing before the
Board on the application for the variance request.
(Ord. 32-18. Passed 4-2-18.)
1503.04   JURISDICTION OF THE BOARD.
   Should the Board of Building Appeals determine that the decision of the
Building Commissioner was unauthorized or that, by reason of special
conditions, undue hardship would result from a literal application of this
Building Code, while a variance in the specific case would be consistent with
the spirit and intent of such Code, then, in either case, the Board shall, in
writing, reverse or modify the Commissioner's decision and order the
Commissioner to take such action as is appropriate and consistent with this
Building Code.
(Ord. 74-79. Passed 5-7-79.)
CHAPTER 1504
Project Labor Agreements and Responsible Contracting Practices
1504.01   Public purpose.
1504.02   Evaluation of project labor agreements required.
1504.03   Rejection of project labor agreement; Council action required.
1504.04   Responsible contracting standards and procedures established.
1504.05   Non-applicability.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Registration of building contractors - see BLDG.
1501.36 et seq.
   Registration of air pollution control contractors - see BLDG.
1530.13
   Registration of electrical contractors - see BLDG.
1531.08 et seq.
   Registration of heating and ventilating contractors - see BLDG.
1541.08 et seq.
1504.01   PUBLIC PURPOSE.
   The City finds that evaluating the feasibility of project labor agreements
for City building and other public improvement projects and articulating
standards and establishing reporting requirements to evaluate the
responsibility of public contractors further the following public purposes:
   (a)   Promotion of better quality workmanship on City building and other
public improvement projects, which in turn saves tax dollars and protects the
public health, safety and morals; and
   (b)   Promotion of labor peace during periods of time when public buildings
or other public improvements are under construction, which likewise confers a
significant benefit to the public's health, safety and morals.
(Ord. 181-00. Passed 7-24-00.)
1504.02   EVALUATION OF PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENTS REQUIRED.
   (a)   The Mayor, or his designee, with the assistance of the Law Department,
shall meet with the Cleveland Building and Construction Trades Council, or
other appropriate trade union, in connection with the public bidding and
contract awarding process for every proposed City building and other City
improvement project in which the engineering estimate for the project exceeds
two hundred thousand dollars ($200,000) to evaluate whether a project labor
agreement will advance the City's procurement interest in cost, efficiency and
quality and in promoting labor-management stability as well as compliance with
applicable legal requirements governing safety and health, equal employment
opportunity, labor and employment standards and other matters.
   (b)   If the Mayor, or his designee, determines that use of a project labor
agreement will serve the goals set forth in subsection (a) hereof, the Mayor,
or his designee, shall negotiate a project labor agreement with the Cleveland
Building and Construction Trades Council or other appropriate trade unions.
   (c)   The bidding documents for each such City building or other improvement
project shall contain a written provision requiring the successful bidder to
comply with and adhere to all of the provisions of any projec4 labor agreement
negotiated by the Mayor for the project.
   (d)   The City shall not thereafter enter into any contract with the
successful bidder for the construction of any such City building or other
improvement unless the contract contains a provision requiring the successful
bidder and all of his contractors and subcontractors to comply with and adhere
to the provisions of the negotiated project labor agreement.
(Ord. 181-00. Passed 7-24-00.)
1504.03   REJECTION OF PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENT; COUNCIL ACTION REQUIRED.
   If the Mayor, with respect to any proposed City building or other
improvement project with an engineer estimate in excess of two hundred thousand
dollars ($200,000), determines that a project labor agreement will not serve
the goals set forth in Section
1504.02(a), the Mayor shall submit a written report and recommendation to the
Clerk of Council, which thereafter shall be acted upon by Council as
hereinafter provided, prior to the preparation of bid documents for the said
project. The report of the Mayor shall state the Mayor's reasons for believing
that negotiating a project labor agreement for the said project will not
substantially further the p5rposes of this chapter, and shall contain his
recommendation to Council to not negotiate a project labor agreement. The
report shall be presented to the members of Council at Council's next regular
or special meeting which occurs at least five days after the Clerk of Council's
receipt of the Mayor's report and recommendation. At that meeting of Council,
or at Council's next regular or special meeting, Council shall, by motion,
determine whether the Mayor's recommendation to not negotiate a project labor
agreement should be adopted. If a majority of the members of Council vote
against the motion to adopt, then the Mayor, or his designee, with the
assistance of the Law Department, shall be required to forthwith negotiate a
project labor agreement for the said project. Thereafter, all of the
requirements of Section
1504.02 shall apply with respect to the said project.
(Ord. 181-00. Passed 7-24-00.)
1504.04   RESPONSIBLE CONTRACTING STANDARDS AND PROCEDURES ESTABLISHED.
   (a)   The Mayor, or his designee, in connection with the public bidding and
contract awarding process for every proposed City building and other City
improvement project, shall, prior to the awarding of contracts, establish
criteria for evaluating the responsibility of the apparent lowest bidder and
require that the apparent lowest responsible bidder provide information
necessary to ascertain the pecuniary and financial responsibility,
accountability, reliability, skill, capacity, judgment, integrity and moral
worth to do business in our community. In the event the apparent lowest bidder
fails to furnish the requested information and/or the information provided
demonstrates a lack of responsibility, the apparent lowest bidder shall be
rejected and thereby is disqualified and the next lowest bidder shall become
the apparent lowest responsible bidder.
   (b)   The Mayor shall require a bidder to furnish the following items:
      (1)   Description of its experience with projects of comparative size,
complexity and cost within recent years, demonstrating the contractor's ability
and capacity to perform a substantial portion of the project with its own
forces;
      (2)   Documentation from previous projects regarding timeliness of
performance, quality of work, extension requests, fines and penalties imposed
and payment thereof, li%ns filed, history of claims for extra work, contract
defaults, together with explanations of same;
      (3)   Identification and description of any projects within the previous
five years in which the apparent lowest bidder was determined by a public
entity not to be a responsible bidder, the reasons given by the public entity,
together with an explanation thereof;
      (4)   An adequate demonstration of financial responsibility, which may
include, in the Mayor's discretion, a certified financial statement prepared by
a certified public accountant, to assure that the apparent lowest bidder
possesses adequate resources and availability of credit and the means and
ability to procure insurance and bonds required for the project;
       (5)   Disclosure of any suspension or revocation of any professional
license of any director, officer, owner or managerial employee of the apparent
lowest bidder, to the extent that any work to be performed is within the field
of such licensed profession;
      (6)   Disclosure of any and all OSHA violations within the previous three
years, as well as all notices of OSHA citations filed against the apparent
lowest bidder in the same three-year period, together with a description and
explanation of remediation or other steps taken regarding such violations and
notices of violation;
      (7)   Disclosure of any and all violations within the previous five years
pertaining to unlawful intimidation or discrimination against any employee by
reason of race, creed, color, disability, sex or national origin and/or
violations of an employee's civil or labor rights or equal employment
opportunities;
      (8)   Disclosure of any litigation (including copies of pleadings) in
which the apparent lowest bidder has been named as a defendant or third party
defendant in an action involving a claim for personal injury or wrongful death
arising from performance of work related to any project in which it has been
engaged within the previous five years;
      (9)   Disclosure of allegations of violations of the prevailing wage law
and any other State or Federal labor law, including, but not limited to, child
labor violations, failure to pay wages, or unemployment insurance tax
delinquencies or unfair labor practices within the past five years;
      (10)   Disclosure of violations of the workers compensation law;
      (11)   Disclosure of any criminal convictions or criminal indictments,
involving the apparent lowest bidder, its officers, directors, owners and/or
managerial employees, within the past five years;
      (12)   Disclosure of any violations within the past five years of pending
charges concerning Federal, State or municipal environmental and/or health
laws, codes, rules and/or regulations;
      (13)   Documentation of the contractor's participation and contributions
to a bona fide apprenticeship program;
      (14)   Documentation that the contractor provides health insurance and
pension benefits to its employees;
      (15)   Identification of whether the contractor's workforce is drawn
mainly from area residents;
      (16)   Identification of all work to be subcontracted. All subcontractors
are also subject to the approval of the Mayor based on the above
considerations.
   (c)   In the event the amount of the lowest bid appears disproportionately
low when compared to estimates undertaken by or on behalf of the City and/or
compared to other bids submitted, the Mayor reserves the right to inquire
further of the apparent lowest bidder to determine whether the bid contains
mathematical errors, omissions and/or erroneous assumptions, and whether the
apparent lowest bidder has the capability to perform and complete the contract
for the bid amount.
   (d)   Prior to a final determination that the apparent lowest bidder is not
responsible, the City shall notify the party of same, in writing, stating the
reasons causing concern and setting forth a time, date and place for the
apparent lowest bidder to appear and be heard by the Mayor or his designee,
prior to a determination being made regarding its responsibility.
(Ord. 181-00. Passed 7-24-00.)
   (e)   In determining whether a contractor is a responsible contractor under
this section, the Mayor and/or his or her designee shall evaluate the
information required to be furnished by bidders. The Mayor or his or her
designee reserves the right to request additional information of a bidder. Any
contractor who fails to satisfy three or more of the criteria listed in
divisions (e)(1) through (e)(23) of this section shall be presumed to not be a
responsible contractor.
      (1)   The contractor and/or its owners must have been in the construction
business for at least five years.
      (2)   The contractor must not have been disqualified from any public
project by virtue of having been found to be not responsible.
      (3)   The contractor must not have had a performance bond canceled or had
a claim made on a performance bond.
      (4)   The contractor must not have been fined or had penalties imposed as
a result of untimeliness in completing a project.
      (5)   The contractor must not have been found in default or failed to
complete any project in accordance with contract requirements.
      (6)   The contractor must not have been found to have committed any
unfair labor practice or any other labor law violation (e.g., FLSA, FMLA).
      (7)   The contractor must not have been found to have violated any
employment discrimination law.
      (8)   The contractor must not have been found to have violated the
Workers' Compensation Law.
      (9)   The contractor must not have been found to have violated either
State or Federal prevailing wage laws.
      (10)   The contractor must not have been found to have committed more
than one willful or repeated OSHA violation in the last three years.
      (11)   The contractor must not have a penalty rating from the Bureau of
Workers' Compensation.
      (12)   The contract must not have failed to file any required tax returns
or failed to pay any required taxes to any governmental entity.
      (13)   Neither the contractor, high level management personnel nor any
owners may have had any professional licenses, permits or certifications
suspended or revoked.
      (14)   Neither the contractor, high level management personnel nor any
owners may have been convicted of a criminal offense in connection with
obtaining, attempting to obtain, and/or performing any public or private
contract.
      (15)   Neither the contractor, high level management personnel nor any
owners may have been convicted of embezzlement, theft, forgery, bribery,
falsification or destruction of records, making false statements, tax evasion
or receiving stolen property.
      (16)   Neither the contract nor its owners may have filed for bankruptcy.
      (17)   The contractor must have obligated itself to make ongoing and
regular contributions to an apprenticeship program registered with the Bureau
of Apprenticeship Training of the United States Department of Labor.
      (18)   The contractor must have obligated itself to provide health
insurance benefits to its employees.
      (19)   The contractor must have obligated itself to provide retirement
benefits to its employees.
      (20)   The contractor must have a substance abuse program that includes
testing and treatment.
      (21)   The contractor must have a written safety and health program that
includes training, inspections and a complaint procedure.
      (22)   The contractor must have at least five satisfactory references
from the most recently completed projects of similar size and scope.
      (23)   The contractor must currently employ or have a reliable source for
hiring sufficient qualified skilled, safety-trained workers to perform the
project.
(Ord. 178-02. Passed 6-3-02; Ord. 260-02. Passed 3-1-04.)
1504.05   NON-APPLICABILITY.
   If Ohio R.C. 4116.01 through 4116.04, or substantially equivalent State law
provisions, are found to be lawful by a court of competent jurisdiction,
Sections
1504.02 and
1504.03 shall not apply to any public improvement project which includes State
funds appropriated for the purposes of that public improvement.
(Ord. 181-00. Passed 7-24-00.)
CHAPTER 1505
Definitions

1505.01   APPLICATION OF DEFINITIONS.
   In the application of this Building Code to buildings, structures and parts
thereof, the following terms shall have the meaning given herein.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.02   ALTERATION.
   "Alteration" means any addition to a building or change in the construction
or occupancy thereof, when not a repair.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.03   ATTIC STORY.
   "Attic story" means one situated wholly or partly in the roof of the
building.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.04   BASEMENT.
   "Basement" means a story partly underground, not less than seven feet high
in the clear, but having at least one-half of its height above the highest
level of the adjoining ground.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.05   BUILDING CODE.
   "Building Code" means Part Fifteen of these Codified Ordinances, consisting
of Titles One through Seven.
1505.06   BUILDING REGULATIONS.
   "Building Regulations" means Title One of Part Fifteen of these Codified
Ordinances.
1505.07   BUILDINGS.
   (a)   "Building" means any structure erected and fixed upon or in the soil
and designed for use in the position in which it is located; the word
"structure" is included.
   (b)   "Existing building or structure" means one which is completed, or
plans for which have been filed prior to the effective date of this section
(Ordinance 1177, passed March 3, 1930).
   (c)   "Frame building" means one having an external wall constructed wholly
or partly of wood, regardless of whether or not such wood is covered with
metal.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.08   BUILDING LINE.
   "Building line" means the line formed by the intersection of the outer face
of the enclosing wall or walls of a building and the surface of the ground.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.09   CELLAR.
   "Cellar" means a story having more than one-half of its height below the
highest level of the adjoining ground.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.10   COURT.
   "Court" means an open space bounded on one or more sides by the walls of a
building, the bottom of which is either above or below the level of the lot of
such building, and which is clear, open and unobstructed from the bottom
thereof to the sky.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.11   GRADE.
   "Grade" means the elevation of the street curb lines, as fixed by the City
Engineer. Where the grade has not been so fixed, the natural surface of the
ground shall be taken as the grade.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.12   HEIGHT OF A BUILDING.
   (a)   "Height of a building" means the distance as measured on the center
line of the principal front of the building from the grade to the highest point
in the coping of flat roofs, to the deck line of a mansard roof, to the center
height of the highest gable in a pitched roof or to half the height of a hip
roof.
   (b)   If the grade in the rear or along the side of the building falls below
the grade of the front, the height shall then be taken in the center of the
side or end, showing the greatest fall.
   (c)   If the total fall on any side or end exceeds ten feet in the length
thereof, the height shall then be measured at the lowermost corner, and the
height of the building shall be terraced or stepped off at every ten feet of
grade.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.13   HEIGHT OF A STORY.
   "Height of a story" means the perpendicular distances from top to top of two
successive floors. The clear height of a story means the distance from the
floor to the ceiling thereof. The height of a topmost story shall be measured
from the level of its floor to the upper side of the ceiling joists or collar
beams forming a tie to the roof, or up to one-half the vertical height of the
rafters, when the roof has no such tie.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.14   INCOMBUSTIBLE MATERIAL.
   "Incombustible material" means any material which will not burn or support
combustion at any temperature under 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.15   LOTS.
   (a)   "Lot" means any tract of land under one ownership within the City and
having a street frontage.
   (b)   "Open lot" means a lot bounded on all sides by street lines.
   (c)   "Corner lot" means a lot bounded on two or more sides by intersecting
streets and which is adjacent to the point of intersection. Any portion of the
width of such lot line and measured at right angles therewith shall not be
regarded as a part of a corner lot but shall be deemed an interior lot.
   (d)   "Through lot" means a lot running through from one street to another
or opposite street. A through lot shall be treated as two interior lots.
   (e)   "Interior lot" means a lot other than a corner lot or through lot.
   (f)   "Front of a lot" means that boundary line which borders on the street.
In the case of a corner lot, the owner shall designate, by a statement on his
drawings and application, one street boundary line as the front which will
thereafter be deemed the front of the lot.
   (g)   "Rear of a lot" means the side opposite to the front. In the case of a
triangle shaped corner lot, the rear shall be the boundary line not bordering
on the street.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.16   LOT LINE.
   "Lot line" means the line of demarcation between the property of different
owners.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.17   LENGTH AND WIDTH OF A BUILDING.
   (a)   "Length of a building" means its greatest lineal dimension.
   (b)   The "width of a building" shall be measured at right angles to its
length and shall be the greatest dimension in that direction.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.18   LOADS ON BUILDINGS.
   (a)   "Dead load" means the actual weight of walls, floors, partitions and
all permanent construction.
   (b)   "Live load" means all imposed fixed or transient loads, other than
dead, due to the occupancy of the building, including wind pressure.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.19   PARTITIONS.
   (a)   "Partition" means an interior subdividing wall. The name of the
structural material used is usually prefixed.
   (b)   "Bearing partition" means one carrying superimposed loads and its own
weight.
   (c)   "Nonbearing partition" means one carrying only its own weight.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.20   REPAIRS.
   "Repairs" means the reconstruction or renewal of any part of an existing
building, for the purpose of maintaining it in its present condition or
occupancy, by the use of the same kind of materials as were originally used in
the construction of the replaced parts.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.21   SHALL.
   "Shall" is always mandatory and not directory.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.22   STREET.
   "Street" means a public right-of-way, including those portions used for
vehicular and pedestrian traffic and the tree lawn area, by whatever name
known, which has been platted, submitted to and approved by the proper
authorities of the City.
1505.23   STREET LINE.
   "Street line" means that line which separates a street from other
properties, public or private.
1505.24   VENEER.
   "Veneer" means the outer facing of an enclosing wall used for the protection
of the backing or as embellishment, but not counted as adding anything to the
strength of the wall.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.25   YARDS.
   "Yard" means an open unoccupied space, clear and unobstructed from the
ground level to the sky. Yards are classified as follows:
   (a)   "Front yard" means a yard immediately in the front of a building.
   (b)   "Rear yard" means a yard immediately in the rear of a building and
extending across the entire width of the lot.
   (c)   "Side yard" means a yard immediately at the side of a building and
extending straight and direct from the front yard or the street to the rear
yard.
   (d)   "Enclosed yard" means a yard surrounded on all sides by the walls of a
building or buildings.
   (e)   "Offset yard" means any yard other than a front, rear, side or
enclosed yard.
(Ord. 1177. Passed 3-3-30.)
1505.26   OUTSIDE ENTRANCEWAY OR DOOR.
   "Outside entranceway or door" means one which leads into a dwelling house
from any outside area, including an attached garage, enclosed patio, sun porch
or breezeway.
(Ord. 30-78. Passed 3-6-78.)
1505.27   FROST WALL.
   "Frost wall" means a barrier placed across a door opening to prevent frost
from developing in or undermining a floor.
(Ord. 90-78. Passed 5-15-78.)
1505.28   STORY.
   "Story" means that portion of a building included between the upper surface
of a floor and the upper surface of the floor or roof next above.
(Ord. 19-80. Passed 3-3-80.)
1505.29   FIRST STORY.
   "First story" means that story which has a floor elevation of not more than
five feet six inches above the average finished grade of the ground adjoining
the building, but not more than three feet six inches below such grade.
(Ord. 19-80. Passed 3-3-80.)
